POSITION OVERVIEW
At BDC, the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, your work contributes directly to the success of small and medium-sized businesses across Canada. As a KYC Analyst, you will provide administrative and analytical support to the Financing team by managing the Know Your Client (KYC) process for loan applications. You will review client files, gather and analyze KYC documentation, identify potential compliance concerns, and work closely with the Business Development Lead (BDL) and Underwriter to ensure complete and accurate submissions. At BDC, we value inclusion, equity, and diversity, and you can be yourself at work.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead the KYC process from end to end, ensuring the timely collection, review, analysis, and validation of required KYC documentation.
Review customer files to understand the overall financing request and identify missing information or documentation.
Analyze KYC information and documentation to identify potential non-compliance issues, risks, or concerns.
Escalate KYC-related findings and concerns to the Business Development Lead (BDL) as required.
Follow up directly with clients to obtain required information and documentation.
Manage multiple KYC files simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.
Collaborate closely with the Business Development Lead, Underwriter, and internal partners to ensure all KYC requirements are met.
Submit complete and error-free KYC documentation in accordance with established policies, procedures, and standards.
Provide timely, accurate, and professional service to existing and prospective clients.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with clients and internal stakeholders.
Stay up to date on changes to KYC policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and industry trends that may impact BDC.
Support BDC's commitment to delivering a high-quality experience to Canadian entrepreneurs.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration or a related field.
Ability to analyze and interpret financial statements.
Strong business acumen.
Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional attention to detail.
Client service orientation with the ability to listen, identify issues, and support resolution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously.
Ability to work independently and meet tight deadlines.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including:
Microsoft Word
Microsoft Excel
Microsoft Outlook
Ability to review, analyze, and validate KYC documentation and information.
Availability to work on-site a minimum of three (3) days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting KYC (Know Your Client), compliance, anti-money laundering (AML), customer due diligence (CDD), or lending-related processes.
Experience working in a financial services, banking, lending, or commercial financing environment.
Demonstrated teamwork and collaboration skills.
Flexibility and adaptability in a fast-paced environment.
Creative problem-solving skills.
Bilingualism in English and French

one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers

As a Senior Business Advisor, Strategy within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a senior strategic advisor to entrepreneurs and executive teams at pivotal moments of growth, transformation, and ownership transition. Enable strong internal collaboration by connecting advisors, delivery teams, and relationship managers, ensuring continuity of client strategy and effective knowledge transfer across engagements.
Represent BDC Advisory Services externally through thought leadership, content development, speaking engagements, and participation in targeted events that promote Business and Organizational Capabilities solutions. At BDC, we think and act differently, and we value inclusion, equity, and authenticity—you can be yourself at work while making a tangible impact on Canadian businesses.

POSITION OVERVIEW
The BDC Seed Venture Fund is an early-stage venture capital fund that seeks to invest in the next generation of built-in-Canada global leaders. The fund works with companies across all seed-stages, from as early as inception, and collaborates deeply with early-stage ecosystem stakeholders including accelerators, incubators, and angel groups.  Thematic areas of interest include sectors that are poised to be transformed in the coming decade including industrials/agriculture, climate/sustainability, defense, and computing, although we like to invest at the edges and therefore remain open to investing across all emerging trends and technologies.  Post-investment the team works closely with portfolio companies and leverages its experience and networks to assist across company operations including go-to-market, hiring, fundraising, and helping portfolio companies become Series A ready.
Who you are
You are someone who wants to be a great partner to founders, someone who will be both a thought-partner and will get their hands dirty to help founders solve their most pressing problems. You are an independent thinker and can build conviction in the midst of incomplete information. You thrive connecting with others, you are collaborative, and like to teach and learn from peers. You’re hungry and motivated to drive impact for your team and the founders you work with.
Your primary responsibility will be helping to manage the daily operations of the fund, including:
Identifying new and interesting entrepreneurs and companies that align with our areas of interest
Performing market research and due diligence for potential investments
Reporting on our portfolio companies, including preparing semi-annual updates
Working with existing portfolio companies, including helping with go-to-market, product, hiring, financial modeling, and research
Executing projects of your own creation that will help build our platform, improve our operations, or support our portfolio companies
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Our future teammate is someone who demonstrates:
Native understanding of the startup ecosystem and awareness of emerging technology trends
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good fundamental business instincts – you see the full picture of a business and how all the functions work together
Strong interpersonal skills – you’ll often be talking to entrepreneurs and other investors
Data-driven thinking and good Excel modeling skills
Ideally, prior design or engineering experience (either software or hardware) or work in an investment-related position
Technical skills in either category or ideally a mix of both: software/hardware/AI/ML or product/sales/operations/GTM
What we’d like to know:
Why do you want to be in VC, why seed-stage, why now?
What areas are of interest to you when it comes to investing and why?
What is an example of a time you went above and beyond, or saw around a corner, for a customer? (A customer could be in the true sense of the word, or an internal stakeholder who was relying on your work)
What is an example of an initiative you took or side project you’ve worked on outside of work or school?
Typical Professional Background
5 years of experience in a role involving critical thinking, product/engineering, financial analysis, and/or other technical expertise.
Bachelor’s degree in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, commerce, or economics.   Philosophy and psychology also viable with demonstrated technical aptitude.
A post-graduate degree or equivalent certification is valuable, including but not limited to: Master’s in business administration (MBA), other STEM Master’s or PhD degree, Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA).

title: Managing Director, Credit Restructuring
description:
Purpose. Performance. People.
Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
Credit Investments (CI) is seeking an experienced restructuring professional to strengthen its capability to manage underperforming, stressed and distressed credit investments as the portfolio grows in scale and complexity.
The Managing Director, Restructuring will provide dedicated senior creditor-side expertise across workouts, liability management exercises (LMEs), restructurings, liquidity solutions and other stressed situations. The role will partner with CI investment teams to preserve investment value, maximize recoveries and support effective positioning ahead of key events.
The Team
Credit Investments currently manages assets in excess of $80.5 billion; investment deal sizes range from $50M to over $1B. The Credit Investments team has over 147 investment professionals across North America, Europe and Asia.
Reporting to the Head of Credit Strategy, the role will work closely with CI investment teams, Legal, Portfolio Management and senior leadership, and will contribute to broader CPP Investments matters where restructuring expertise can add value. The role is expected to be based in Toronto or New York.
Accountabilities
Lead Restructuring Strategy and Execution
Serve as CI's senior restructuring expert and provide commercial leadership and decision-making authority on material stressed and distressed investments.
Partner with investment teams to develop and execute restructuring strategies designed to protect investment value and maximize recoveries. The restructuring lead and relevant deal team will be co-accountable, with the deal team retaining ownership of the ultimate investment outcome.
Lead negotiations involving amendments, waivers, recapitalizations, exchange offers, LMEs, rescue financings, asset sales, refinancings and formal restructuring processes.
Assess alternative restructuring pathways and advise on likely outcomes, negotiating leverage, new-money requirements, timing and execution risk, drawing on relevant market precedents and judgment on key economic terms.
Support investment teams in anticipating potential creditor actions and positioning CI effectively ahead of key events.
Provide Senior Commercial Judgment
Provide independent challenge and advice on capital structure, liquidity, valuation, recovery scenarios, financing alternatives and strategic options in distressed situations.
Help teams identify and use sources of negotiating leverage, including opportunities to build alignment with other stakeholders, while engaging constructively and credibly with borrowers, sponsors, shareholders and other creditors.
Advise on creditor-group formation, steering committees and lender-coordination processes, and support the selection and efficient direction of external restructuring bankers, financial advisers and other specialists.
Bring current restructuring market intelligence, conventions and precedents to portfolio-management decisions.
Assess proposed outcomes across recovery value, incremental capital, time to resolution, external costs, reputational considerations and demands on deal-team capacity. Success will be measured primarily through avoided losses and recoveries achieved rather than direct AUM attribution.
Partner with Deal Teams and Legal
Work alongside existing deal teams as athe lead restructuring specialist adviser rather than operating as a separate distressed-investing team; deal teams remain actively involved and accountable for the investment outcome.
Work closely with CI Legal, including dedicated restructuring legal resources, to integrate commercial, negotiating and legal strategy. Legal will advise on documentation, contractual rights and available legal pathways, while this role will lead the commercial strategy and value-maximizing trade-offs informed by that advice.
Partner with Portfolio Management and senior CI leadership to identify situations requiring early intervention and build strong working relationships across CI and, where appropriate, other CPP Investments departments.
Strengthen CI's Restructuring Platform
Play a leadership role in CI's restructuring panel, including triaging situations, challenging strategies and mobilizing resources.
Establish regular watchlist triage to identify situations where specialist involvement can add value before a formal default or restructuring.
Develop restructuring playbooks, precedent libraries, market intelligence and other institutional resources; lead post-mortems and transfer lessons across CI investment teams.
Coach and develop investment professionals to increase restructuring knowledge and judgment and help build a scalable capability for a substantially larger CI portfolio. The role will have no direct people-leadership responsibilities initially, although this may change as the portfolio and workout activity grow.
Broader Contribution
During periods of lower restructuring activity, contribute to broader CI strategic and portfolio initiatives where restructuring, capital-structure, valuation, transaction or market expertise can add value.
Where appropriate, provide restructuring expertise to other parts of CPP Investments and represent CPP Investments credibly with borrowers, sponsors, banks, advisers and institutional creditors in complex and sensitive situations.
What You Bring
Significant restructuring experience gained as a banker or adviser at a leading restructuring advisory firm, or investment bank.
Senior-level experience (approximately 15 years) consistent with a Managing Director appointment, with a demonstrated ability to lead complex restructuring processes and advise sophisticated institutional clients.
Deep creditor-side experience representing lenders, bondholders, creditor groups and/or institutional investors.
Extensive experience with LMEs, complex out-of-court restructurings and formal restructuring processes.
Strong expertise in liquidity analysis, capital structures, valuation, recovery analysis, financing alternatives and transaction execution.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with sponsors, companies, creditor groups and advisers in high-stakes situations.
Strong knowledge of restructuring market conventions, precedents and creditor dynamics.
Meaningful familiarity with restructuring documentation and legal concepts, and the ability to work effectively with counsel.
Strong executive presence and judgment, with the ability to influence senior investment professionals while operating in a collaborative, advisory capacity.
Ability to move between detailed transaction execution and broader strategic judgment, with a collaborative mindset suited to CI's deal-team ownership model.

In this role, you’ll sit right where editorial meets audience growth, collaborating with content teams across CBC News, Entertainment and Sports to make CBC a top destination for financial journalism and related content.

Own the digital publishing strategy for cross division financial reporting,  working in close association with the CBC News publishing team, including aggregation, packaging, lineup management and other direct publishing functions.

Play a key role in planning and live event plans for major financial and money-related journalism. As required, verify user-generated content to ensure accuracy.

Aggregate, showcase and promote financial, business and consumer content from CBC News, CBC Entertainment and CBC Sports.
Use data and analytics to shape our headlines, thumbnails, and rollout plans.

Ensure that CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve.

At least seven (7) years of recent experience in a large digital news environment,
Substantial experience writing, editing, packaging and copy editing digital content in a compelling way.

The Opportunity
Are you passionate about technology transformation, evolving operating models and shaping new ways of working from concept through to adoption? In this key role, you will serve as a strategic technology transformation adviser to leaders and teams, helping diagnose challenges, define and structure change initiatives, and drive operational implementation and adoption across the organization.
Reporting to the Director of the Operational Excellence Office within Technology & Infrastructure (T&I), you will join the team leading the Daily Content initiative in Innovation & Delivery. You will be joining us at a pivotal moment as CBC/Radio-Canada undergoes a major overhaul to modernize its content creation platforms. This transformation goes beyond software and tools — it redefines how production platforms are designed, delivered and used within an organizational model focused on product management, agile at scale, and continuous value creation.
In this role, you will combine a strategic consulting mindset with hands-on execution across all stages of the transformation. You will analyze complex issues, challenge established ways of working and provide actionable recommendations while actively driving their implementation by designing and producing the strategies, plans, frameworks, tools and other deliverables needed to execute and adopt the transformation.
Key areas of focus include transitioning to a product management model, modernizing collaboration with partners and contributors, and driving user adoption of new production tools. You will help define, structure and roll out the transformation and change management strategies required across all levels of the organization.
You will also play a central role in bringing together and aligning diverse teams and stakeholders across CBC/Radio-Canada around a shared vision and common goals. Your ability to grasp and navigate a complex organizational ecosystem, balance operational constraints and competing priorities, and exert influence without direct authority will be essential to align perspectives, build consensus, streamline decision-making and remove roadblocks.
Working alongside key stakeholders, you will support the organization in preparing for and implementing changes — including by developing and rolling out effective engagement and communications strategies — and by preparing and supporting end users in tandem with our Learning & Development partners.
You will work closely with operational and strategic leaders, as well as with the Daily Content Director, to structure challenges, shape recommendations and guide the evolution of work practices and production tools.
As a member of T&I’s Operational Excellence Office, you will help ensure alignment, practical execution and long-term adoption of the transformation by continuously refining our approaches based on results, key insights and frontline needs. Beyond the Daily Content initiative, you will also help build the Office’s methods, practices and capabilities as well as nurture a transformation community of practice across CBC/Radio-Canada to share lessons learned and scale high-impact practices.
This position can be based in Toronto or Montreal, with occasional travel required.
Key Responsibilities
Advise leaders and teams on defining and implementing technology transformations, engaging early in the life cycle to analyze needs, diagnose challenges, identify required changes and deliver recommendations aligned with the organization's vision and goals.
Guide departments and divisions in evolving their operating models and ways of working, advising on process design, governance, roles and responsibilities, and team collaboration structures.
Develop approaches, frameworks and tools to structure and implement transformation — including simple, scalable and reusable interaction models and practical guides — with a focus on change management, Lean, SAFe and Scrum methodologies.
Design and execute change management and adoption strategies and plans, incorporating impact assessments, organizational readiness, risk mitigation and stakeholder support.
Define and lead engagement, communication and capacity-building strategies — including user training and the preparation of delivery teams and change agents — in partnership with Learning & Development.
Proactively identify and resolve risks, resistance and operational roadblocks that could hinder transformation and adoption.
Define and track metrics to measure the progress, adoption and effectiveness of new ways of working, using data and insights to continuously refine strategies.
Actively participate in key transformation forums and events, including strategic and alignment meetings, sprint reviews, program demos and quarterly planning sessions.
What You Bring
Undergraduate degree in business administration, technology or a field relevant to organizational transformation (or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience).
Seven to 10 years' experience leading large-scale technology transformations, including evolving technology operating models, processes, governance structures, roles and responsibilities, and ways of working within complex, matrixed environments.
Proven track record as a strategic transformation adviser, with strong skills in analyzing and diagnosing complex issues, challenging current practices, formulating actionable recommendations and guiding execution.

Evaluate and standardize integration protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) architectures to interconnect our models with complex production platforms (Avid, Dalet, Adobe).
Ensure absolute data security while developing video understanding systems that can interact with both file-based workflows (codecs, wrappers) and IP live workflows (SMPTE‑2110).
Technical Leadership, Mentoring and MLOps
Provide expert guidance on system efficiency, spearheading initiatives to dramatically improve architectural scalability, latency and reliability.
Mentor and elevate the organization’s engineers and data scientists in large-scale ML system design and performance engineering.
Develop robust MLOps/LLMOps pipelines with a constant focus on observability, performance profiling and automated testing.
Summarize and explain technological innovations to make them understandable to decision-makers and production teams and influence our strategic investments.

At least five years’ proven experience developing and deploying AI/ML solutions.

In this role, you will champion the lifecycle of our Workday product features, ensuring they align with broader business objectives and deliver maximum value to the organization.
You will lead, mentor, and scale a high-performing, cross-functional team of Business Analysts and Product Owners. As the bridge between business strategy and technical execution, you will own the Workday product evolution roadmap, investment alignment, governance and drive the end-to-end project management of feature rollouts, system optimizations, and semi-annual Workday releases.

Strategic Leadership & Roadmap Management
Own the Evolution Roadmap: Define, manage, and execute the multi-year product evolution roadmap for the Workday platform and third party system integrations, balancing business-critical enhancements with technical debt and scalability.

Stakeholder Alignment: Provide enterprise leadership and guidance by collaborating with People & Culture colleagues, Finance, IT, and other business units to translate organizational pain points into scalable technical solutions.
Team Management & Capability Building

Establishes and monitors performance metrics to ensure operational effectiveness and value realization.
Delivery & Project Management

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Human Resources, Information Technology, or related field

IMCO’s actively managed Global Credit strategy (~$10.1B AUM) delivers higher risk-adjusted returns through a unified approach to credit investing, integrating public and private credit within a single, globally diversified portfolio. Our collaborative culture and value-add approach to strategic partnerships makes us a preferred partner to some of the largest investors in the world. We have a targeted strategy to grow our highly diversified Global Credit portfolio and are looking for a highly motivated Associate Portfolio Manager to join our Global Credit team with a focus on public credit!
The Associate Portfolio Manager, Public Credit will play a key role in managing IMCO’s externally managed Public Credit portfolio, with responsibilities spanning manager selection and due diligence, portfolio strategy and construction, and ongoing monitoring and oversight. The role combines rigorous investment analysis with active portfolio management, while also contributing to ongoing initiatives to enhance the Global Credit platform and target operating model, including the implementation of investment systems and processes and the development of advanced analytics and AI capabilities to improve portfolio insights and support investment decision-making.

Provide analytical and portfolio management support to the Managing Director in overseeing externally managed public credit portfolios on a day-to-day basis, including ad hoc analysis and strategic initiatives.

Lead and support the preparation of investment recommendations, including drafting investment memos and presentations for internal Investment Committee approval.
Assist in structuring and negotiating investment mandates, guidelines, and negotiating fee arrangements with external managers in collaboration with risk, legal and other internal teams.
Conduct ongoing monitoring of external managers, including performance attribution, risk exposures, style drift, and adherence to investment guidelines; leverage AI to enhance efficiency in analysis, identify performance and risk trends, and support the development of portfolio-level reporting and insights for senior management.
Lead or contribute to initiatives within Global Credit to enhance portfolio management infrastructure through the application of AI and the integration of new investment systems and analytics capabilities; partner with internal teams (Risk, Performance, Operations, Technology) to improve investment data quality to enable more effective analysis, reporting, and decision-making.
Support portfolio construction and strategic asset allocation across public credit, including contributing to capital allocation decisions across segments and managers, and shaping overall portfolio strategy.
Maintain a strong understanding of global public credit markets, including macroeconomic trends, interest rates, credit spreads, and technical factors, to inform manager selection and portfolio positioning.
Engage regularly with external managers through diligence meetings, portfolio reviews, and on-site visits to assess portfolio strategy, market outlook, and execution capabilities.
Support client and stakeholder reporting, including preparation of quarterly updates, market commentary, and materials for senior management and board-level discussions.

Minimum 5+ years of experience in asset management, with a focus on public credit investing and manager selection and oversight.
Experience leveraging data analytics and AI-enabled tools to support investment research, manager evaluation, or portfolio insights.
Strong understanding of global public credit markets, including corporate bonds, leveraged loans, structured credit, and credit market dynamics.
Experience conducting due diligence on external investment managers, including evaluation of investment processes, portfolio construction, and risk management.
Experience in private debt / private credit or broader private markets is considered an asset.
Undergraduate degree required. CFA designation, MBA or master’s degree(s) are considered an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex investment information into clear, actionable insights.
Effective communicator with the ability to present investment recommendations and market views to senior stakeholders.
Collaborative team player with an appreciation for diverse perspectives and a high-performing team environment.

Located in downtown Toronto, our vision is to be the partner of choice for Ontario’s public sector funds and to build a high-performing, value-driven asset management firm.
This job posting is for an existing vacancy. If you are ready to deliver best-in-class service and join a collaborative, motivated and fun team of professionals, IMCO offers the opportunity to do impactful work and broaden your expertise.
If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
‎
We are looking for a highly motivated Principal to join our Client Relationship Management team!
IMCO’s Client Portfolio Management (CPM) Committee is a cross-functional forum with membership comprised of senior client-facing, investment and risk leaders. It is co-chaired by the Chief Investment Strategist and Chief Client Officer and enables discussion and alignment on significant investment strategy decisions that impact client portfolios.
The Principal, Client Portfolio Strategy and Governance will partner with IMCO’s client, investment, and risk teams to develop and advance strategic recommendations affecting portfolios and, where appropriate, participate in client discussions.
The role will help connect CPM’s internal investment work with client priorities by bringing client perspectives into committee discussions and supporting clear communication of portfolio implications, recommendations and trade-offs.
Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Portfolio Construction, this role will contribute to the investment decision making process by bringing investment expertise and judgment to shape portfolio themes, challenging submissions, translating investment team perspectives into decision-ready narratives, and ensuring that CPM discussions and decisions are anchored in client objectives, portfolio construction considerations, risks, trade-offs, and outcomes. The role also owns the forward-looking investment agenda and content for the CPM committee and is accountable for coordinating and advancing the development of integrated recommendations on strategic, investment and total portfolio matters within the committee’s mandate.
As a Member of Our Team You Will be Responsible For:
Client Portfolio Strategy and Recommendation Development
Partner with investment teams to identify the analysis and information required to support recommendations, interpret findings, and synthesize investment, risk, performance, portfolio construction, and client perspectives into clear implications for client portfolios.
Bring a client portfolio perspective to CPM discussions regarding strategic asset allocation (SAA) reviews, discretionary SAA matters, new investment strategies, material strategy changes, benchmarks, and other total portfolio matters within CPM’s mandate.
Partner with client-facing teams to understand evolving client objectives, constraints and governance considerations. Where appropriate, support or participate in client discussions on SAA, portfolio strategy and other material CPM matters, helping explain the investment rationale, portfolio implications, risks and trade-offs.
Ensure recommendations address client objectives, portfolio constraints, expected outcomes, implementation considerations, material risks, and trade offs.
Investment Content & Insights
Set standards for the quality of analysis and data used in CPM materials and ensure conclusions and recommendations are evidence-based, actionable, and aligned to client and portfolio objectives.
Shape complex portfolio topics into concise decision ready narratives that clearly articulate the issue, analysis, options, recommendations, key trade-offs, risks, client implications and implementation considerations, applying investment knowledge to strengthen the quality, coherence, and decision usefulness of content.
Partner with reporting, risk, and investment teams to improve the consistency, visual quality, and usability of CPM materials.
CPM Committee Leadership and Governance
Strengthen governance and elevate the quality of investment decision making, ensuring CPM discussions and outputs are rigorous, well-framed and anchored to client objectives and desired portfolio outcomes.
Lead and facilitate productive discussion among CPM members and subject matter experts, ensuring that key questions, differing perspectives, and trade offs are addressed.
Own the forward-looking CPM agenda, proactively identifying, curating, prioritizing, and sequencing items that require CPM discussion, alignment, or decision.
Maintain clear ownership of CPM outcomes, including decisions, rationale, implications, accountable owners and follow-through.
Continuously improve decision frameworks, templates, and ways of working to sharpen investment content, reduce cycle time, and improve the effectiveness of discussions.
Strategic Delivery & Cross-Functional Execution
Act as a senior advisor and CPM representative on cross-functional initiatives impacting portfolios, aligning stakeholders and driving delivery.
Work closely with and influence the CPM co-chairs, helping translate their broader priorities into a focused committee agenda, clear decision pathways, and high-impact investment content.
Build trusted, credible relationships with investment teams, senior leaders and internal partners, engaging effectively on portfolio themes, recommendations and implications.
Set clear expectations for submission quality, analytical depth, and decision framing.
Coach contributors on improving investment content for senior-level discussion and CPM decision-making.
Contribute to a high-performance, collaborative culture across CPM and partner teams.
What do you need to succeed?
7–10+ years of relevant experience in investment management, portfolio strategy, consulting/advisory, or related fields; experience supporting senior decision forums is an asset.
University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related discipline; graduate degree is an asset.
CFA designation required. Other professional designations, such as FCIA, FSA, CAIA, CIPM, or FRM, would be an asset.
Experience working in a multi-client institutional investment environment, with an understanding of how differences in client objectives, liabilities, risk tolerances, liquidity needs and governance requirements affect portfolio recommendations.
Strong understanding of portfolio construction, asset allocation, investment products, risk concepts, and how investment decisions translate into client outcomes.
Strong judgment and analytical skills including ability to synthesize complex portfolio topics and frame clear recommendations for senior audiences.
Strong writing, editing, and presentation skills; demonstrated ability to elevate materials to an executive standard.
Proven ability to influence and build relationships across functions, manage competing priorities, and drive outcomes through others.
Strong project management skills, including scoping, structuring, and delivering under tight timelines.
Credibility with investment professionals and the ability to quickly develop a strong understanding of client objectives, portfolio requirements, organizational processes, and investment products.

description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.
Our culture is built on collaboration and passion, with a shared commitment to delivering lasting value to the clients we serve. If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
‎
Risk Technology is part of the Data Technology group and partners primarily with Investment Risk to deliver technology, data, analytics, reporting, and production-support capabilities through small and medium-sized initiatives, multi-year programs, and ongoing operational services.
As a key member of the Risk Technology team, the Senior Data Engineer will be the team’s senior hands-on Power BI developer, responsible for designing complex reports and visuals, scalable semantic models, and governed business intelligence solutions. The successful candidate will be expected to apply a practical understanding of Fabric capacity, compute consumption, memory constraints, performance, and workload management.
The role also requires strong data engineering capability. The successful candidate will build and support reliable data pipelines that hydrate Power BI semantic models from enterprise data warehouses and will develop complex ETL and transformation solutions using Azure Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Data Factory, SQL, Python, and PySpark.
This position combines deep technical delivery with stakeholder partnership. The incumbent will collaborate with business users, business systems analysts, data engineers, platform teams, and external providers, and will contribute to a constructive, inclusive, and accountable team environment. The role follows the organization’s hybrid working model and requires regular in-office collaboration.
The incumbent will report to the Senior Manager, Data Technology.
As a Member of Our Team You Will be Responsible For:
Power BI development and reporting framework (Primary Area of Accountability)
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support sophisticated Power BI reports, dashboards, and interactive visual experiences for Investment Risk and related stakeholders.
Build and optimize enterprise-grade Power BI semantic models, including dimensional design, relationships, measures, calculation groups where appropriate, row-level security, object-level security, incremental refresh, and model performance tuning.
Write and optimize complex DAX and Power Query (M) logic, applying clear development standards and reusable design patterns.
Partner closely with business users to translate analytical requirements into intuitive visual designs, rapidly prototype solutions, validate usability, and incorporate feedback throughout delivery.
Understand and actively manage Fabric capacity considerations, including compute consumption, memory guardrails, concurrency, refresh demand, background versus interactive workloads, throttling risk, and workload optimization.
Use capacity and performance telemetry to identify bottlenecks, recommend remediation, and balance report responsiveness, refresh schedules, model size, and platform stability.
Design and support data pipelines that reliably hydrate Power BI semantic models from Snowflake, Databricks, enterprise data warehouses, lakehouses, and other approved data sources.
Implement governed Power BI access management, including workspaces, apps, audiences, Microsoft Entra security groups, role-based access, sharing, row-level security, deployment permissions, and periodic access reviews.
Design, build, test, and support Power Automate cloud flows that extend Power BI solutions through data-driven alerts, notifications, approvals, scheduled actions, and user-triggered workflows.
Apply appropriate Power Automate governance and support practices, including connection management, environment awareness, secure sharing, run monitoring, exception handling, and operational documentation.
Promote effective Power BI lifecycle management through source control, deployment pipelines, environment segregation, release controls, documentation, and CI/CD practices.
Data Engineering (Secondary Area of Accountability)
Develop complex, performant, and maintainable solutions in Azure Databricks and Snowflake using SQL, Python, and PySpark.
Develop and orchestrate data integration workflows using Azure Data Factory and other approved Azure data services.
Create and optimize database objects, data transformations, data quality controls, and reconciliation processes with a strong understanding of dimensional and analytical data modeling.
Build custom services and workflows when needed to complement platform capabilities, including file-format conversion, third-party API integration, and external web-service calls.
Automate manual processes and improve data delivery, observability, scalability, recoverability, and operational efficiency.
Contribute to solution architecture and technical design for the Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, and Azure data ecosystem.
Delivery, Operations and Collaboration
Work closely with business systems analysts, subject-matter experts, platform teams, and vendors to deliver solutions, investigate root causes, recommend changes, and maintain accurate technical and operational documentation.
Monitor production solutions, investigate incidents, perform performance tuning, and enhance service reliability through effective incident, problem, change, configuration, and release-management practices.
Prepare functional and technical specifications, data-flow documentation, support procedures, test evidence, deployment plans, and knowledge-transfer materials.
Facilitate testing and production implementation while acting as a trusted liaison between Technology, Investment Risk stakeholders, and external solution providers.
Share design, coding, troubleshooting, and analytical practices with colleagues through reviews, pairing, documentation, and knowledge sessions.
Demonstrate a constructive and collaborative working style, openness to feedback, accountability for outcomes, and willingness to support colleagues across disciplines.
Participate effectively in the organization’s hybrid working model, including regular in-office collaboration with the team and stakeholders.
What do you need to succeed?
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in advanced Power BI development expertise, including complex report design, visual storytelling, semantic modeling, DAX, Power Query, model optimization, refresh design, and troubleshooting.
Experience of delivering data, analytics, data warehousing, or business intelligence solutions, with substantial recent hands-on Power BI development experience.
Demonstrated experience building governed, enterprise-scale Power BI solutions rather than solely creating ad hoc or departmental reports.
Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience, or directly transferable experience with Power BI Premium capacity, including capacity monitoring, compute and memory constraints, workload management, performance tuning, and migration planning.
Experience designing and operating pipelines that load or transform data for Power BI semantic models from cloud data warehouses or Lakehouse platforms.
Practical experience administering Power BI access through workspaces, apps, audiences, security groups, permissions, and row-level security, with an understanding of least-privilege access and controlled content distribution.
Hands-on experience developing and supporting Power Automate cloud flows, ideally integrated with Power BI, Microsoft 365, approvals, alerts, or other enterprise services.
Minimum 3 years of Databricks experience with strong data engineering experience, including complex transformations and performance-aware development.
Advanced SQL skills, including complex queries, tables, views, stored procedures, query optimization, and performance tuning.
Proficiency in Python and PySpark for scalable data processing and automation.
Developed data warehouses with change data capture (CDC) and implemented dimensional data warehouses.
Understanding data quality, GitHub source control, CI/CD, and production support practices for enterprise BI and data solutions.
Strong communication, problem-solving, prioritization, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and business stakeholders in a hybrid environment.
Experience in financial services, pension management, investment management, and capital markets is desirable.
Relevant Microsoft Power BI, Fabric, Azure data engineering, Databricks, Snowflake, or Power Platform certification is an asset.

Develop communication plan to support product adoption, transition and release activities.
Ensure stakeholder needs are effectively addressed.

Coordinate cross-functional teams, including business, technical, clinical, vendor, and external partner resources, to achieve transition work.
Identify and mitigate project risks and proactively resolve issues that may impact timelines, deliverables, or stakeholder expectations.
·

Support feasibility assessments, vendor evaluations, and RFP development activities.
Research and assess software solutions to support business needs.
Collaborate within Agile delivery teams to ensure successful product implementation and ongoing optimization.

Reporting to the Manager, Cancer and Ontario Health Priorities, the Lead will connect Ontario Health portfolios, business units and regions with governments, health service providers, agencies and community partners. Build trusted partnerships
Lead engagement with internal and external partners, project teams, working groups and committees involved in policy, program design and health-system planning.

Review provincial and regional Indigenous initiatives and provide strategic recommendations that reflect FNIMUI needs and relevant strategies.
Advise Ontario Health portfolios and regions on implementing the FNIMUI Health Framework and Health Plan, including commitments and reporting.
Coordinate with the Measure, Monitor and Evaluate team to align projects with Indigenous data governance processes.
Communicate and influence
Translate complex concepts into clear written, verbal and visual materials for senior leaders, Indigenous communities and health-system partners.
Apply critical thinking and sound judgment to resolve issues, manage engagement risk and protect trusted relationships.

Completion of master’s degree in a health-related field, or an acceptable combination of education, training and experience.
At least 3-5 years of experience successfully leading and managing health care projects and/or programs
Knowledge and Skills
Build effective relationships and collaborate productively in complex, high-volume, fast-paced environments, using strong leadership, communication and influencing skills.
Think strategically, exercise sound decision-making and problem-solving, and implement programs and initiatives effectively.
Apply risk mitigation and sound judgment to protect Ontario Health’s reputation.
Work independently in a self-directed, goal-oriented manner with minimal supervision, supported by strong organization, attention to detail and time-management skills.

Strong understanding of the social determinants of health and health equity.
Extensive knowledge of federal and provincial departments responsible for Indigenous issues and Ontario’s provincial health care system.
Extensive knowledge and understanding of First Nations, Inuit and Métis history, cultures, governance structures, and health and socio-economic needs in Ontario.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and people.

You will develop meaningful visualizations and key performance indicators, connect provincial datasets, identify measurement gaps, and advise on new data collection.
You will also be the primary lead for the Ontario Laboratory Medicine Program’s Key Performance Indicator Framework—working across Ontario Health and with system partners to improve planning, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation. Your work will reveal quality gaps, explain regional and institutional variation, inform executive decisions, and translate complex data challenges into practical action.
Here is what you will be doing:
Design, develop, and optimize performance-management capabilities for Ontario’s laboratory network, including monitoring, analytics, key metrics, and reporting.
Lead KPI processes and translate provincial and regional trends into actionable insights for Laboratory Medicine testing.
Review and refine operational dashboards, scorecards, targets, tracking tools, audits, and feedback reports—including the performance-management system for Respiratory Virus testing.
Identify and resolve network operating issues, and deliver timely ad hoc analyses and recommendations to senior leaders.
Partner across Ontario Health, ministries, agencies, and laboratory-sector stakeholders to provide accurate, timely information for data-driven decisions.
Collaborate with Performance & Accountability on funding requirements, allocations, costing models, and accountability agreements.
Communicate complex findings through compelling data stories, executive reports, and practical recommendations for improvement.
Build trusted stakeholder relationships, gather feedback on program and service needs, and apply evaluation methods to guide the Ontario Laboratory Medicine Program’s evolution.
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Health Informatics, Data Analytics or a related health care field
Project Management (PMP) Certification is an asset
8+ years experience in the provision of expertise and services in the area of data analytics within the health care sector
Laboratory-related experience is an asset
Knowledge and Skills
Specialized knowledge of health data with an ability to understand and interpret qualitative and quantitative data to both identify the need for and assess the impact of changes and inform strategic decisions and goals
Knowledge in performance measurement, metrics and reporting
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, provide guidance and technical advice to solve issues as they arise, implement change and motivate team to drive strategic objectives
Exceptional judgment and extensive skillset in data analytics, evidence-based decision making, and storytelling through data visualization
Highly proficient in excel and proficiency/familiarity with other analytical tools (e.g. Python, R, PowerBI and Tableau)
Strong supervisory and project management experience that allow for managing multiple priorities at once across various stakeholder groups
An ability to distill complex and/or ambiguous problems into clear, clear, concise, compelling messages
Self-directed, with enthusiasm, initiative and demonstrated ability to work independently to deadlines under high pressure

The Health Equity Lead, Indigenous Populations will play a key role in strengthening Ontario Health Toronto’s Indigenous engagement and health equity strategies, aligned with Ontario Health’s broader Equity, Inclusion, Diversity and Anti-Racism and Indigenous Health Equity portfolios.
Working with regional and provincial partners, Indigenous communities and organizations, this role will help advance culturally safe learning, working and care environments, improve access to services, and support system-level change that responds to the needs, values and preferences of Indigenous peoples.
As a trusted connector and subject matter lead, the successful candidate will support engagement with First Nations, Inuit, Métis and Urban Indigenous communities, patients, caregivers, partners and internal teams to shape strategies that improve Indigenous health outcomes and experiences across the Toronto Region.

The Director, Cancer Clinical Programs
provides visionary leadership for a diverse portfolio of provincial clinical programs that drive excellence in cancer care across Ontario. This influential role is responsible for advancing quality improvement, clinical standards, innovation, and system-wide initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and experiences throughout the cancer journey.
Leading a broad portfolio that includes Psychosocial Oncology, Survivorship, Symptom Management, Oncology Nursing, Surgical Oncology, Radiation and Systemic Treatment, Cancer Care Integration, Specialized Services, and Patient Experience & Engagement, the Director partners with provincial clinical leaders and healthcare stakeholders to identify emerging needs, shape strategic priorities, and translate evidence into meaningful action.
The Director is accountable for developing and executing strategies that improve quality, access, equity, and outcomes across the cancer system. Through strong relationships, innovative thinking, and a commitment to continuous improvement, they drive transformational change, respond to evolving system challenges, and identify opportunities to strengthen cancer care delivery across the province.
As a senior leader, the Director oversees a high-performing multidisciplinary team, ensuring the people, resources, and capabilities are in place to successfully deliver on the portfolio's mandate. The successful candidate will be a collaborative and inspiring leader with a passion for person-centred care, a track record of driving innovation, and the ability to thrive in a complex, fast-paced healthcare environment.

Provides full people leadership through a team of managers, including recruitment, performance management, coaching and development, succession planning and establishment of clear accountabilities and priorities.
Oversees the recruitment, onboarding, performance and ongoing engagement of Provincial Clinical Leads and other clinical experts.
Develops and advances business cases, funding proposals and recommendations to support provincial clinical and system priorities.
Collaborate with internal and external project teams, partners, government, working groups, committees, and colleagues to conceptualize, secure funding, plan and implement quality improvement initiatives

title: Lead, Capacity, Access & Flow
description:
Responsable, Capacité, accès aux soins et flux des patients
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Ce que Santé Ontario offre:
Chez Santé Ontario, votre croissance et votre bien-être ne sont pas seulement soutenus, ils sont célébrés à chaque étape. Ici, vous avez l'opportunité d'avoir un impact significatif tout en construisant une carrière épanouissante et durable. En fonction du poste que vous occupez, vous pourriez avoir droit
Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,
avec des prestations médicales, dentaires et optiques entièrement prises en charge pour vous et votre famille
Des comptes de dépenses flexibles pour les soins de santé ou le bien-être,
ainsi qu'un programme inclusif pour soutenir votre bien-être.
Un régime de retraite préférentiel à prestations déterminées,
assurant une sécurité financière à long terme
Un droit à des congés compétitifs
qui donnent le temps de se ressourcer
Trois jours personnels et deux jours flottants par an
, offrant ainsi une flexibilité favorisant l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, en plus des jours de congés
Des opportunités de formation continue et de développement de carrière
conçues pour vous aider à progresser, à évoluer et à vous épanouir dans votre profession.
Un environnement de travail collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs,
où l'intégrité, la bienveillance, l'humilité, l'inspiration et la ténacité façonnent tout ce que nous faisons.
Des possibilités de participer à des communautés inclusives –
favorisant le sentiment d’appartenance, l’équité et le partage de perspectives diverses au sein de notre équipe
Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Relevant du directeur, Capacité, accès aux soins et flux des patients, le responsable fait progresser les stratégies régionales visant à améliorer la capacité du système de santé, l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux autres niveaux de soins (ANS) à Toronto.
Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le titulaire collabore avec des dirigeants cliniques et administratifs ainsi qu'avec des équipes transversales afin de renforcer la performance et les activités du système de santé dans l'ensemble de la région de Toronto.
Il s'agit d'un rôle régional axé sur l'évolution des besoins et des priorités de la région de Toronto.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Planification et amélioration du système de santé
Analyser les données régionales, les commentaires de la communauté et les pratiques exemplaires afin de cerner les lacunes du système, les priorités et les possibilités d'amélioration.
Diriger des initiatives régionales et des plans d'action éclairés par les données afin d'améliorer l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux ANS.
Planification de la capacité du système
Surveiller la performance régionale en matière d'accès et de flux, cerner les tendances et les lacunes et soutenir les plans de capacité à court et à long terme qui favorisent le flux des patients.
Établissement et gestion des relations avec les intervenants
Établir des relations de confiance avec les fournisseurs de services de santé, les partenaires provinciaux et régionaux et les équipes internes afin d'harmoniser les priorités et de faire progresser les objectifs communs du système.
Fournir des conseils stratégiques et diriger des comités, des groupes de travail et des discussions avec les intervenants concernant l'accès, le flux et l'amélioration du système.
Gestion et réalisation de projets
Diriger des initiatives complexes et de grande envergure tout au long du cycle de vie des projets, en établissant des plans de travail, des jalons, les risques, la gouvernance et les outils de réalisation.
Coordonner les ressources internes et externes, harmoniser les processus de planification et communiquer les progrès aux partenaires et aux dirigeants principaux.
Gestion des enjeux et des intervenants
Anticiper et résoudre les enjeux complexes, élaborer des solutions pratiques et faciliter l'harmonisation entre les partenaires et les intervenants.
Cerner les possibilités de partenariat qui font progresser les priorités et les initiatives de Santé Ontario Toronto.
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme universitaire en administration de la santé, en soins de santé, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise est privilégiée. Une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience sera prise en considération.
Au moins cinq années d'expérience dans un milieu de soins de santé.
Expérience en analyse de données, assortie d'un solide sens des finances.
Excellentes compétences informatiques, notamment dans l'utilisation de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint et SharePoint.
Capacité démontrée à établir, à renforcer et à maintenir des relations stratégiques avec les cliniciens, les gouvernements locaux et provincial, les fournisseurs de services de santé et d'autres intervenants clés, ainsi qu'à travailler efficacement au sein d'équipes diversifiées.
Connaissances et compétences
Solide compréhension du système de soins de santé et du continuum de soins, notamment des processus cliniques, de l'accès et du flux à l'échelle régionale ainsi que de leurs interactions avec les intervenants du système.

This is a unique opportunity to influence system-wide change by applying a provincial perspective to complex clinical quality challenges and helping remove barriers that enable meaningful improvements at the point of care.
This is an exciting opportunity to address complex healthcare challenges from a system-wide perspective, influence frontline change, and support the ongoing success of Ontario Health's Quality Improvement Plan (QIP) program.
Here is what you will be doing:
Supports Quality Improvement Programs
Working in partnership with internal and external stakeholders, develops, implements and evaluates strategies to facilitate the large scale spread of provincial programs designed to promote quality and to reduce clinical variation and inequities

Ensures timely response to concerns arising from a large and diverse audience

Establishes trust and builds strong internal and external relationships with partners and key stakeholders to remain current on local priorities, emerging issues, and trends
Supports committees and working groups comprised of both internal and external stakeholders
Works collaboratively across Ontario Health portfolios, including the regions, and with system partners

Drives an understanding of relevant indicators needed for areas of focus with colleagues and stakeholders
Recommends relevant indicators in consultation within OH and external partners
In consultation with senior analyst, designs mixed methods analysis, incorporating into reports
Leads learning collaboratives and communities of practice to drive improvement in priority areas
Understands how to navigate multiple BI platforms and health system performance reporting products (e.g., Quality Standards eReports, Quality Based Procedures, Power BI dashboards)

Experience engaging clinicians, front line staff, patients and caregivers in design and delivery of clinical care

Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer
Ontario Health is implementing one of the most significant health system transformations in Canada. Created in 2019 to connect and coordinate care across the province, the agency unites world-class expertise in clinical care, digital health, quality, and system planning. Guided by its values of
Integrity, Inspiration, Tenacity, Humility, and Care
, Ontario Health works with partners across hospitals, community services, mental health, home care, and more to deliver better health outcomes and experiences for every Ontarian.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
The Position
Ontario Health is seeking an accomplished, astute, and highly strategic executive to serve as its next Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer. Reporting to the President and CEO and serving as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will provide enterprise leadership for Ontario Health communications, corporate and public affairs, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is a highly influential role at the intersection of government, health system transformation, and enterprise leadership. As a trusted advisor to the President and CEO, Board Chair, and senior leaders, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will help shape Ontario Health’s strategic positioning, reputation, and relationships with government and the health system.
A central priority will be maintaining strong relationships with Ministers’ offices, Ministry leadership, and other senior government decision makers. The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will bring executive judgment, anticipate emerging issues and sensitivities, and ensure Ontario Health remains closely aligned with government priorities and expectations.
The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will also position communications as a driver and enabler of the Ontario Health strategic agenda. Through proactive planning and a clear cadence of communications, they will help ensure Ontario Health has a compelling story to share about its priorities, progress, and impact, both within the organization and with external stakeholders. The Communications and Corporate Affairs portfolio includes internal and external communications, media and issues management, digital communications, brand and reputation, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is not simply a communications leadership role. It is an enterprise role for an executive who can navigate complexity, influence at the highest levels, and help advance Ontario Health’s mandate across government and the health system.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished senior executive with significant leadership experience in communications, corporate affairs, or public affairs within government, the broader public sector, health care, or another complex and highly visible environment.
They bring deep experience working with elected officials and their teams, senior public servants, Boards, CEOs, and executive teams. They are recognized for sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to anticipate issues, navigate complex government environments, and build trust with senior decision makers.
An exceptional communicator and relationship builder, they can translate complex issues into compelling messages, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and operate effectively within a Crown agency environment. They combine strategic thinking with sound judgment and pragmatism and bring breadth and versatility to contribute beyond the traditional boundaries of a communications portfolio.

Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Santé Ontario recherche un cadre expérimenté, avisé et doté d'un sens aigu de la stratégie pour occuper le poste de Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes. Rattaché(e) au Président-Directeur général et membre de l'équipe de direction, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes assurera la direction stratégique des activités de Santé Ontario en matière de communication, d'affaires internes et d'affaires publiques, ainsi que de l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et de leurs familles.
Il s'agit d'un poste très influent, à la croisée des domaines de l'action publique, de la transformation du système de santé et de la direction stratégique des activités. En tant que conseiller de confiance du Président-directeur général, du président du conseil d’administration et des hauts dirigeants, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes contribuera à définir le positionnement stratégique de Santé Ontario, sa réputation et ses relations avec le gouvernement et le système de santé.
L'une des principales priorités consistera à entretenir des relations solides avec les cabinets des ministres, les responsables des ministères et les autres hauts responsables gouvernementaux. Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes fera preuve d'un jugement de haut niveau, anticipera les enjeux émergents et les sujets sensibles, et veillera à ce que Santé Ontario reste en parfaite adéquation avec les priorités et les attentes du gouvernement.
Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes aura également pour mission de faire de la communication un moteur et un catalyseur du programme stratégique de Santé Ontario. Grâce à une planification proactive et à un rythme de communication bien défini, il contribuera à faire en sorte que Santé Ontario dispose d'un message convaincant à transmettre concernant ses priorités, ses progrès et son impact, tant au sein de l'organisation qu'auprès des intervenants externes. Le portefeuille du Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes comprend les communications internes et externes, les relations avec les médias et la gestion des enjeux, les communications numériques, la marque et la réputation, ainsi que l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et des familles.
Il ne s'agit pas simplement d'un poste de direction dans le domaine de la communication. Il s'agit d'un poste de direction destiné à un cadre supérieur capable de gérer la complexité, d'exercer une influence au plus haut niveau et de contribuer à faire progresser la mission de Santé Ontario au sein du gouvernement et du système de santé.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un cadre supérieur chevronné, doté d'une solide expérience en matière de direction dans les domaines de la communication, des affaires internes ou des affaires publiques, acquise au sein du gouvernement, du secteur public au sens large, du secteur de la santé ou dans tout autre environnement complexe et très exposé aux regards du public.
Il possède une grande expérience de la collaboration avec les élus et leurs équipes, les hauts fonctionnaires, les conseils d'administration, les PDG et les équipes de direction. Il est reconnu pour son bon jugement, sa discrétion et sa capacité à anticiper les problèmes, à évoluer dans des environnements administratifs complexes et à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les hauts responsables.
Doté d'un talent exceptionnel pour la communication et la création de liens, il est capable de traduire des enjeux complexes en messages convaincants, d'instaurer un climat de confiance entre des intervenants divers et de travailler efficacement au sein d'un organisme public. Il allie réflexion stratégique, bon sens et pragmatisme, et apporte une vision large et une grande polyvalence qui lui permettent d'aller au-delà des limites traditionnelles d'un portefeuille de communication.

Reporting to the Manager, Investigations, the Investigator leads fair, thorough and timely investigations into complaints involving Ontario health sector organizations. Managing both individual and systemic matters, the role develops investigation plans, gathers and analyzes evidence, conducts interviews and inspections, and prepares clear, objective reports with well-reasoned findings and recommendations.
Here is what you will be doing:
Investigations
Manage a varied caseload of sensitive, high-profile and time-critical individual and systemic investigations, balancing timeliness, fairness and attention to detail.
Assess complaints and case files, identify key issues and risks, and develop proportionate investigation plans, methodologies and lines of inquiry.
Gather, review and analyze relevant records and evidence; plan and conduct interviews, site visits and inspections with complainants, witnesses and health sector organization staff.
Identify barriers to effective investigations, recommend practical solutions, and consult with the Manager and colleagues on strategy, resolution and escalation.
Share investigative expertise through file reviews, quality-improvement activities and support to Early Resolution Specialists.
Analysis and Report Writing
Evaluate evidence and relevant legal or regulatory considerations to develop impartial findings, recommendations and next steps.
Maintain complete, accurate and objective investigation records in the case management system.
Prepare clear, persuasive and accessible reports and correspondence that present the facts, analysis and evidence-based conclusions.
Communication
Use active listening, sound judgment and advanced interviewing skills to obtain relevant information and navigate sensitive or emotionally charged situations.
Communicate clearly, respectfully and professionally with complainants, health sector organizations, witnesses and other stakeholders across written, virtual, telephone and in-person channels.
Collaborate with the Patient Ombudsman team, provide timely case updates, flag emerging challenges and seek guidance as needed.
Compliance
Conduct work in accordance with applicable legislation, including the
Excellent Care for All Act
,
Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
,
Ontario Human Rights Code
,
Health Care Consent Act
and
Occupational Health and Safety Act
, as well as Patient Ombudsman policies and procedures.
Other Activities
Protect personal and personal health information and maintain strict confidentiality.
Contribute to learning, committees and special projects; coach colleagues and provide backup support to Early Resolution Specialists, as required.

Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and integrity, remain independent and impartial, and analyze and identify issues without injecting opinion or acting as an advocate.
Demonstrated experience in mediation and alternative dispute resolution, including effective problem-solving and facilitating resolutions.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing investigation plans, supported by strong research and analytical skills to assess evidentiary relevance, identify risks and take appropriate steps to mitigate them.
Proven ability to interview individuals at all organizational levels, using strong interpersonal skills and discretion to manage and diffuse emotionally charged situations.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, with a demonstrated commitment to customer service and quality service delivery and the ability to work with and respond effectively to a diverse population.
Self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively, maintain effective professional working relationships, and manage multiple priorities while completing investigations quickly without compromising quality or objectivity.
Proficient in Microsoft Office, case and information management systems, and office technologies.
Valid Class “G” driver’s licence and demonstrated ability to drive a motor vehicle.
Ability to travel to conduct interviews, gather evidence and complete inspections, and to attend meetings, events, training or conferences; occasional overnight travel is required.
Ability to attend public hospitals, long-term care facilities and private homes to conduct interviews and inspections, including working independently and interacting with vulnerable people. Investigators must provide a Vulnerable Sector Police Reference Check within sixty (60) days of employment.

title: Chief Regional Officer, Toronto and East
description:
La version française de cette offre d'emploi est fournie ci-dessous.
At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care.
What Ontario Health offers:
At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:
Comprehensive health coverage from day one
, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts
, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan

that encourages time to rest and recharge
