Ongoing learning and career development opportunities
designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace
where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion
, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity.
Ontario Health is implementing one of the most significant health system transformations in Canada. Created in 2019 to connect and coordinate care across the province, the agency unites world-class expertise in clinical care, digital health, quality, and system planning. Guided by its values of
Integrity, Inspiration, Tenacity, Humility, and Care
, Ontario Health works with partners across hospitals, community services, mental health, home care, and more to deliver better health outcomes and experiences for every Ontarian.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
The Position
Reporting to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Regional Officer (CRO) for the Toronto and East Regions leads one of Ontario Health’s most complex and diverse portfolios. This region spans major urban academic centres and regional hospitals to small rural providers, as well as a diverse network of community-based services. The CRO is a visible and trusted system leader, accountable for translating provincial priorities into action, advancing regional integration, and ensuring consistent, high-quality, and measurable results across a challenging and dynamic environment.
Internally, the CRO will work closely with Ontario Health’s senior leadership team to align people, resources, and strategy, building team cohesion, strengthening operational capacity, and fostering a culture of collaboration and high performance. Externally, the CRO will represent Ontario Health with health service providers, Ministry officials, community leaders, and political stakeholders, cultivating trust-based relationships and navigating complex issues with clarity and integrity.
The CRO will provide credible, solution-focused leadership to help providers navigate workforce shortages, financial pressures, and infrastructure challenges while maintaining alignment with provincial standards. They will strengthen integration and planning across sectors, using data, relationships, and funding levers to improve access, continuity, and efficiency of care. Accountable for delivering on provincial performance targets that directly affect patient care and system sustainability, the CRO will monitor progress, act on emerging issues, and ensure measurable results. In a politically complex environment, they will build strong, respectful relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, addressing sensitive matters with diplomacy and transparency. At the same time, they will lead long-term system transformation, ensuring that immediate operational successes lay the foundation for a forward-looking vision of regional health system improvement.
This is an exceptional opportunity to shape system performance and integration in a region that reflects the full diversity of Ontario’s health landscape. The incoming CRO will guide the regions through ongoing operational pressures, while keeping a clear focus on long-term transformation and equity.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished health system leader with senior-level experience in health care service delivery, operational and financial administration, performance management, and/or data analytics. Adept at navigating complex, multi-stakeholder environments, they bring strong political acumen and a proven ability to work effectively with government, service providers, boards, and community stakeholders. They possess deep knowledge of Ontario’s health sector, including funding models, policy directions, and transformation priorities, and are skilled at turning strategic vision into measurable results. A collaborative and values-driven leader, they build trust, foster alignment, and inspire teams toward shared goals. Resilient and grounded, they demonstrate sound judgment, thrive in complexity, and remain focused on improving care and equity for the people and communities of Ontario.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.

Directeur général régional de Toronto et de l'Est
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Relevant du président-directeur général, le directeur général régional (DGR) des régions de Toronto et de l'Est dirige l'un des portefeuilles les plus complexes et diversifiés de Santé Ontario. Cette région englobe aussi bien de grands centres universitaires urbains et des hôpitaux régionaux que de petits fournisseurs en milieu rural, ainsi qu'un réseau diversifié de services communautaires. Le DGR est un responsable reconnu et de confiance du système, chargé de traduire les priorités provinciales en actions, de faire progresser l'intégration régionale et de garantir des résultats cohérents, de haute qualité et mesurables dans un environnement difficile et dynamique.
En interne, le DGR travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de haute direction de Santé Ontario afin d'harmoniser les personnes, les ressources et la stratégie, de renforcer la cohésion de l'équipe et la capacité opérationnelle et de favoriser une culture de collaboration et de haute performance. En externe, le DGR représente Santé Ontario auprès des fournisseurs de services de santé, des représentants du ministère, des dirigeants communautaires et des intervenants politiques, en cultivant des relations fondées sur la confiance et en abordant des questions complexes avec clarté et intégrité.
Le DGR assure une direction crédible et axée sur les solutions afin d'aider les fournisseurs à faire face aux pénuries de main-d'œuvre, aux pressions financières et aux défis liés aux infrastructures, tout en maintenant la conformité aux normes provinciales. Il renforcera l'intégration et la planification entre les secteurs, en utilisant les données, les relations et les leviers de financement afin d'améliorer l'accès, la continuité et l'efficacité des soins. Responsable de la réalisation des objectifs de performance provinciaux qui influent directement sur les soins aux patients et la viabilité du système, le DGR suit les progrès accomplis, prend des mesures pour régler les problèmes émergents et veille à l'obtention de résultats mesurables. Dans un environnement politiquement complexe, il établit des relations solides et respectueuses avec un large éventail d'intervenants, tout en abordant les questions sensibles avec diplomatie et transparence. Parallèlement, il coordonne la transformation à long terme du système, en veillant à ce que les succès opérationnels immédiats jettent les bases d'une vision prospective de l'amélioration du système de santé régional.
Il s'agit d'une occasion exceptionnelle de façonner la performance et l'intégration du système dans une région qui reflète toute la diversité du paysage de la santé en Ontario. Le nouveau DGR guidera les régions face aux pressions opérationnelles continues, tout en maintenant clairement le cap sur la transformation à long terme et l'équité.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un responsable accompli du système de santé possédant une expérience de haut niveau dans la fourniture de services de soins de santé, l'administration opérationnelle et financière, la gestion du rendement et/ou l'analyse des données. Apte à évoluer dans des environnements complexes impliquant de multiples intervenants, il fait preuve d'un sens politique aigu et d'une capacité avérée à travailler efficacement avec les pouvoirs publics, les fournisseurs de services, les conseils d'administration et les intervenants communautaires. Il possède une connaissance approfondie du secteur de la santé de l'Ontario, notamment des modèles de financement, des orientations politiques et des priorités de transformation. Il est également capable de transformer la vision stratégique en résultats mesurables. En tant que responsable collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs, il instaure la confiance, favorise la coordination et motive les équipes à atteindre des objectifs communs. Résilient et pragmatique, il fait preuve d'un bon jugement, s'épanouit dans les situations complexes et reste concentré sur l'amélioration des soins et de l'équité pour la population et les communautés de l'Ontario.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.

title: Manager, Planning and Implementation
description:
Responsable de la planification et de la mise en œuvre
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Ce que Santé Ontario offre:
Chez Santé Ontario, votre croissance et votre bien-être ne sont pas seulement soutenus, ils sont célébrés à chaque étape. Ici, vous avez l'opportunité d'avoir un impact significatif tout en construisant une carrière épanouissante et durable. En fonction du poste que vous occupez, vous pourriez avoir droit
Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,
avec des prestations médicales, dentaires et optiques entièrement prises en charge pour vous et votre famille
Des comptes de dépenses flexibles pour les soins de santé ou le bien-être,
ainsi qu'un programme inclusif pour soutenir votre bien-être.
Un régime de retraite préférentiel à prestations déterminées,
assurant une sécurité financière à long terme
Un droit à des congés compétitifs
qui donnent le temps de se ressourcer
Trois jours personnels et deux jours flottants par an
, offrant ainsi une flexibilité favorisant l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle, en plus des jours de congés
Des opportunités de formation continue et de développement de carrière
conçues pour vous aider à progresser, à évoluer et à vous épanouir dans votre profession.
Un environnement de travail collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs,
où l'intégrité, la bienveillance, l'humilité, l'inspiration et la ténacité façonnent tout ce que nous faisons.
Des possibilités de participer à des communautés inclusives –
favorisant le sentiment d’appartenance, l’équité et le partage de perspectives diverses au sein de notre équipe
Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Le Responsable de la planification et de la mise en œuvre joue un rôle clé de direction dans la promotion d'une planification intégrée et axée sur la communauté du système de santé dans toute la région Est de Santé Ontario. En étroite collaboration avec le Directeur de la planification et de la mise en œuvre, le titulaire de ce poste contribue à définir, mettre en œuvre et évaluer les stratégies régionales visant à améliorer l'accès, l'équité, les résultats et l'expérience des communautés que nous servons.
Il s'agit d'une opportunité pour un dirigeant doté d'un esprit de collaboration et d'une approche systémique de piloter des initiatives de planification, de nouer des partenariats solides et de soutenir la mise en œuvre de programmes prioritaires en adéquation avec les objectifs provinciaux et régionaux.
Ce rôle régional vise à répondre aux besoins et priorités spécifiques de la région Est de Santé Ontario.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Diriger et soutenir la planification, la conception, la mise en œuvre et l'évaluation, à l'échelle régionale, des initiatives visant à promouvoir l'équité en matière de santé, à soutenir les populations prioritaires, à favoriser l'intégration, à renforcer l'engagement et à répondre aux autres priorités de la région Est.
Mettre en place des structures, des processus et des mesures de performance au niveau régional afin de faciliter la mise en œuvre, le suivi, l'établissement de rapports et l'amélioration continue.
Établir et entretenir des relations solides avec les partenaires internes et externes afin d'identifier les obstacles, les lacunes et les possibilités d'amélioration du système.
Mettre à profit la connaissance du système et les partenariats pour soutenir des programmes novateurs et intégrés qui aident les communautés à accéder aux soins et aux services appropriés au moment où elles en ont besoin.
Promouvoir la prise de décisions fondée sur des données probantes, les principes d’équité en santé et l’harmonisation avec les stratégies provinciales et régionales.
Représenter la région au sein des instances locales, régionales et provinciales compétentes afin de contribuer à la planification, à la coordination, à la mise en place de bonnes pratiques et à la définition des priorités en matière de financement.
Assurer le leadership, l'encadrement et la gestion quotidienne du personnel et des domaines de programme assignés, en veillant à leur conformité avec les meilleures pratiques, normes, directives, politiques et procédures acceptées.
Suivre, évaluer et rendre compte des activités régionales, en utilisant les données et les analyses pour appuyer la planification, l'amélioration des performances et la réalisation des objectifs stratégiques.
Se tenir informé des enjeux actuels du système de santé et des initiatives de changement liées aux priorités de la planification annuelle des activités et aux principaux domaines de résultats.
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Une licence en gestion de la santé, en administration publique ou dans un domaine connexe, assortie d'une expérience pertinente, est obligatoire; un master est préférable.
Sept années d'expérience progressive dans le domaine de la santé sont requises; une expérience axée sur l'équité en santé est préférable.
Une solide expérience dans la gestion d'équipe, la supervision des activités opérationnelles quotidiennes et l'alignement du travail sur les objectifs généraux de l'entreprise.
Une solide expérience dans l'intégration de projets d'envergure et complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution, avec une expertise en matière de mise en œuvre opérationnelle et de programmes.
Un sens profond des affaires, avec la capacité de mobiliser les principaux partenaires du système dans la réalisation des activités opérationnelles et des programmes; une expérience clinique est un atout.
Une expérience avérée dans l'établissement et le maintien de relations et de partenariats au sein du secteur de la santé et du gouvernement provincial, en mettant l'accent sur l'intégration des systèmes et la promotion de changements à l'échelle du système.
Des capacités de leadership exceptionnelles, notamment en matière de créativité, d'innovation, d'intégrité, d'initiative et de passion.
La capacité à travailler de manière autonome, à assumer la responsabilité de ses actions et à s'aligner sur la vision et les orientations de la direction.
La capacité à préparer et à présenter des exposés sur des informations techniques et/ou sensibles à des publics divers.
La capacité à gérer plusieurs projets simultanément, appuyée par des compétences avancées en gestion de projet.
La capacité à faire preuve de discernement sur des questions sensibles et controversées et à négocier un consensus autour de stratégies politiques complexes.
D’excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite, avec la capacité de fournir et d'obtenir des informations complexes, techniques ou sensibles de manière claire, concise, logique et dans un format adapté au public.
La maîtrise de la langue française est un atout.
Connaissances et compétences
Un sens des affaires et réflexion systémique, ainsi que la capacité à mettre en œuvre les principes de gestion financière, de gestion des ressources humaines, de dynamique organisationnelle et de gouvernance, de planification stratégique, de gestion des risques et d'amélioration de la qualité dans le secteur de la santé.
Une capacité à mobiliser les intervenants, à gérer les relations et à faire preuve de finesse politique, avec l'aptitude à développer des réseaux, à nouer des alliances, à collaborer au-delà des frontières et à entretenir des relations internes et externes qui soutiennent la performance du département et les initiatives communes.
Des compétences en communication, relations interpersonnelles et travail d'équipe, notamment l'écoute active, une communication claire et concise, le tact, la compassion, la sensibilité et le respect des besoins et des capacités des autres.
Des compétences en gestion des risques et en mesure de la performance, notamment la capacité à mesurer et à évaluer les résultats, à ajuster la direction en conséquence et à soutenir le dialogue et l'analyse grâce aux informations sur la performance organisationnelle.
Des compétences en matière de planification stratégique et de gestion du changement, associées à la capacité de communiquer les objectifs de l'entreprise, d'harmoniser les tâches et les objectifs du service, de définir des cibles et des indicateurs clairs, et d'accompagner les collaborateurs dans les efforts de changement et les initiatives visant à améliorer les performances du service.
Des connaissances en matière de conception de systèmes, de planification des soins de santé et d'élaboration de programmes, notamment la capacité à rechercher des idées, des bonnes pratiques et des tendances; à comprendre le système et l'environnement des soins de santé; et à planifier, mettre en œuvre et évaluer des politiques et/ou des programmes de santé.
Une capacité à développer de nouvelles perspectives, à mettre en œuvre des solutions innovantes, à favoriser la pensée créative et l'innovation, ainsi qu'à concevoir et mettre en œuvre des programmes ou des processus nouveaux ou de pointe.
Une connaissance du secteur de la santé en Ontario, des tendances relatives à la main-d'œuvre dans ce secteur, des enjeux, priorités et besoins locaux en matière de santé, ainsi que des grandes tendances en matière de politique de santé et de développement du système de santé.
Une connaissance et une compréhension du secteur associatif et des programmes qui y sont liés, notamment, mais sans s'y limiter, la santé mentale, les dépendances et la santé liée à la consommation de substances, ainsi que l'intégration au sein du système de santé.
Une connaissance des besoins des populations autochtones urbaines et communautaires ainsi que des communautés francophones.
Une connaissance approfondie des modèles et approches de planification.

The Manager, Planning and Implementation plays a key leadership role in advancing integrated, community-based health system planning across Ontario Health’s East Region. This regional role is focused on addressing the distinct needs and priorities of Ontario Health’s East Region.
Here is what you will be doing:
Lead and support regional planning, design, implementation and evaluation of initiatives that advance health equity, priority populations, integrations, engagement and other East Region priorities.
Develop regional structures, processes and performance measures to support implementation, monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external partners to identify system barriers, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
Leverage system knowledge and partnerships to support innovative, integrated programs that help communities access the right care and services when they need them.
Promote evidence-informed decision-making, health equity principles and alignment with provincial and regional strategies.
Represent the region at appropriate local, regional and provincial tables to inform planning, coordination, best practices and funding priorities.
Provide leadership, guidance and day-to-day management to staff and assigned program areas, ensuring alignment with accepted best practices, standards, directives, policies and procedures.
Monitor, evaluate and report on regional activities, using data and analysis to support planning, performance improvement and achievement of strategic objectives.

7 years of progressive healthcare experience is required; experience with a health equity focus is preferred.
Solid background leading staff, overseeing day-to-day operational activities and aligning work to overarching corporate objectives.

Exceptional leadership abilities, including creativity, innovation, integrity, initiative and passion.

Ability to exercise sound judgement on sensitive and contentious issues and negotiate consensus around complex policy strategies.

title: Business and Market Data Analyst
description:
Business Unit
Regular, Full time
Closing Date: October 23, 2026
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The
Investment Management Division
oversees the regulation of investment funds and structured products that offer securities to the public in Ontario. Our function in the OSC’s mandate of providing investors protection is a vital one. We have a leadership role in developing new rules and policies within the OSC and within the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) to adapt to the changing environment in the investment fund and structured products industry. Our scope of activity includes reviewing and considering investor protection issues related to the offerings of investment products (including mutual funds, exchange traded funds, structured products, scholarship plans and labour-sponsored funds); assessing product disclosure, including prospectus and continuous disclosure filings; and considering applications for discretionary relief from Ontario securities legislation and rules.
The
Business and Market Data Analyst
position will involve playing a key role in profiling the activities of the Investment Management Division by reporting on the success and impact of Division initiatives and core work processes. The Divisions core processes include rule and policy consultation, prospectus and exemptive relief application reviews and issue-oriented reviews of important regulatory development. The Business and Market Data Analyst’s primary function will be to support the Division’s core processes by conducting research, collecting and interpreting market data and activities and supporting special policy projects the Division undertakes (i.e. Risk Methodologies, and Regulatory burden-reduction initiatives).
Reporting to the Manager, Analytics, the
Business and Market Data Analyst
will be instrumental in developing, maintaining and analyzing key financial data to measure, and report on, internally and for publication (i.e. quarterly and annual reports).
Key Duties and Responsibilities:
Market Research for Division Core Processes
Provide research, including conducting background research on topics relating to investment activities in the funds industry, novel investment products, capital market development, and investor protection concerns, as requested.
With division staff identify, plan and conduct qualitative and quantitative market research to inform on mutual funds industry trends which impact on core Division processes and decisions, including prospectus, application and continuous disclosure reviews.
Conduct analysis of investment products’ attributes and risks using internally developed analytical datasets and frameworks.
Monitor, assess and interpret trends in the investment funds and structured products markets, both in Canada and globally, and prepare and design requirements on these trends.
Proactively identify additional market data and information to collect, maintain and analyze which is conducive to the efficient and effective operation of Investment Management Division.
Identify problems whereby efficiencies can be achieved, research and evaluate various alternatives and proceed with the most efficient solution.
Assess data quality, completeness, and limitations, and document analytical assumptions and methodologies. Present research findings to the Division management team, senior staff, policy project leads and/or committees (i.e. CSA) and address questions and/or defend analysis.
Data Collection, Preparation and Analysis
Work with other divisions to identify, evaluate, access, organize, clean, validate, and maintain internal and external data sources required to support Division research, analysis, and reporting.
Maintain analytical datasets and models to support market monitoring, operational oversight, and risk‑based analysis.
With division staff interpret information related to Division operations, analyze market data, and present and report issues, findings and trends that impact on the work of the Division.
Reporting, Dashboards, and Performance Measurement
Develop, maintain dashboards and report, using Division-wide operational performance measures, to better reflect how the Division is meeting its mandate (i.e. for use in quarterly reports).
Analyze trends, anomalies, and emerging risks in market and operational data and surface issues that may require supervisory, policy, or operational action.
Enterprise Systems and Data Access
Leverage enterprise systems and platforms to extract and use data required for Division analysis and reporting.
Coordinate with enterprise system and digital teams as required to ensure appropriate data access and alignment with organizational standards.
Skills & Qualifications:
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to collect, organize, and translate data into clear insights.
Knowledge of financial markets and investment products, including mutual funds and ETFs, with the ability to analyze market trends and interpret data.
Excellent presentation, problem-solving and strategic thinking skills.
Clear and concise verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated tact and sensitivity when negotiating with diverse parties.
Ability to interact professionally with management and professionals at various levels.
Demonstrated ability to respond to ad hoc unstructured problems with planning, flexibility, communication and execution.
Demonstrated ability to conduct research and prepare dashboards.
Ability to work with minimal direction and prioritize and meet strict deadlines.
Knowledge or experience in the securities industry.
Understanding of investment funds regulation and funds’ operations.
Education & Training:
University degree in Business, Finance or a related discipline.
Experience working with data analysis and visualization skills with, data science tools such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, Python and SQL for data preparation, automation and analytical initiatives.
A minimum of 3-5 years of intermediate-level experience in the financial and/or regulatory sector, performing a similar function. Equivalent combinations of education, experience, and demonstrated competencies will be considered.
Understanding of the Canadian securities regulatory environment, with the capability of assessing the impact of various regulatory actions on stakeholders and the capital markets.
Basic knowledge of the Ontario Securities Act, regulations, policy statements, rules and internal operating procedures.
High proficiency in the MS Office suite of products.
Completion of the Canadian Securities Course, an asset.

description:

Fixed Term (Fixed Term), Full time

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
Senior Forensic Accountant
Enforcement Division
18-month Contract
The
Enforcement Division
of the Ontario Securities Commission delivers fair, vigorous, and timely enforcement responses to capital markets misconduct. The Enforcement Division investigates and litigates breaches of securities laws in Ontario.  Team members work closely with other securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations and law-enforcement agencies to enhance initiatives to fight misconduct.  A strong visible enforcement presence assists in protecting investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, fosters fair, efficient and competitive capital markets, fosters capital formation, and contributes to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk.
The Enforcement Division is recruiting a
Senior Forensic Accountant
(18-month Contract) to support the investigation of criminal activity with a focus on fraudulent and recidivist behaviour that harms retail investors. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing the Division's efforts to bring more Enforcement cases before the courts, where offenders may face significant penalties, including jail terms.
What’s in it for you?
Be an integral part of a leading-edge team leveraging an innovative mix of traditional investigative techniques, data analytics, and open-source intelligence analysis to investigate and assist in the prosecution of complex cases of Securities Act and Criminal Code offences.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.
Make a difference and have a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets.
What will you do?
Participate in complex financial investigations from intake through conclusion, including assessing referrals, identifying investigative objectives, and developing investigative strategies that evolve as the case progresses.
Lead or participate in multi-disciplinary investigation teams, establish priorities, coordinate investigative activities, and drive the timely progression of investigative files.
Direct the forensic accounting aspects of investigations in collaboration with investigators, litigators, and external law enforcement partners.
Collect, review, and analyze complex financial and non-financial evidence, including banking records, accounting records, corporate documents, digital evidence, and witness testimony, in accordance with investigative and evidentiary best practices.
Identify financial schemes, asset flows, concealment methods, and indicators of fraud, market misconduct, or other criminal and regulatory offences, and recommend appropriate investigative approaches.
Prepare comprehensive forensic accounting analyses, financial reconstructions, timelines, transaction flow charts, and evidentiary summaries to support investigative findings and recommended regulatory or criminal proceedings.
Assess evidence and make well-supported recommendations regarding investigative outcomes, enforcement action, regulatory proceedings, or criminal charges, taking into account legal considerations, evidentiary issues, and potential defences.
Draft and review investigative and legal documentation, including affidavits, Informations to Obtain (ITOs), production order materials, witness statements, evidentiary summaries, reports, and other court or tribunal-related documents.
Work closely with litigators and prosecutors to support hearing and court preparation, including disclosure review, witness preparation, identification of evidentiary gaps, analysis of inconsistencies, and development of examination strategies.
Testify as a fact witness regarding forensic accounting analyses, financial transactions, investigative findings, and chronology of events in regulatory or criminal proceedings.
What do you need to be successful in this role?
Undergraduate degree and prescribed course content required for Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) exams.
Membership in good standing with CPA Ontario or equivalent designation in another jurisdiction.
Master of Forensic Accounting (MFAcc), Certified in Financial Forensics (CFF), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), or equivalent experience.
8 to 10 years of relevant forensic accounting experience as a qualified CPA.
Strong project management skills and strategic thinking on large, complex files, with the ability to effectively manage investigative scope and deadlines by designing structured approaches based on experience.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to actively listen, probe, and interpret information, including in examining witnesses, and to present complex technical information orally and in writing in a coherent, concise, and persuasive manner.
Problem-solving skills with the ability to demonstrate professional skepticism, resourcefulness, and good business judgment.
A demonstrated understanding of the Canadian and international securities environment and securities law. Familiarity with criminal law and procedure is an asset.
Experience with fraud investigations and forensic accounting in the context of capital markets is an asset.
Knowledge of business processes and procedures, accounting standards and systems of internal control.
Experience with e-discovery software and other data analytics tools is an asset.

is passionate about making a difference and having a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets;
desires the opportunity to investigate challenging issues and work on high-profile and complex cases; and
enjoys being part of a dynamic and flexible work environment with a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.

The

This opportunity is considered to be a business critical role supporting the Enforcement Division.
The
Regulatory Investigation Team
within the Enforcement Division is hiring
Investigators
to conduct investigations into breaches of Ontario securities law and make recommendations for appropriate regulatory action.  Leveraging their prior investigative experience, the investigator will plan investigations, gather evidence, and analyze gathered information to make recommendations to move forward with litigation and participate in the litigation process when appropriate.
What will you do?
Apply investigative and industry experience to assess referrals and develop a structured investigation plan, adjusting and adapting the investigation strategy as the case develops.
Work independently, or within a multi-disciplinary investigation team, to establish priorities, identify critical tasks and advance investigations forward in a timely manner.
Manage large volumes of documents and data and work with data scientists to implement appropriate data analytics/quantitative analyses approaches.  Use your knowledge of open-source intelligence gathering and work with open-source intelligence specialists.
Collect, review and analyze documentary evidence and testimony in accordance with best practices, and identify and recommend solutions to potential issues.
Participate in making thorough recommendations as to appropriate proceedings, considering potential defenses, and prepare evidence briefs that support the recommendation.
Work collaboratively with the litigator on the preparation for court or hearings (disclosures, witnesses, hearing briefs and settlement discussions) and testify as a fact witness.
What do you need to be successful in this role?
We are looking for someone who is committed to working to protect investors and foster confidence in our capital markets, and who is naturally curious.  Experience with data analytics, open source intelligence gathering, and law enforcement or intelligence agency investigation techniques are assets as is experience and knowledge of our capital markets.  More particularly, we would prefer to see a candidate with:
Completion of an undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Criminology, Computer Science, or other STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Math) degree.
Minimum of 5 years of investigative experience specializing in financial investigations, fraud investigations, money laundering, proceeds of crime, and/or computer evidence analysis.
Law enforcement experience specializing in financial investigations, fraud investigations, money laundering, proceeds of crime, and/or computer evidence analysis.
Previous experience in an intelligence gathering role and/or formal training on intelligence extraction.
Strong understanding and knowledge of the capital markets industry, trading products, and role of participants as well as administrative and criminal justice systems, and securities legislation.
Strong understanding of emerging crypto currencies, crypto assets, crypto platforms, and current social media.
Strong project management and problem-solving skills with the ability to demonstrate professional skepticism, resourcefulness, and good business judgment.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to actively listen, probe, and interpret information, including in examining witnesses, and to present information orally and in writing coherently and concisely.
Excellent interpersonal skills and a demonstrated collaborative and results-oriented style in working effectively both within a team structure and independently, while delivering on expectations in a dynamic environment.
Superior team-based skills necessary to collaborate, inspire and demonstrate a service excellence mindset within the team and other OSC staff.
Completion of the Canadian Securities Course and/or other related industry courses is an asset.
Strong understanding of emerging crypto currencies, crypto assets, crypto platforms, and social media is an asset.

is passionate about making a difference and having a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets,

description:
Translation Services Coordinator
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: Product Development and Publishing
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
Coordinates and provides advice on translation and the integration of French language services into PHO activities and into delivery of products and services to meet the requirements of the French Language Services Act (FLSA).
Objectifs du poste
Coordonner, fournir des conseils en matière de traduction et d'intégration des services en français aux activités de Santé publique Ontario (SPO) et pour la livraison de produits et de services conformément aux exigences de la Loi sur les services en français (LSF).
Key Responsibilities-
Under the direction of the Team Lead, Production Development and Publishing, supports the implementation and execution of PHO's French Language Services (FLS) policy and strategy as well as supporting tools, training and resources including PHO managing translation requests, French-English lexicon, defining internal processes.
Manages the translation request process including the translation tracker and coordinates translation of PHO products and digital content with external service provides, ensuring compliance with Ontario Ministry of Government Services (MSG) procurement directives and guidelines; ensures all invoicing is accurate and complete.
Reviews and proofreads translated materials for quality assurance and liaises with vendors as required to enforce quality control.
Supports the development and ongoing content management of PHO's French language website and related digital content.
Provides expertise and support to internal program areas on FLS compliance and advises where PHO programs and policies may have an impact on the Francophone community.
Provides strategic advice, responses, issues management support, legislation interpretation and application on issues, trends, or complaints related to the provision of FLS.
Develops administrative processes, evaluation tools, performance measures and monitoring systems to monitor, track, evaluate and report PHO FLS requirements and activities and effectiveness of FLS implementation and compliance plans.
Supports manager in development and implementation of PHO operational policies, processes, best practices, tools and resources to promote compliance with FLS.
Develops, recommends and supports initiatives and special projects with direct impact on the Francophone community.

title: Practicum Student
employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Practicum Student
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: IPAC Physicians, Third Party Grants
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
Audit and feedback (A&F) interventions are widely used to improve antibiotic prescribing in primary care and are a key strategy in antimicrobial stewardship. Randomized trials and systematic reviews have shown that A&F can reduce inappropriate prescribing; however, the magnitude of effect varies substantially across studies.
This variability likely reflects differences in how A&F interventions are designed and delivered. A set of predefined components for A&F has been proposed based on prior evidence and expert consensus, covering aspects such as feedback content, delivery, and targeting (1). Despite this, there is limited empirical evidence on which specific components are most strongly associated with intervention effectiveness.
Understanding the contribution of individual components is essential for optimizing A&F design and improving impact. A meta-epidemiological approach allows examination of whether the presence of specific components across trials is associated with variation in effect sizes.
This study aims to systematically synthesize evidence from trials of A&F interventions for antibiotic prescribing and to assess the association between predefined intervention components and observed outcomes. The student will join a team and take the lead for this study using systematic review methodology using an AI tool.
Please note:
•	this position is only open to students who are currently enrolled in an academic program where the completion of a practicum placement is required.
•	this position is only open to students currently residing in Ontario and attending a Canadian academic institution. Preference will be given to students enrolled in Ontario-based academic institutions.
•	this is a paid placement.
Suggested placement start & end date: January to April 2027
Educational objectives
:
1.     Gain knowledge about AMR and interventions to improve antibiotic prescribing.
2.     Gain knowledge in systematic review methodology including screening and extraction of study data.
3.     Gain experience using an AI tool supporting systematic review work.
4.     Gain experience performing data analysis and manuscript writing.
Proposed deliverables at the end of the placement:
·         Participate in screening and extracting data.
·         Support the analysis of data.
·         Assist in drafting of a manuscript.
·         Presentation of findings.
Required education and experience:
·         Currently enrolled in an MPH program.
·         Experience with systematic reviews and data analysis in R is an asset.

Performs highly specialized and complex laboratory testing to respond to potential public health threats from emerging pathogens, protect public health and safety, and to support disease diagnosis, prevention and treatment and other organism of public health importance.
Performs tests and provides input to principal investigators on highly specialized and complex laboratory testing and equipment.
Under the direction of a principal investigator (e.g. molecular specialist) recommends changes to formalized procedures and new protocols for diagnostic laboratory testing of emerging pathogens. Assesses proposed laboratory procedures and reports on findings to a PI for consideration in the improvement of laboratory practices and protocols.

Job Purpose
The Manager, Building Maintenance & Operations (“Manager”) is responsible for the first‑line management of the building, and provides coordination and planning throughout the Law Society. This includes the planning, implementation and monitoring of safe and efficient services related to mechanical and electrical maintenance and operations and overseeing various service contracts.
The Manager is also accountable for the effective management of employees to facilitate responsive support services to employees across the organization. This includes managing the day-to-day work order management, janitorial services, move management, and ergonomic requests.
Qualifications
The minimum level of education required is a post-secondary university and/or college diploma or equivalent, with courses in general mechanical and electrical services, health and safety, fire and building codes.
Professional Engineer, LEED AP, and/or IFMA designations with facilities management experience implementing / managing BOMA certification program(s) is desirable.
As the Manager is expected to provide hands‑on management, the incumbent is required to have a minimum of 7 years of broad experience with a strong mechanical aptitude and experience, with at least 2 years of supervisory experience in a customer service-oriented environment.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
Thorough knowledge of mechanical systems and its associated distribution including, but not limited to, low pressure steam (ENWAVE) and circulating hot water heating systems and forced air heating and cooling systems, their maintenance and operation.
Thorough knowledge of electrical systems and its associated distribution including high voltage sub stations, electrical rooms with associated equipment, etc.
Thorough knowledge of plumbing systems and its associated distribution including sewage sump pits, boilers, tanks, etc.
Thorough knowledge of fire alarm systems and its associated distribution including F/A panels, sprinkler systems, heat/smoke detectors, etc.
Proven mechanical ability in assessing and scheduling repairs and service calls for various equipment.
Ability to read floor plans and technical drawings (i.e., riser diagrams, schematics, details, etc.) along with excellent reading and writing skills.
Thorough knowledge of construction/building materials and their usages.
Working knowledge of industry standards and safety guidelines, WHMIS, OHS Act, AODA, Building Codes, Fire Codes, Electrical Codes.
Good computer skills, experience in the use of Microsoft Word, Excel, and G Suite (Gmail, Calendar, etc.).
Sustainability: Identify and implement initiatives, cost savings, energy reduction and efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, operations, etc.
Working knowledge of a Computer Maintenance Management System (Asset Essentials)
Working knowledge of Building Automation Systems (Automated Logic).
Speaks and writes in a clear, articulate manner for individual and/or group situations.
Valid driver’s license is desirable.
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Familiarity with various software applications, including word processing, spreadsheets and computer assistance drawing programs, e‑mail and the Intranet/Internet.

Client / Customer Service Planning
Plans and coordinates the service delivery of the Building Maintenance and Operations team to ensure the safe, clean, and efficient operation of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, pneumatic and electronic systems.
Collects, monitors, and evaluates utility and waste consumption data to help implement opportunities for operational cost savings, reduce utility consumption, and improve operational efficiencies of building engineering systems.
Implements and manages a nationally recognized facility operations certification program to help continuously track and assess building operational efficiency, improve sustainability practices, reduce overall environmental footprint, and lower carbon generation.
Evaluates the required maintenance or operational work to be completed within the building and based on the impacted variables (building operations, department operations, costs/budget, time/scheduling, and physical site constraints/logistics), strategically develops a plan which minimizes negative impacts to LSO operations, while considering costs.
Evaluates the health and safety risks (dust, odours, noise, fire, flood, etc.) associated with proposed maintenance work, and details the appropriate health and safety measures to ensure both regulatory compliance while addressing any work specific concerns.
Oversees various service contracts, including but not limited to, groundskeeping, waste management, office cleaning, office shredding, graffiti removal, elevator maintenance, building automation system maintenance, emergency power testing and maintenance, grease trap removal, backflow prevention inspections, fire safety systems, washroom and hygiene products.
In collaboration with the Director, Facilities and Planning and department representatives, assesses the impact of programs related to mechanical and electrical systems, staffing, maintenance projects, budgets, supplies, and legal issues, recommending courses of action.
Plans for potential utility outages and troubleshoots to determine faults, and initiate repairs of infrastructure systems.
Coordinates and supervises preventative and proactive maintenance and repairs of systems.
Receives requests for services from staff throughout the building, assessing feasibility and prioritizing maintenance requests, liaising with clients to ensure that needed support is provided in a timely and efficient manner.
Completes work requests, either directing employees, and/or coordinating with external contractors.
Prepares Requests for Proposals, interviews, and decides on successful contractors, seeking input and approval from the Director for major contracts.
Client / Customer Service Delivery
Actively contributes to the secure and safe maintenance, repair and replacement of mechanical and electrical systems.
Responds to employee, member and builder users’ related issues and concerns.
Monitors contracts and service contractors for compliance with scope, timeline, budget and quality control, and effectiveness of service delivery.
Establishes relationships with service providers to maintain service level agreements beneficial to the Law Society.
Identifies and implements initiatives for cost savings, energy reduction and improved efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, and operations, with a commitment to sustainability.
Performs daily monitoring and checks, anticipating deadlines and seasonal requirements.
Monitors and maintains inventories of supplies, including required purchasing.
Keeps accurate and timely logs and schedules.
Ensures all services meet relevant codes and standards, including health and safety, WHMIS, and regular inspections, such as fire monitoring and sprinkler systems.
Maintains current knowledge and expertise in the area of mechanical services, ensuring a proactive approach to service delivery.

Solid understanding of payroll processes and relevant legislation, benefits administration, source deduction and government remittance procedures
General understanding of general accounting functions, including GAAP / CICA guidelines, accounts payable and financial reporting

1. Enterprise Planning & Performance Framework (Planning)
Under the guidance of the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director provides leadership and expertise to the CEO, Executive Committee, and Convocation to achieve the Law Society’s objectives with respect to enterprise planning, execution discipline, and performance accountability. Establishes and maintains enterprise planning cycles, templates and routines that translate approved strategic priorities into clear initiatives, milestones and measurable outcomes. Supports enterprise prioritization, sequencing and trade-off decisions across initiatives and resources.
2. Enterprise Planning & Accountability Reporting (Delivery)
Coordinates the development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of enterprise-level performance measures and progress against the Strategic Plan, supporting the CEO’s and Executive Committee’s accountability to the Board through clear and measurable reporting. Works with various internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams, providing leadership and expertise to team members, ensuring broad information and idea exchange.

Superior analytical and communication skills coupled with excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills.

The Ontario Cannabis Store provides safe, responsible access to recreational cannabis for adults 19 and older. We operate the sole legal online store for recreational cannabis in Ontario and are the provincial wholesaler of cannabis for private retail stores.
Working at the OCS is a unique opportunity to be part of an agile start-up in a ground-breaking new industry.  We’re a diverse team passionate about delivering a great customer experience, working together with mutual respect and building value out of our differences.  We’re an inclusive organization that understands that delivering great results comes out of ensuring every voice is heard.

Collaborate with Logistics, Supply Chain, Customer Care, and Operations teams to ensure channel readiness, inventory availability, service levels, and successful execution of key initiatives.
Optimize fulfillment performance and experience, shipping costs, and cost-to-serve while maintaining a best-in-class customer experience.
Identify operational risks, performance gaps, and continuous improvement opportunities, balancing customer, operational, regulatory, and financial objectives.

Working at the OCS is a unique opportunity to be part of an agile start-up in a ground-breaking new industry.  We’re a diverse team passionate about delivering a great customer experience, working together with mutual respect and building value out of our differences.  We’re an inclusive organization that understands that delivering great results comes out of ensuring every voice is heard.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Senior Policy Advisor to join our Corporate Affairs & Policy team—someone who can lead complex policy research and analysis, manage our day‑to‑day relationships with public‑sector partners, and assess emerging issues to support evidence‑based policy advice for senior leadership, business units across the OCS, and the Government of Ontario. This role will collaborate across the organization to support our relationship with the Ontario Ministry of Finance, develop high‑quality materials for internal and external audiences aligned with corporate priorities, and help shape policies and programs that advance Ontario’s cannabis legalization objectives. We’re looking for someone who is detail‑oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple priorities at once, and who can build strong relationships across teams to effectively deliver on key initiatives.
About Your Day
Provide policy development, market analysis, and strategic advice to the Ontario Government to inform decision‑making and recommend strategic, regulatory, and legislative actions that support a vibrant legal cannabis market, reduce illegal market activity, and enable economic growth
Develop factual, data‑driven policy analysis—including reports, briefing materials, issue notes, presentations, and jurisdictional scans—to address emerging industry issues and support organizational and government decision‑making.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders to support the delivery of strategic projects and initiatives.
Lead internal and external consultations in coordination with department leadership, senior management, and government partners.
Guide other advisors and analysts in delivering high‑quality policy products and departmental outputs.
Collaborate with the Manager, Policy to provide policy and strategic advice to operational teams and senior leadership, ensuring alignment with the OCS mandate, provincial priorities, and legislative requirements.
Monitor the policy and regulatory environment to identify opportunities, evaluate risks, and assess impacts on OCS operations.
Work with the Manager to coordinate business readiness for federal or provincial regulatory changes that affect OCS operations.
Support day‑to‑day engagement with public‑sector partners, including the Ministry of Finance, the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario, and Health Canada.
Partner with Corporate Affairs to respond to government information requests and ensure accurate, timely submissions.
Support the Manager in maintaining and strengthening relationships with municipal, provincial, and federal government partners to advance organizational and provincial cannabis‑related priorities.
Assist business units in engaging with external stakeholders to advance OCS initiatives, policies, and priorities aligned with the OCS mandate.
Support department leadership in managing acute issues and stakeholder challenges, working closely with Communications & Stakeholder Engagement.
About You
Completion of a post-secondary degree in public policy, public administration, business administration or a related field.
A Master’s degree or advanced degree in a similar field is preferred.
3-5 years+ experience in an area involving policy analysis and development, stakeholder relations, ideally within a public sector organization or within a regulated sector.
Experience interfacing with senior management, with proven ability to develop and maintain strong professional relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Significant understanding of government processes, policy, and operations.
Advanced knowledge of policy analysis and development techniques.
Exceptional time management skills, highly organized and keen attention to detail, with proven track record of simultaneously managing several deliverables delivered on time.
Strong political acuity, interpersonal, diplomatic and negotiating skills, and ability to exercise discretion and judgment.
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills (written and verbal).
Developed critical thinking, research, and analytical skills.
Intermediate skill in Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, Excel and Outlook.
Stakeholder consultation experience is preferred.
Strong analytical and evaluative skills, with comfort navigating financial and business concepts is an asset.
Project management skills to effectively lead complex initiatives is preferred .
Working knowledge of cannabis industry and issues is preferred.
Ability to provide guidance and technical leadership to other advisors/analysts is an asset.

The Contract Administrator is responsible for managing the full post-award lifecycle of procurement contracts, from contract setup through amendments, renewals, extensions, and close-out. The role ensures contracts are accurately established, maintained, and administered within the Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system, in compliance with organizational policies, approvals, and governance requirements.
Working closely with Legal, Finance, SPU colleagues, Divisions, Vendors, Vendor Relationship Management (VRM), and the Data, Analytics & Technology team, the Contract Administrator ensures contract records are complete, compliant, and support effective vendor performance oversight and reporting.
What you’ll do
Contract Execution & Administration (60%)
Review award documentation to confirm contract type, scope, value, and contractual dates prior to initiating contract setup and storage in the CLM system.
Select the correct contract workflow (new contract, amendment, renewal, or extension) and validate that all required approvals are in place before processing.
Create, update, and maintain contract records in the CLM system, ensuring contract metadata, milestones, values, key dates, and supporting documentation are complete and accurate.
Route contracts for internal and external signatures, upload fully executed documents, and activate contract records only once all contractual and procedural requirements are met.
Track upcoming contract expirations and coordinate with Divisions to confirm renewal intent or determine next steps in advance of key dates.
Manage contract amendments, renewals, and extensions by initiating the appropriate workflows, validating scope and date changes with stakeholders, and ensuring all modifications are properly documented.
Monitor contract compliance by reviewing deliverables and vendor performance obligations throughout the contract term.
Close out contracts by confirming completion of deliverables with Divisions, attaching final documentation, and archiving contract records in accordance with internal procedures.
Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Collaboration (25%)
Work closely with Legal to review proposed contract changes, confirm contractual clauses, and resolve non-standard terms as required.
Communicate with Divisions to verify deliverables, service timelines, performance expectations, and updates throughout the contract lifecycle.
Follow up with Vendors to obtain missing compliance documentation or to clarify discrepancies in submitted materials.
Collaborate with Vendor Relationship Management (VRM) to share contract compliance results for integration into vendor performance reporting and scorecards.
Partner with Sourcing Specialists to take over awarded contracts following negotiations and confirm final contract details for setup.
Oversight, Risk & Continuous Improvement (15%)
Apply established naming conventions, version control standards, and contract checklists to ensure consistency, auditability, and compliance across all contract records.
Use contract reporting provided by the Data, Analytics & Technology team (e.g., upcoming expirations, incomplete records, amendment volumes) to identify required follow-ups and confirm next steps with stakeholders.
Monitor system alerts related to key contract milestones and proactively notify responsible teams to support timely action.
Escalate recurring delays, compliance gaps, or system-related issues to the Supervisor and contribute recommendations for workflow, process, or template enhancements to improve efficiency and controls.

What you’ll do
CSWB Strategy Implementation and Portfolio Management
Translates the Board-approved CSWB Strategy and annual priorities into a multi-year implementation roadmap and detailed annual workplans.
Maintains the master implementation plan across the five CSWB outcome areas, including deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies and timelines.
Establishes and maintains a portfolio view of major CSU and cross-divisional projects to support prioritization, sequencing and management oversight.
Develops project charters, governance structures, work breakdowns, schedules, decision logs, risk and issue registers, and project-closure documentation.
Monitors implementation progress, tests the reliability of status updates and identifies delays, scope changes, unresolved decisions and capacity constraints.
Escalates material barriers and recommends practical corrective action, re-sequencing, resource adjustments or governance decisions.
Promotes consistent project-management methods while tailoring the level of documentation and control to the size, risk and complexity of each initiative.
Ensures implementation reflects TCHC’s strategic priorities, tenant-centred service commitments, equity obligations and approved CSWB principles.
Place-Based Pilots and Community Safety Planning
Leads the project management of East, Central and West CSWB pilots and any approved expansion to additional communities.
Coordinates development, implementation and periodic review of place-based Community Safety and Well-Being Plans.
Integrates operational information, tenant experience, community conditions, environmental findings, partner capacity and available analytical evidence into practical action plans.
Ensures each pilot or plan includes clearly defined outcomes, actions, owners, timelines, resources, measures and review points.
Maintains pilot-specific action, risk, issue and decision logs and ensures overdue or unresolved matters are addressed through the appropriate escalation route.
Documents implementation learning, identifies transferable practices and recommends adjustments to the operating model before broader expansion.
Develops and applies readiness, need, sustainability and capacity criteria when recommending whether and how CSWB planning should expand.
Integrated Service Coordination, Partnerships and Tenant Input
Establishes and supports integrated working tables for complex community safety and well-being priorities requiring coordinated action.
Coordinates participation from CSU, Regional Operations, Facilities, Tenancy Management, Programs and Partnerships, Communications and other relevant TCHC functions.
Supports structured involvement of external partners, including community organizations, health and social services, violence-prevention partners, emergency services and other public institutions.
Ensures meetings result in documented decisions, assigned actions, clear deadlines and appropriate follow-through rather than information-sharing alone.
Coordinates with corporate and regional engagement leads so that tenant priorities and lived experience inform local plans and implementation decisions.
Tracks commitments arising from tenant and partner engagement and supports timely communication back to tenants on progress and constraints.
Maintains role clarity between project coordination and the operational delivery responsibilities of Special Constables, Community Safety Advisors, investigators and other service teams.
Implementation Frameworks, Governance and Reporting
Designs and maintains implementation frameworks for cross-functional priorities, including the CSU call follow-up model and other approved service improvements.
Defines governance requirements, accountabilities, service expectations, escalation paths and closure criteria in consultation with functional owners.
Prepares concise implementation dashboards, status reports, briefing notes, presentations and decision materials for the Senior Director and senior management.
Supports preparation of ELT, Committee and Board reports by providing validated implementation status, risks, milestones, lessons and next steps.
Works with Research, Analytics and Performance to align implementation milestones with appropriate performance measures, baselines and evaluation plans.
Works with Records and Quality Assurance to ensure implementation controls, records and compliance requirements are incorporated into project design.
Maintains complete, accurate and accessible project records in accordance with TCHC records-management, privacy and information-security requirements.
Functional Leadership, Resource Stewardship and Continuous Improvement
Provides functional leadership and direction to employees, consultants, working groups and project teams assigned to CSWB implementation initiatives.
Builds cooperation among stakeholders with different mandates, priorities and operational pressures and facilitates resolution of implementation issues.
Develops project resource estimates and supports annual business planning, budget development, procurement and business-case preparation.
Monitors approved project expenditures, contracts and deliverables within delegated authority and promptly identifies variances or emerging pressures.
Identifies change-management, communication, policy, technology and training requirements needed for successful implementation and coordinates with the accountable functional leads.
Promotes an inclusive, respectful, trauma-informed and learning-oriented approach to project leadership and community safety planning.
Undertakes other related responsibilities and special projects assigned by the Senior Director.
What you’ll need
Post-secondary degree or diploma in public administration, business administration, project management, community development, social sciences, public policy or a related discipline.
A Project Management Professional (PMP), PRINCE2, Change Management or comparable project-management credential is an asset.
An equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible experience may be considered.
Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible experience leading complex projects, strategy implementation, program implementation or cross-functional service improvement.
Demonstrated experience coordinating initiatives involving multiple business units, external partners and community stakeholders.
Experience in housing, municipal government, community safety and well-being, public safety, social services or another complex public-service environment is an asset.
Experience developing implementation plans, risk and issue registers, executive briefings, governance materials and progress reports.
Experience providing leadership to project teams, consultants or staff; formal people-management experience is an asset.
Thorough knowledge of project and program management methods, including scope, schedule, risk, dependency, change, stakeholder and benefits management.
Strong understanding of place-based planning, integrated service delivery, community development, tenant engagement and equity-informed implementation.
Ability to translate broad strategic direction into clear work packages, accountabilities, milestones and measurable deliverables.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify implementation barriers, assess options and make practical recommendations.
Excellent facilitation, negotiation and relationship-management skills, with the ability to secure cooperation where authority is shared.
Excellent written communication skills to prepare Board and executive materials, project documentation, presentations and plain-language updates.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities, deadlines and stakeholders.
