title: Director, Legal Services
description:
CreateTO
is shaping Toronto’s future through impactful real estate solutions. A City of Toronto agency, CreateTO works collaboratively with internal stakeholders, external partners and community members to create more livable, sustainable and inclusive communities. CreateTO is here to increase the social, cultural and economic value of our city’s $27-billion real estate portfolio, ensuring positive impacts for residents and a bright future for Toronto.
We are looking for a lawyer who understands the business and strategic objectives behind a transaction, can identify and manage risk while minimizing project delays, and can provide clear, practical advice to senior leaders and project teams. If you’re passionate about contributing to the best use of one of North America’s largest and most valuable real estate portfolios, we’d love to have you on the team.
THE OPPORTUNITY
The Director, Legal Services supports the Associate General Counsels and Chief Legal Counsel in resolving legal issues, ensuring legal compliance and mitigating risks. The role includes:
Supporting the legal aspects of the assigned portfolio of projects and corporate functions.
Providing advice on legal implications related to CreateTO’s projects.
Maintaining an awareness of legal and regulatory matters relevant to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Advising project leads on all legal matters affecting CreateTO’s projects and business arrangements to support operational decision-making.
PRINCIPAL FUNCTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Maintaining a deep understanding of CreateTO’s business and industry and providing leadership in operational business decisions from a legal perspective.
Leading the drafting and negotiating of complex real estate and leasing transactions, including acquisitions, dispositions, leases, licences, easements, rights-of-way, development agreements, reciprocal rights and operating agreements, and other property-related arrangements.
Providing strategic legal advice on lease structuring, property/asset management, development rights, environmental matters, litigation and other landlord and tenant issues.
Advising on transaction structures involving public and private-sector partners, joint ventures, development partners and other stakeholders.
Providing legal advice throughout the development lifecycle, from early feasibility and structuring through approvals, financing, construction, project delivery and long-term operations.
Providing legal advice on construction and capital projects, including construction agreements (e.g. CCDC and OAA), consultant agreements, low carbon and sustainability initiatives, procurement, project delivery, insurance, contractor/consultant performance, change orders, claims, disputes, litigation and other construction related matters.
Conducting due diligence on real estate and commercial leasing transactions, including title searches and corporate searches.
Navigating legal and regulatory challenges to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Providing direction and supervision to external counsel, including with respect to litigation, arbitrations, mediations and expropriations.
CANDIDATE ATTRIBUTES
An experienced lawyer with 7+ years of broad real estate, commercial leasing, development and construction experience that meets the above requirements, and the ability to lead cross-divisional teams to resolve legal issues.
Ideally will have had exposure to public and private sector real estate interests and land use planning, as well as gained corporate governance experience and board experience.
Aptitude for detail, with a high level of accuracy and superior legal drafting skills.
Exceptional organizational skills are necessary to coordinate a variety of responsibilities, in an often-changing environment, to achieve stated goals and objectives.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to exercise good judgment, tact and discretion.
Ability to work with highly confidential information with both maturity and professionalism.
A high degree of competence in verbal and written communication.
Ability to solve problems and take the initiative.
TOTAL COMPENSATION
The salary range for this position is $128,270 to $192,910 annually, with the expected range for this role to start between $150,000 to $160,000 commensurate with qualifications and experience.
In addition to base salary, CreateTO offers a comprehensive total compensation package including participation in the OMERS defined benefit pension plan, competitive vacation entitlement, extended health and dental benefits, life and disability insurance, and access to employee wellness support including an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
With a highly engaged team, CreateTO scores well above benchmarked organizations in terms of its employees’ passion, commitment, diversity and pride. As part of the organization’s Strategic Plan 2023-2027, “Inspire internal success” was named as one of five priority objectives.
CreateTO wants its team to reflect the city we represent, and we strive to provide an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and perspective, all of which are proven to build better companies. Our goal is to create an environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work and be themselves.
We provide equitable treatment and accommodation to ensure barrier-free employment in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Candidates can request accommodation related to the protected grounds at any stage of the hiring process.
Interested and qualified candidates are required to submit their resume and cover letter. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Submissions that don’t include the requirements noted above will not be considered. Only those individuals selected for an interview will be contacted. No agencies at this time please.
We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess, or select applicants. All applications are reviewed by our hiring team.
For more information on CreateTO, please visit our website at
www.createto.ca
.
Please note that this is a hybrid working environment with a minimum of 3 days in-office.

title: Licensing Analyst
description:
WHY WORK AT HCRA:
We foster a professional home building industry that Ontarians can trust.
The Home Construction Regulatory Authority (HCRA) is a not-for-profit corporation that is designated by the provincial government of Ontario to administer and enforce the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017 and associated regulations. HCRA holds licensed builders to professional standards, protects the public interest, and enhances consumer confidence in the homebuilding industry in Ontario. In addition, HCRA strives to educate consumers to ensure that they can make informed decisions and understand the benefits of a regulated homebuilding sector. As one of Ontario’s newest regulators, HCRA is dedicated to providing the highest level of service to everyone they serve.
HCRA provides a flexible, hybrid and collaborative work environment, with an array of benefits as well as considerable time off allowances. Additionally, as a mid-sized organization, team members have direct exposure to senior management on a regular basis, and they get the opportunity to work on a range of assignments with significant responsibilities. By joining the HCRA, you'll be a part of the establishment of a growing regulator that is passionate, engaged, forward-thinking, and innovative.
WHAT THE POSITION IS:
We are seeking a permanent, full-time Licensing Analyst as a backfill. Reporting to the Supervisor, Licensing, you'll review and assess new licence and licence renewal applications, including supporting and historical information, and make recommendations in line with HCRA's licensing criteria and operational policies under the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017. You'll carry your own file of applications, recommending approval, conditions on the licence, or refusal, and using sound judgement about when a file needs to be escalatedfor further review. Day to day, you'll follow up with applicants to close information gaps, respond to escalated licensing inquiries, and keep records accurate and complete in Dynamics 365 CRM and the Ontario Builder Directory. You'll also support the team's administrative work as needed, including fees, payments and incoming applications. Beyond your own files, you may be asked to contribute to the development of licensing processes, guidelines, tools and forms, and consumer and public education materials, helping the team improve how licensing works and roll out program changes.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:
Success in this role requires hands-on experience assessing applications or files against legislation or policy, so you can work independently on most files within your first few months. You'll bring a sharp eye for detail and a commitment to accuracy, whether you're reviewing an application, entering data or reconciling fees. You should be able to interpret and apply legislation and policy to individual files, reach a sound, well-documented recommendation, and recognize when a file needs to be escalated. You'll manage a high-volume caseload and competing deadlines without losing accuracy, and work well both independently and with colleagues in Licensing, Finance, Professional Conduct and other teams. Just as important are strong client service and communication skills (written and verbal), including the ability to explain recommendations clearly to the Supervisor, Assistant Deputy Registrar, and senior staff, and to communicate licensing requirements to applicants in plain terms.
We are looking for two to four years of experience reviewing applications, files or submissions against legislation, regulations or policy, ideally in a regulatory, licensing or compliance environment. These skills may come from work experience, education, training, or a combination.
Experience at a Delegated Administrative Authority, regulator or licensing body would be an asset, as would knowledge of the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017 and the Ontario Building Code.
We would also value experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 or a similar CRM, experience reviewing financial, background or conduct information, and proficiency in French or another language that helps us communicate with Ontario's builders and homebuyers
Annual Salary Range:
The salary range for this position is between $68,000.00 CAD and $85,000.00 CAD (Depending on qualifications, skills, and experience).

Our Capital Projects Group workforce is made up of driven and dedicated professionals who care deeply about working together to deliver infrastructure and make a positive impact in our communities.  Join us as we build a knowledgeable and collaborative team that courageously changes how transit projects will be delivered.
Our Commercial Management Office is hiring a Claims Analyst – CPG Claims. This role will provide review, assessment, and expertise in the management of the claims process to support the Capital Projects Group’s delivery of capital and infrastructure projects, including analysis of claims and providing recommendations for resolution of those claims under the guidance of the Claims Manager, along with in-depth estimation and review of variations.
What will I be doing?
CONSTRUCTION PROJECT CLAIM ANALYST ROLE: This job ad is related to claims and change management in rail infrastructure and heavy civil construction projects. Background in civil and engineering works, including estimating and quantity surveying, is required.
Conduct analysis of claims following Metrolinx’s Claims Management Procedures for both P3 and Non-P3 Contracts, ascertaining entitlement, analyzing and assessing impacts and associated costs, and providing recommendations for resolution of the claims involving variations, delay, disruption, acceleration, and loss of production etc.
Conducts detailed review of cost impacts pertaining to Contractor’s/Subcontractor’s claims for direct costs, prolongation, loss of productivity/disruption, acceleration, escalation, unresolved variation notices/change requests.

Provides the Project Delivery Teams (PDT’s) support and advice in their analysis and mitigation of claims and Early Warning Notices and, in any negotiation, and dispute resolution with Contractors and Consultants.
Liaises with the PDT and CST in the review and analysis of claims, including engaging claim estimators and forensic schedule analyst from the CST as well as the legal teams.
Supports Claims Lead/Manager in the preparation of claim strategy, evaluations, correspondence and recommendation for resolution.
Conducts the claims management process across chosen Metrolinx transit and infrastructure projects, including management and maintenance of claims documentation/records and the timely reporting of claims status.
Implements claims analysis and management templates, policies, processes, and tools to support effective and efficient claims management.
Supports the Claims Lead/Manager during the negotiation and resolution phase and prepare various reports and presentations.
Support the CST by monitoring and providing updates to the Claims Register, managing, and resolving claims in the register, and ensuring accuracy and integrity of the data logged in the Claims Register and Unifier.
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?

a degree or diploma in construction management, project management, engineering, quantity surveying or a related discipline – or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.
Demonstrated experience of at least 2 (two) years in
major project commercial and/or claims management; progressive experience in the administration of major construction/infrastructure contracts.
Active membership in PEO, AACE, PMI, CIQS, RICS or similar association
is an asset.
Knowledge and understanding of capital construction methods, practices, contractors’ methods of tendering and contract/subcontract administration, schedule/delay analysis, cost / damage analysis, prolongation costs, acceleration costs and disruption/loss of productivity analysis.
Knowledge of AACE recommended techniques for estimating claims for extension of time/prolongation and loss of productivity. Knowledge of contractor’s estimation practices and construction pricing.
Experience and knowledge of detailed assessment of Contractor’s variations for entitlement and costs impacts in coordinating with the members of the Project Teams including SMEs, for resolving pending and potential variations and claims.
Knowledge of contract administration and project delivery using AFP, P3, or design/build methodology. Good understanding and knowledge of the practical application of contract administration and document management software, CM14, Aconex, ProjectWise, and SharePoint. Excellent written, verbal and presentation communication skills. Proficiency in MS Office (e.g., Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.). Knowledge of Scheduling software like P6, MS Project etc. will be an asset.
Well-developed problem solving and analytical skills, including being highly responsive with the ability to act quickly under changing circumstances and anticipate multiple claim paths and investigate client impacts, to keep ahead of the claimant.
Communication with Metrolinx stakeholders to update the high priority claim resolution process. Well-developed organizational skills with the ability to process and efficiently manage numerous claims. Political acuity and ability to maintain professional demeanor in challenging meetings.
A valid driver’s license is an asset since this position may require travel up to 5% to various site locations or public meetings, etc.

At Metrolinx, equity, diversity, and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.
Our Deputy Chief Financial Officer’s (DCFO) Office is looking for multiple Co-op Students to provide support within the various Finance teams. You will work with internal and external stakeholders to support financial analysis, reporting, presentations, systems maintenance, and process improvement initiatives while gaining exposure to a variety of finance functions within a large public sector organization.
We have DCFO Office, Finance co-op roles available in the following areas:
Accounting:
1 vacancy, 8-month term
Embedded Finance:
5 vacancies, 4- or 8-month terms
Financial Planning & Analysis:
1 vacancy, 8-month term
Descriptions of each area are provided below:
Accounting:
The Accounting team leads the month end close processes which facilitates the preparation of the quarterly balance sheet and annual financial statements for Senior Management, Board of Directors and our stakeholders such as the Ministry of Transportation and the Province of Ontario. The team activities include supporting the assurance work with external auditors, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Diesel Fuel Hedging, General Ledger accounting and analysis, statutory financial reporting ensuring compliance with corporate policies and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and tax compliance.
Embedded Finance - Corporate Finance, Payments Finance, and Operations Finance GO/UP:
The Embedded Finance Team works alongside the departments as a trusted business partner and is crucial in advancing the financial strategies, goals and decisions of the departments. Through active involvement, it provides well-informed financial guidance and support to enable the departments to achieve its financial goals and savings initiatives. The teams support operating and capital financial portfolios and financial asset management functions. This includes capital budgeting/forecasting, financial reporting and insights to drive effective business decisions, asset classes on memo development, and capital funding strategy development.
Embedded Finance - Operations GO/UP Capital:
The Capital team plays a key role in supporting the delivery of Operations’ capital infrastructure program. The team provides financial oversight throughout the entire project lifecycle, from project planning and funding approval to budgeting, forecasting, capitalization, and project closeout. As part of the team, you will gain exposure to capital planning, financial analysis, performance reporting, and governance processes that support major transit and infrastructure investments across the organization.
Financial Planning & Analysis:
The FP&A team plays a pivotal role in ensuring that Metrolinx is meeting its financial objectives to deliver its growing programs, while adhering to government policy and legislative requirements. The team provides analytical support to senior management and the Embedded Finance teams to enable effective data-driven decisions. This includes development of Metrolinx’s operating budget, monthly Business Performance Review report, quarterly forecasts, Metrolinx’s public-facing Business Plan as well as the Management Discussion and Analysis section of the Annual Report. The team also manages the Oracle Hyperion application.
What will I be doing?
Support business case financial modeling for various business intake projects and initiatives with a view to monitor and manage costs and inform performance management activities.
Assist with ad hoc deliverables and projects that may involve developing worksheet templates for analyses, updating process documentation/manuals, preparing PowerPoint slides, and working with various cross-functional teams on initiatives.
Help produce daily, weekly, and monthly operational documentation and reports, as assigned.
Support to staff in a variety of areas, including gathering, inputting, organizing, and interpreting data for reports/presentations/meetings/projects, and supporting year-end inventory counts.
Prepare agendas, coordinate, attend, and take minutes for daily technical/operational meetings.
Support gathering audit evidence in the external auditor’s portal.
Maintain and update electronic and hardcopy filing systems and provide records management support.
Recommend improvements to existing processes and procedures to achieve greater efficiency.
Assist with the maintenance, development, monitoring and reporting of tools and systems for data analysis.
Develop spreadsheets, forms, and databases to input, track, store and retrieve data.
Present key findings to team members and management as required.
What will I gain?
Hands-on experience supporting finance, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, and business planning activities.
Exposure to a variety of finance functions, including Accounting, Embedded Finance, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), and Capital Finance.
Opportunities to develop financial analysis, data management, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience working with financial systems, reporting tools, and large datasets.
Exposure to budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audit support, and business performance reporting processes.
Mentorship and guidance from experienced finance professionals.
The opportunity to contribute to projects that support major transit operations and infrastructure investments across the region.
What skills and qualifications do I need?
Required
Currently enrolled full-time in a recognized post-secondary co-op program and eligible to complete a co-op work term as part of your academic requirements, with plans to return to school following the work term.
Must be enrolled in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, or a related program at a post-secondary institution.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Willingness to learn and gain exposure to various areas of Finance.
Assets
Interest in Finance, Accounting, Financial Planning & Analysis, or business partnering.
Progress toward, or interest in pursuing, a CPA or CFA designation.
Experience with Power BI or other reporting and data visualization tools.
Knowledge of AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot.
French language skills.
Previous academic, volunteer, work, or co-op experience involving financial analysis, reporting, research, or data management.
Don’t Meet Every Requirement?

Reporting to the Manager, Customer Protection, Customer Protection Officers/Special Constables protect the safety and security of passengers, employees and property and to maintain the integrity of the fare system.
What will I be doing?
Proactively engages with individuals with housing needs who may be finding shelter in and around the transit system with goal of finding supports, referrals to social agencies and other assistance.
Provides the first level of emergency response assistance for infrastructure threats, fatalities and/or catastrophic injuries, fires, accidents, medical emergencies, and unlawful intrusions of Metrolinx, GO Transit and UP Express facilities and equipment.
Ensures consistent and non-discriminatory enforcement of provincial and federal statutes and GO Transit bylaw pertaining to the general conduct of patrons, fare inspections, liquor offences, and parking control.  May issue appropriate offence notices, summonses, or appearance notices to individuals for non-compliance.
Performs such duties as crowd control, searching of Metrolinx/GO Transit premises, equipment or passenger vehicles, protecting site or evidence, obtaining statements from witnesses, providing first aid and/or assistance to passengers, employees and emergency services.
Responds to criminal offences committed on or within the Metrolinx, GO Transit and UP Express system and make arrests in accordance with policy, training and legislation. Initiates on scene investigative steps and reports information to investigators/management. Transports and processes arrested persons to the regional police facility.
When necessary and appropriate, responds to persons experiencing mental health crisis, on or within the Metrolinx, Go Transit and Up Express system and apprehends under the Mental Health Act. Transports apprehended person to regional facilities when necessary.
Promote and maintain excellent customer relations and maintain the public peace within the Transit system.
Maintains operating protocol with railway and regional police services and all levels of court services within the jurisdictions serviced by Metrolinx/GO Transit.  Prepares appropriate incident reports and supplementary reports, with witness statements (if applicable) Secures, maintains and presents evidence for prosecution in the various levels of court.
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Knowledge of principles and practices normally attained through completion of a community college program in law enforcement, social work or relevant field and/or equivalent experience.
Minimum six (6) months experience directly involving law enforcement activities, social/community work with exposure to the justice system
Achievement of a passing grade in the Special Constable Fitness Assessment
Must have (prior to start date)
a Valid Level "C" First Aid, C.P.R. certificate
a Mental Health First Aid Certification from the Mental Health Commission of Canada
a valid Ontario Class “G” driver’s license and be able to meet the corporate standard for a good driving record.
Ability to interpret and apply Federal and Provincial statutes and local Bylaws.
Good interpersonal skills in order to maintain good customer service and operating protocol with railway and local police and court services within all jurisdictions serviced by Metrolinx/GO Transit.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.  Bilingual abilities would be considered an asset.
Effective and strong decision-making skills that can be applied on a regular basis in a variety of circumstances/ situations including under potentially harmful and stressful conditions.
Other Work Requirements:
Must be able to:
Pass an Ontario Provincial Police (O.P.P.) security clearance and background investigation which includes education, employment, personal history, credit and reference checks for the purpose of obtaining Special Constable Status, and to access the C.P.I.C and P.A.R.I.S information systems.
Complete environmental, safety and any other training required by corporate policy and obtain Metrolinx Equipment Operator’s Permits
Attainment and maintenance of the Special Constable Status
Achievement of a passing grade in the Special Constable Fitness Assessment prior to offer (further information on the assessment will be provided prior to the assessment)
All aspects of the Metrolinx Special Constable training program, including the field training portions
Ongoing adherence to the Special Constable Code of Conduct

Must be prepared to work on a 24-hour rotating shift basis (including days, evenings, weekends and holidays).

Work may involve encountering confrontational situations. This position requires extended periods of walking, standing, climbing stairs and regular operation of departmental vehicles over long distances for prolonged periods of time.
Work may involve encountering individuals who are violent, potentially violent, armed, mentally unstable, under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs and persons suffering from poor hygiene and/or disease.

The Enterprise AI & Data Centre of Excellence (CoE) within I&IT delivers trusted data, analytics, and AI solutions that help Metrolinx make better decisions and improve business outcomes. As a Data Scientist, you will partner with business stakeholders and technical teams to analyze data, develop machine learning models, build data pipelines, and generate insights that support strategic and operational decision-making. This role offers the opportunity to work with modern data and AI technologies while contributing to enterprise-wide innovation and continuous improvement.
What will I be doing?
Design, develop, and maintain scalable data pipelines and analytical solutions using Microsoft Azure, Databricks Lakehouse, Azure AI Foundry, Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, and Azure Data Lake Storage to support enterprise analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning initiatives.
Build, curate, and manage trusted datasets through data ingestion, transformation, integration, and quality validation processes using SQL, Python, PySpark, and Databricks.
Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to identify trends, patterns, anomalies, and opportunities that support business and operational decision-making.
Develop, validate, deploy, and monitor machine learning and AI models using regression, classification, clustering, forecasting, and generative AI techniques to solve business challenges.
Leverage Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI services to develop, evaluate, and operationalize AI applications, including generative AI, intelligent agents, and retrieval-augmented solutions.
Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand requirements, define success metrics, and translate business problems into scalable data science, analytics, and AI solutions.
Partner with Data Engineers, AI Engineers, and Solution Architects to operationalize machine learning and AI solutions through MLOps and LLMOps best practices, including model deployment, monitoring, retraining, and lifecycle management.
Extract, integrate, and analyze large-scale enterprise data from Azure cloud platforms, Databricks environments, and operational systems using distributed computing frameworks.
Develop reusable notebooks, feature engineering pipelines, semantic models, and AI assets that improve the scalability and consistency of enterprise analytics and AI capabilities.
Apply advanced statistical techniques, machine learning algorithms, and experimentation methodologies to evaluate business opportunities, measure outcomes, and quantify business value.

The Senior Manager, Internal Audit provides technical leadership and expertise in the development of audit approaches for Metrolinx’s complex I&IT and Operations programs.  The position applies deep subject matter expertise in information and payments technology, data governance and project management.  This experience will serve our multi-year audit strategies and approaches to address operational risk in alignment with international industry and audit best practices.  This role will provide leadership to the audit team on the application of International Auditing Standards and Risk Management frameworks.
The Senior Manager, Internal Audit is the senior level management position responsible for managing and overseeing complex and critical engagements within Internal Audit, in coordination with the IT and Operational Audit Director.
What will I be doing?
Advises Senior Management and the ARCC executive team on the development of multi-year audit strategies to provide assurance over Metrolinx’s complex I&IT and Operations process models, with consideration of international best practice approaches.
Leverages subject matter expertise in all aspects of the SDLC project lifecycle, and operations program management, and contracting to develop audit approaches tailored to Metrolinx’s evolving business model.
Determines the adequacy of Metrolinx’s network of risk management, controls, and governance processes, including maintaining current information on the various sources of assurance across the organization (e.g., reviews, audits, evaluations and assessments performed by the business areas or elsewhere in the organization).
Oversees execution of various audit projects and coordinates priorities with other audit manager(s) and across audit teams.
Provides strategic advice to Senior Management and the ARCC Executive on audit, risk, and compliance activities related to the Ministry of Transportation (MTO), the Office of the Auditor General of Ontario, and other external audit functions, and assesses compliance with other regulatory bodies.

Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certification in Risk Management Assurance (CRMA) certification is an asset.

Today, PRESTO offers one of the most globally advanced fare payment systems in the world having delivered new ways to pay for customers, including real time PRESTO Contactless with credit and Interac debit and PRESTO in Mobile Wallet across its transit agency clients, including the Toronto Transit Commission (TTC). Enhancing the customer experience through continuous improvement while working with our transit agency clients to support their needs, and maintaining a system that performs exceptionally, continue to drive PRESTO toward making transit better for all.
Our PRESTO (Payments) office is hiring a PCI Senior Systems Analyst, in the Compliance Oversight team, to support PCI Compliance with technical oversight, along with advisory to the PRESTO Scheme Certification assessment program, to meet internal and external client, partner and vendor needs.

What will I be doing?
Leverages subject matter expertise to provide technical oversight and guidance for full compliance with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI-DSS) - that aim to protect cardholder data during payment card transactions.
Drives the coordination of PCI compliance annual Audit and reporting as appropriate in conjunction with Senior Compliance Analyst.
Drives Remediation of PCI Audit findings / recommendations as per defined timelines
Conducts Compliance Impact Assessment/Threat Risk Assessment against multiple projects/initiatives/third party engagements.

Provides advisory to internal / external stakeholders on policies and procedures related to PCI-DSS compliance in conjunction with Senior Compliance Analyst.
Reviews contracts and RFP documentation for PCI related considerations.
Analyzes and documents technical Business Processes and Information Flows /Cardholder Dataflows.
Provides technical recommendations to mitigate risks and improve compliance operations and streamline processes to safeguard payment card information and support the integrity of the PRESTO fare collection system.

This includes, but not limited to, testing requirement and design, enhancements, and modifications, training and support as well as providing authoritative advice and recommendations for remedying risk and problems.
Provides guidance on test strategies, plans, test scenarios, test scripts and execution of certification test for the application of technology in partnership with business leaders.
Works with other team members to monitor PCI Compliance, and Certification testing, against system requirements to meet performance goals.
Reviews technical and administrative procedures are in place, training is provided, and maintenance and support arrangements are made to ensure a smooth transition into production from PCI Compliance, Certification testing, perspective in conjunction with Senior Compliance Analyst.
Monitors and tracks project progress and oversees vendor activities.
Formulates and prepares project justifications in terms of the proposed scope, budget and schedule as appropriate.

Completion of a degree in Computer Science or a related discipline – or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.
Demonstrated years’ experience in the development and support of complex technology, PCI, and preferably code certification programs or systems that meet business needs. PCIP certification is a plus.
Certification in CISSP is considered as an asset.

title: Director, Sector & Regional Development
description:
Position Summary:
The Director, Sector and Regional Development is responsible for executing on OVIN’s external engagement strategy to drive sector growth, strategic partnerships, and commercialization opportunities across Ontario’s automotive and mobility ecosystem. This role is focused on building and activating relationships with industry, global partners, government, and the broader innovation ecosystem to reinforce OVIN as a key connector and catalyst.
About the Ontario Centre of Innovation:
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is a not-for-profit organization committed to accelerating economic growth in Ontario through the commercialization of advanced technologies and research. OCI acts as a bridge among academia, industry, and government, investing in collaborative R&D, fostering innovation ecosystems, and helping promising ventures bring new technologies to market. In 2024, OCI invested $117 million across the province, including $61 million in industry contributions. These efforts helped drive the creation and retention of over 5,500 jobs and catalyzed more than $700 million in private-sector follow-on investments. OCI’s role is central to Ontario’s vision of innovation-led prosperity: by reducing the risk of commercialization, facilitating partnerships, and strategically deploying capital into high-impact technologies, OCI contributes to the province’s competitiveness, talent retention, and long-term economic resilience.
Key Responsibilities:
As the Director, you will be expected assume the following responsibilities:
Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement
Support the development and deliver on the execution of OVIN’s external engagement strategy across Ontario and priority global markets.
Build, maintain, and expand relationships with industry leaders, SMEs, post-secondary institutions, government, and ecosystem partners.
Identify and secure high-value partnerships that drive commercialization, sector growth, and new opportunities.
Represent OVIN at industry forums, events, and engagements.
Sector Strategy & Market Intelligence
Maintain a deep understanding of sector trends across automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, and defence and dual-use technologies.
Identify emerging opportunities and align engagement strategies to advance OVIN’s strategic priorities.
Provide market insights and strategic advice to inform organizational direction and portfolio growth.
Regional & Ecosystem Development
Strengthen relationships across Ontario’s regional innovation ecosystems.
Lead initiatives that promote regional development, supply chain growth, and cross-sector collaboration.
Facilitate connections between Ontario companies and global markets, customers, and partners.
Work closely with internal teams to align external opportunities with program priorities and pipeline development.
Support and contribute to corporate initiatives, advisory committees, and cross-functional activities.
Other duties as assigned
Skills and Competencies:
10+ years of progressive experience in business development, strategic partnerships, or ecosystem development within automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, or related sectors
Demonstrated success in originating, structuring, and closing complex, multi-party partnerships and collaborations.
Strong, established network across industry, government, academia, and/or global markets.
Deep understanding of the Ontario innovation ecosystem, including funding programs, commercialization pathways, and key stakeholders.
Proven ability to identify and translate market and technology trends into actionable strategic opportunities.
Experience engaging with global partners and navigating international markets and partnerships
Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to assess business cases, partnership models, and investment opportunities.
Experience working with or alongside large industry players (OEMs, Tier 1s), SMEs, and scaling companies.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-evolving environments.
Strong communication and executive presence, with experience representing organizations in high-profile forums.
Experience contributing to or shaping strategy, policy, or sector-level initiatives.
Highly developed analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights.
Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels, connecting ecosystem opportunities to programmatic outcomes.
High degree of professionalism, integrity, and sound judgment.
Internal Contacts/External Contacts
OCI staff at all levels
Industry (from the CEO to the shop floor)
Academic researchers, students, university research administrative staff
University/college/hospital/government administration
Government (at all levels, federal, provincial, and municipal)
Working Conditions
Frequent travel (30 – 70%) across Ontario.
Participation required in non-office hour events such as networking meetings and workshops

title: Lead, OVIN Incubators
description:
Who We Are:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) was established in 1987 and is a leading not-for-profit organization that works with industry, academia, and government. OCI focuses on ensuring that the people of Ontario reap the personal and economic benefits of leading-edge research underway at our publicly funded universities, colleges, and research hospitals - research that can be transformed into technologies and services that enhance quality of life and help build a globally competitive, job-creating economy in Ontario.
Specifically, OCI supports the commercialization of academic intellectual property (IP), industry-academic collaborations, and the development and adoption of emerging technologies. This includes overseeing the execution of advanced technology platforms that will equip Ontario companies to compete in a competitive global digital economy.
We also support and invest in early-stage projects where the probability of commercial success and investment return on innovation are substantial. OCI’s strong expertise in de-risking innovation helps attract private investors and other funders to new ventures, bolstering their success. We also contribute to the development and retention of talent to ensure that industry has access to personnel with the most advanced skills and knowledge and that highly trained personnel find opportunities to apply their expertise in Ontario.
OCI leads the Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network (OVIN) initiative on behalf of the Government of Ontario. OVIN builds upon Ontario’s position as a world-leading automotive manufacturing and supply jurisdiction in addition to the large cluster of information and communication technology companies operating in the province. Ontario’s high-quality post-secondary institutions, first class talent, innovative small and medium sized enterprises, and infrastructure to support entrepreneurship ensure that the province is uniquely positioned to capture the economic opportunity of the automotive technology and smart mobility innovation space and lead the global mobility transformation.
Through resources such as research and development (R&D) funding, talent development, technology acceleration, business and technical supports, and demonstration grounds, OVIN provides a competitive advantage to Ontario-based automotive and mobility companies – allowing Ontario to reinforce its position as a North American leader in transformative automotive technologies, as well as transportation and infrastructure systems.
The Opportunity:
OVIN, in collaboration with industry partners, post-secondary institutions, municipalities and regional stakeholders is launching automotive and mobility incubators, designed to:
Foster a collaborative ecosystem where researchers, entrepreneurs, startups and scale-ups can systematically engage with industry
Support research and the commercialization of IP through interdisciplinary projects
Support the translation of IP and new technologies into the creation of new ventures across the province
Provide resources and programming to support the success and viability of new ventures and regional incubation and acceleration space in the province
Reporting to the Manager, Incubators, the Lead, OVIN Incubators will be the regional representative for all incubator activities, manage the day-to-operations, and play a coordinating role between all key stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
The Lead is expected to assume operational responsibilities, including, but not limited to:
Support the Manager on the strategic planning and design of OVIN Incubators, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
Apply knowledge of research commercialization and start-up incubation/acceleration to make recommendations on program development, execution and improvements, in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
Develop and maintain a database of enterprises active in the sector.
Develop and maintain a database of academic researchers active in the sector.
Pursue extensive outreach to enterprises in the sector.
Develop and manage the incubator intake and review processes, timelines, program budgets and the day-to-day delivery of the program.
Work collaboratively and liaise with incubator partners, including members of industry and post-secondary institutions, to ensure that key requirements are defined, and program delivery executed within the appropriate framework.
Execute on the promotion of incubator programming, working in tandem with the key stakeholders and departments within OCI.
Support steering committee and other stakeholder meetings.
Support OCI/ OVIN Incubator presence at external events and functions, including delivering content at meetings, workshops, and events in support of incubator programming.
Work cross-functionally across departments and collaboratively with other OCI staff (Business Development Operations, Programs, and MARCOM etc.).
Manage program stewardship, including program monitoring and metrics, outcomes, and impacts for internal strategy and external reporting.
Support Manager to identify and manage program outcomes, and work with marketing and communications teams to develop success stories.
May be required to perform other related duties as assigned.
Qualifications
:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Business, Technology, Project Management).
3-5 years experience in program management, incubators, start-up/SME support or technology/IP development particularly in: automotive and mobility, research projects or technology integration.
Strong project management skills, including budgeting, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
Problem-solving abilities and adaptability in a dynamic environment.
Highly developed, interpretive and analytical skills in MS Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Innovation, technology commercialization, or entrepreneurship program management experience; experience with automotive and mobility programs would be a strong asset.
Occasional requirement to attend events outside of normal business hours.
Occasional travel within Ontario.
Competencies:
Team player with highly developed interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively and collaborate with people at all levels within the organization and externally.
Demonstrated high degree of initiative, efficient, organized and able to produce high quality work under pressure in a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage numerous conflicting and changing priorities simultaneously.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and take accountability to address obstacles and overcome barriers by identifying possible resolution options and alternatives.
Intellectually curious about developments and trends in a sector.
Able to demonstrate integrity and ethics in decision making and in relationships with colleagues and clients.
Able to reflect and promote OCI’s values through work with colleagues, clients and stakeholders.
Embody OCI’s commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI).

title: Manager, Strategic Sponsorships
description:

Manager, Strategic Sponsorship
s
leads the development and execution of sponsorship and funding strategies for DiscoveryX, Ontario’s premier innovation showcase and conference, and other Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) marketing and communications initiatives.

title: Program Portfolio Manager, Auto & Mobility- 9 month contract
description:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) drives the development of Ontario’s economy by helping create new jobs, products, services, technologies, and businesses. In partnership with industry, OCI co-invests to commercialize innovation originating in the province’s publicly funded colleges, universities, and research hospitals. We also support and invest in early-stage projects, where the probability of commercial success and potential total return on innovation are substantial. Another expanding focus for OCI is the development of the next generation of innovators through our entrepreneurship fellowships and programs for students and youth across Ontario. OCI’s efforts are focused on sectors of the economy with the greatest potential to drive Ontario’s future prosperity and global competitiveness: energy and environment (including water); advanced manufacturing; advanced health technologies; and information, communications technologies, and digital media. A trusted partner of government in program delivery, we are committed to advancing a whole-of-government approach as a means of streamlining funding application processes for companies and entrepreneurs.
OVIN (Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network), led by OCI, is the Government of Ontario’s flagship initiative to support the future of the automotive and mobility sector. Through innovative programming, business and technical supports, and testing and demonstration sites, the OVIN initiative is driving the commercialization of advanced technologies, cultivating the capacity of a province-wide network to drive future mobility solutions and addressing the evolving needs of Ontario's automotive and mobility sector's workforce.
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Director, Strategy & Programs - Automotive and Mobility, the Program Portfolio Manager in this contract role is responsible for the day-to-day execution of programs within the Automotive and Mobility portfolio, with additional outward-facing program oversight responsibilities with funders and projects, including project monitoring, program administration activities, and stakeholder relations. This role will work within existing financial and program administration processes and frameworks to ensure organizational efficiencies are maintained and/or maximized and that there is full alignment across all programs and initiatives.
Key Job Responsibilities:
Lead the delivery, review, and continuous improvement of OVIN’s communications strategy, including the development of communication assets, such as press releases, briefing documents, social media posts, speaker notes and keynote presentations.
Engage stakeholders in the creation and execution of industry-leading events and education opportunities (conferences, meetups, workshops, panels, hackathons, best practices, etc.).
Working in with the OCI Marcom team, manage the development of creative assets, marketing collateral, promotional videos, and other relevant products.
Working with Strategic Programs and Workforce Planning and Talent Strategy teams, support the planning, design, development, and deployment of promotion of programs, partnership opportunities and strategic initiatives.
Engage, develop, and maintain strong networks with stakeholders in the automotive and mobility sector, including individual and corporate contacts, post-secondary institutions, research partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
Foster and identify partnership opportunities with industry to benefit OCI and the ventures we support including automotive and mobility industry organizations and government bodies.
Identify conferences, speaking, media, and publication opportunities to promote and address the needs of our stakeholders and promote the OVIN/OCI brand.
Keep abreast of industry and/or domain knowledge and activities, including current events, breakthroughs, trends, regulatory issues and key contacts and possess a solid understanding of the global industry to support thought leadership.
Provide regular updates to senior leadership, communicating opportunities and escalating risks when appropriate.
Interface and liaise with stakeholders; work cross-functionally across departments to assemble resources and ensure the successful delivery of projects

Other related duties as assigned, with occasional requirements to attend events outside of normal business hours, and occasional travel within Ontario.

Formal, specialized education (4-year university degree).

Client and stakeholder relationship management experience particularly working with senior level private and public sector representatives.
Process oriented, with superior operational experience.

Strong oral and written communication skills.

Consummate professional, able to represent the organization in all circumstances.

title: Director, Education Design & Intelligence
description:
Position Title:
Director, Education Design & Intelligence
Employment Type:
Full-Time Staff | Non-Union
Annual Salary Range:
$120,000 - $130,000
Division:
Education
Reports To:
Vice President, Education
Location:
2180 Yonge Street, Toronto, ON
TVO Media Education Group (
TVO
) is devoted to inspiring learning that changes lives and enriches communities. We are an internationally recognized digital learning organization that strives to engage, inform, and educate Ontarians of all ages.
Who we are
We are an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Education and a registered charity that contributes to learning, civic engagement, and public service media across Ontario. We provide free, trusted, and accessible educational content that can support Ontarians of all ages, regardless of background, location, or circumstance. To fulfill our mandate, TVO delivers curriculum-connected resources through TVO Learn and TVOkids, offers Ontario’s largest online high school through TVO ILC, and produces journalism, documentaries, current affairs programming, and podcasts with TVO Today that help Ontarians understand the issues shaping their communities.
What we’re looking for
TVO’s purpose is to inspire learning that changes lives and enriches communities. Our mission is to create engaging learning experiences for all through quality content, services, and technology. To realize our vision of becoming a globally recognized digital learning organization, we must continually reimagine how learning experiences are designed and delivered.
Artificial intelligence is reshaping education, from assessment and academic integrity to learner pathways, instructional practice, and support. These changes create extraordinary opportunities while raising important questions about equity, accessibility, ethics, and educational quality. TVO has an opportunity to help lead this transformation.
The Director, Education Design & Intelligence will shape how TVO responds. Working across TVOkids, TVO Learn, Mathify, TVO ILC, and emerging lifelong learning initiatives, this leader will guide TVO Education’s approach to AI, advance future-focused learning design, build staff capability, and ensure our learning experiences remain relevant, inclusive, and impactful. This is the opportunity to help TVO Education design what learning becomes next.
The Role
Reporting to the Vice President, Education, the Director, Education Design & Intelligence leads TVO’s Learning Experience Design and Production functions, with direct accountability for the Manager, Learning Experience Design and the Production Manager.
The Director works in close partnership with the Director, Curriculum & Course Production, Director, Content Engagement, and Director, Academic Services. Together, the Directors bring complementary expertise to the design and delivery of TVO’s education portfolio. The Director, Education Design & Intelligence contributes specialized leadership in learning design, AI integration, emerging technology, professional learning, and production.
Operating at the intersection of learning science, educational design, artificial intelligence, and digital innovation, the Director translates emerging developments into practical strategies, standards, and learning experiences that strengthen learner outcomes and organizational capability.
How you will make an impact
Learning Design, Pathways & Assessment
Lead the human-centred design and continuous improvement of learning experiences across TVO’s education portfolio, ensuring they are inclusive, accessible, pedagogically grounded, and responsive to changing learner needs.
Establish and maintain shared learning design principles, standards, and frameworks that guide how educational experiences are conceived, developed, evaluated, and improved across programs and platforms.
Work in close partnership with the Director, Curriculum & Course Production, Director, Content Engagement, and Director, Academic Services to strengthen learner journeys, pathways, engagement, and educational outcomes.
Lead the continuous review and modernization of assessment and evaluation practices across TVO Education, responding to developments in AI, academic integrity, learner evidence, and emerging approaches to teaching and learning.
Establish processes for regularly evaluating learning design standards, assessment approaches, and learner journeys, using research, learner feedback, outcomes data, prototyping, and testing to guide continuous improvement.
Examine how AI and emerging technologies are reshaping curriculum, instruction, assessment, learner supports, credentialing, and progression, and translate those developments into practical opportunities for TVO.
Embed collaborative design practices that centre diverse perspectives, lived experiences, accessibility, and learner needs.
AI Strategy, Emerging Technology & Professional Learning
Develop and lead TVO Education’s AI in Education strategy, guiding principles, and implementation roadmap.
Establish responsible, ethical, equitable, accessible, and learner-centred approaches to integrating AI into educational experiences, services, and internal workflows.
Work closely with the Vice President, Education, the Chief Technology Officer, and technology teams to align AI and educational priorities with platform development, system integration, technology roadmaps, data governance, privacy, and security requirements.
Identify, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, tools, platforms, and practices that can advance TVO’s educational mission and improve learning experiences.
Provide timely advice to Education leaders on the educational opportunities, risks, and implications of AI and other disruptive technologies.
Develop and implement a professional learning strategy that builds AI literacy, digital fluency, instructional capability, and confidence across the Education division.
Create learning experiences, communities of practice, guidance, and resources that help employees use emerging technologies effectively, critically, creatively, and responsibly.
Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning that enables teams to navigate educational and technological change.
Contribute expertise to the development of AI literacy and fluency initiatives for educators, learners, and families in collaboration with the Directors responsible for programming, content, and academic services.
Learning Experience Design & Production Leadership
Provide direct leadership and strategic direction to the Manager, Learning Experience Design and the Production Manager, developing a cohesive, high-performing, and multidisciplinary team.
Ensure Learning Experience Design and Production operate as an integrated, multifunctional team supporting programming priorities across the Education division.
Work with Directors and program teams to translate educational priorities into clear scopes, design approaches, production plans, and high-quality learner experiences.
Establish effective operating models, standards, processes, and workflows that support quality, consistency, accessibility, efficiency, innovation, and accountability.
Oversee the delivery of educational experiences and digital learning assets, ensuring work is completed to agreed standards, timelines, and program requirements.
Balance portfolio-wide priorities and deploy design and production capacity where it can create the greatest learner and organizational impact.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, creating clarity, encouraging collaboration, and building the capabilities needed for future-focused educational design and production.
Manage budgets, contracts, technology investments, and resources associated with Learning Experience Design and Production, and oversee allocated resources for professional learning and innovation initiatives in AI and emerging educational technology.
Cross-Portfolio Leadership, Collaboration & Sector Engagement
Serve as a fully integrated member of the Education leadership team, contributing to divisional strategy, planning, priority setting, and decision-making.
Work in close partnership with Directors across Education to ensure that learning design, AI, production, technology, and learner experience decisions support shared educational priorities.
Build strong working relationships across TVO so that educational design and AI initiatives are aligned with broader organizational, technology, research, communications, and operational directions.
Represent TVO in provincial, national, and international conversations about AI in Education, learning design, assessment, emerging technology, and the future of learning.
Develop relationships with educational institutions, researchers, government, technology organizations, and innovation networks that can contribute expertise, evidence, or capabilities to TVO’s work.
Identify and help advance appropriate opportunities for research, pilots, technology integration, and collaboration that support TVO’s educational priorities.
Bring emerging research, sector developments, and external perspectives into TVO to inform strategy, program design, professional learning, and continuous improvement.
Help position TVO as a trusted leader in the responsible, equitable, and educationally sound application of AI in publicly funded education.
What you will bring to TVO
Qualifications and Experience
Education
A postsecondary degree in Education, Educational Leadership, Learning Design, Educational Technology, Instructional Design, Digital Learning, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field is required. An equivalent combination of education and significant relevant leadership experience will be considered.
Formal training, research experience, or demonstrated expertise in AI and its applications in education is essential.
The Person
We are looking for a forward-thinking, intellectually curious, and collaborative leader who can help TVO navigate the future of learning. The successful candidate will be:
Current, practical expertise in AI in Education and a record of translating emerging developments into responsible implementation.
Strategic thinking that balances innovation with practical delivery.
Demonstrated expertise in learning design, assessment, learner success, and educational transformation.
The systems thinking required to navigate complex organizational, technological, and educational environments.
A collaborative approach to working across teams and disciplines and building trusted professional relationships.
A deep commitment to equity, inclusion, accessibility, and responsible innovation.
Energy for leading through change and helping shape the future of education.
A strong connection to TVO’s public mission and the transformative power of learning.
Leadership Experience
Significant leadership experience in educational design, educational technology, digital learning, AI in Education, innovation, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing AI or digital transformation strategies within educational or learning-focused organizations.

What we’re looking for
Learning can open doors and change lives. At TVO, we bring that belief to life through engaging content, services, and technology for learners across Ontario. As we work toward becoming a globally recognized digital learning organization, we need a leader who can turn bold ideas into strong, sustainable operations.
TVO Education supports learners at every stage. TVOkids sparks curiosity in young children and families. TVO Learn and Mathify support students and educators. TVO ILC creates pathways for secondary students and adult learners. Together, these programs form a powerful continuum of learning across Ontario.
Digital education is moving quickly, and so are we. Learner needs, technology, and expectations for impact continue to evolve. TVO Education needs smart, connected operations that help great programs thrive. This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic, entrepreneurial leader who enjoys making complex things work better. The Director, Education Operations will connect strategy, performance, finance, data, and accountability across TVO Education, building the operational engine that helps the portfolio adapt, grow, and deliver greater impact.
The Role
Reporting to the Vice President, Education and working alongside the Education Director team, the Director, Education Operations leads learner and customer experience, portfolio operations, business planning, financial stewardship, and data and analytics across TVO Education. The Director turns strategy into coordinated plans, strengthens performance intelligence, and collaborates with Growth on revenue diversification and sustainable growth. The role also supports the Vice President, Education in developing and stewarding strategic education partnerships and external relationships through operational insight, financial analysis, implementation planning, and performance measurement.
This role calls for an entrepreneurial mindset, strong business judgment, confidence with data, and a collaborative approach. Rather than managing education programs directly, the Director creates the systems, insight, and operating conditions that help the portfolio work smarter and deliver greater impact.
How you will make an impact
Portfolio Strategy, Planning & Performance
Develop and operationalize a multi-year portfolio strategy that connects TVO ILC, TVO Learn, Mathify, and TVOkids to TVO’s mission and long-term sustainability.
Work with the Vice President, Education and Education Director team to align business and operational planning with program priorities and the educational mission.
Collaborate with the Vice President, Growth and Growth team to assess revenue diversification, licensing, partnership, and earned-revenue opportunities, providing the analysis and business cases needed to inform decisions.
Connect Education priorities and operational requirements to TVO-wide growth, communications, marketing, technology, and data strategies.
Monitor changes in education policy, public funding, and digital learning, and assess the implications for TVO Education’s strategy and financial position.
Data, Impact & Accountability
Build and lead TVO Education’s performance intelligence function, establishing the governance, tools, and processes needed for reliable, actionable portfolio information.
Work with the Vice President, Education, the Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, and internal teams to develop accessible dashboards for learner outcomes, reach, engagement, completion, service quality, revenue, equity, and return on investment.

Lead impact measurement and reporting that meets Ministry, funder, and Board expectations and clearly communicates learner impact.
Work with Technology, Finance, Legal, and Research to strengthen data integration, access, and long-term sustainability.

Manage TVO Education’s portfolio-level operating budget, giving the Vice President, Education a clear view of performance, cost drivers, risks, commitments, and future resource needs.
Establish consistent service standards focused on learner and customer experience, accessibility, quality, and continuous improvement.
Lead annual and multi-year business planning, government reporting contributions, risk management, and strategic priority-setting within TVO’s broader planning cycle.

title: Executive Coordinator, Collections Care
description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement. As a globally recognized field research institute, ROM houses an impressive collection of over 18 million artworks, cultural objects, and natural history specimens, showcased in over 40 galleries and exhibition spaces. We are committed to creating a space where art, culture, and nature intersect, connecting people and communities to the past, present and shared future.
As we continue to work toward our goals to transform and evolve as one of the world’s foremost museums, we seek passionate and dynamic team members who embody our mission and values.
WHO WE NEED
We are seeking an Executive Coordinator, Collections Care to support the operational, administrative, financial, and project coordination needs of the Collections Care division. Reporting to the Chief, Collections Care, this role serves as a key operational partner, ensuring the department runs smoothly through executive support, budget administration, project coordination, and process improvement. The successful candidate will manage complex administrative activities, support strategic initiatives, coordinate departmental projects, and maintain effective communication across a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. This role is ideal for a highly organized professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys balancing executive support, financial administration, and project coordination responsibilities.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Provide executive-level administrative support to the Chief, Collections Care, including calendar management, meeting coordination, briefing materials, correspondence, and presentations
Coordinate departmental operations, procedures, and administrative processes to support efficiency and productivity across Collections Care
Manage departmental financial administration, including budgeting support, invoice processing, purchase orders, expenditure tracking, reconciliations, and financial reporting
Support the planning, coordination, and execution of Collections Care projects and strategic initiatives, including resource planning, procurement, scheduling, and reporting
Conduct research, environmental scans, stakeholder outreach, and data gathering to support departmental planning and decision-making
Prepare executive summaries, reports, presentations, and briefing materials for leadership and stakeholders
Coordinate departmental events, meetings, travel arrangements, onboarding activities, and professional memberships
Assist with grant, fellowship, and funding-related initiatives that support Collections Care objectives
Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders, handling sensitive and confidential matters with professionalism and discretion
WHAT YOU BRING
University degree, college diploma, or equivalent combination of education and experience in business administration, arts administration, museum studies, cultural management, or a related field
Minimum five (5) years of experience supporting senior leadership in an executive coordination, operations, administrative, or project coordination capacity
Demonstrated experience managing complex calendars, projects, competing priorities, and administrative processes
Experience supporting budgets, financial tracking, expenditure reporting, and procurement processes
Strong proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint
Experience using Power BI, Copilot, Adobe Acrobat, DocuSign, or similar business productivity tools
Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills
Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage confidential information with discretion
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, presentations, and executive correspondence
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders and navigate complex organizational environments
Experience supporting project coordination, process improvement, or strategic initiatives is an asset
French language proficiency is considered an asset
WHAT WE OFFER
Comprehensive benefits coverage:
For permanent and full-time contract positions (conditions apply), enjoy paid benefits for individuals and families, a health spending account, and an Employee Assistance Program.
Worry-free retirement savings:
With our pension plan, you benefit from an employer-matched Defined Benefit contribution plan, which provides predictable lifetime retirement income, survivor benefits, and early retirement options without the stress of investment decisions.
Support for new parents:
Enjoy a parental leave top-up to 95 percent of your salary for 17 weeks, helping you balance work and family life.
Perks:
Free ROM membership for permanent full-time and part-time staff, plus discounts to over 200 attractions through Attractions Ontario.
And more!
SALARY & TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT
START DATE: November 2026
OPEN DATE: October 7, 2026
CLOSE DATE: Open until filled
STATUS: Full-time, permanent
EMPLOYEE GROUP: Non-Union
EXPECTED COMPENSATION: Salary: $74,419 - $87,552
SCHEDULE: 35 hours weekly
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Six (6) months
LOCATION (onsite): Toronto, ON
WHAT TO EXPECT IN OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS
Application & initial screening:
Apply online. Selected individuals will be invited to complete a pre-recorded video questionnaire to tell us more about your interest in ROM, your team leadership, operations support, and customer service experience, and the impact you could make as part of our Visitor Experience team.
First interview:
A 1-hour in-person interview with the Hiring team. This in-depth interview will focus on your skills and how they align with the team's and ROM's needs.
Second interview:
A 1-hour in-person meeting with the hiring team. You may be asked to present a pre-assigned case study and discuss scenarios relevant to your role. Depending on the position, you might also receive a tour of ROM and a preview of your responsibilities and interactions.
The above-listed process may change or vary based on the nature and scope of the position.
WHY PEOPLE CHOOSE ROM
Cultural engagement:
Daily interactions with Toronto's diverse culture and international visitors offer insights into social and cultural trends. We champion inclusive community programs and connections through diverse experiences.
Continuous learning:
At ROM, expertise and continuous skill development are paramount. Our culture of curiosity and open-mindedness fosters growth beyond traditional career paths.
Passion & fulfillment:
Our work in preserving and curating cultural narratives brings deep satisfaction. We are passionate about the arts, global history, cultural diversity, and leveraging digital technologies to enhance accessibility.
Team & culture:
ROM promotes a positive workplace with collaborative, supportive teams that encourage creativity and innovation. We value new ideas and collective problem-solving.
Academic collaboration:
We are committed to education, partnering with universities and providing student resources, underscoring our dedication to research and accessibility.
If you’re excited about this role, even if your experience differs from the specific requirements, we encourage you to apply. We’re keen to meet candidates who can contribute their talents to our goals, and will consider an equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, education, and experience.
COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, INCLUSION, & ACCESSIBILITY
At ROM, we embrace diversity in our exhibits, communities, and teams. We encourage applications from racialized persons, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, and those who can further diversify our ideas. We are committed to equitable employment opportunities and a workplace free from discrimination and harassment.
We welcome and accommodate candidates with disabilities throughout the selection process. Please contact us at careers@rom.on.ca for assistance.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
ROM does not require “Canadian experience.” International applicants with equivalent experience are encouraged to apply.
ROM uses technology-assisted tools (including JazzHR TalentFit) to support the review and screening of applications. All hiring decisions are made by human reviewers.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
APPLY NOW
Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please note that all candidates receiving a verbal job offer will be subject to a background check. This includes a criminal background check and verification of professional references, and, other checks depending on the role.

description:
WHO WE ARE
Opened in 1914 and welcoming over 1.3 million visitors annually, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM) is Canada's most-visited museum. At ROM, we are dedicated to building and sharing global collections, sharing knowledge, inspiring learning, and fostering community engagement.
