title: Supervisor, Traffic Planning
description:
Req ID: 28597
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/16/2026
Job Summary
Reporting to the Executive Manager of Development Engineering & Construction, the Supervisor of Traffic Planning leads a team of technical and professional staff in the review of development and permit applications, realty related requests and other roadway planning matters from a traffic planning perspective, including traffic impact studies, access modification permits, site plans, and pedestrian and vehicular circulation plans, while ensuring that best practices are followed and the City’s interests and objectives are maintained.
Duties and Responsibilities
Talent Management:
Provides strategic vision, leadership, direction, professional/technical guidance, coaching and mentorship to the Traffic Planning team members;
Manages and develops the performance of direct reports including recruitment, development of annual work plans, goals and objectives for each team member, and ensuring quality and production of each individual's work;
On-boards and trains new staff;
Follows/tracks trends/changes regarding industry best practices and applicable regulatory regimes, forecasts pressures, and prepares business cases for resources as required; and,
Oversees, directs and ensures the successful delivery of the Traffic Planning team's duties, responsibilities and workplan deliverables.
Ensuring Compliance:
Oversees and provides technical leadership to ensure the team’s review of the development applications, permits and realty request comply with guidelines, industry best practices, engineering standards, the City's Official Plan, the Planning Act and its regulations;
Leads studies to update City guidelines, Zoning regulations, and other matters; and,
Ensures the traffic planning process remains up to date by developing, implementing and continuously improving the team’s programs, processes, guidelines and standards.
Providing Expertise:
Regularly attends Planning and Development Committee meetings as a panelist to represent the Planning & Building Department and to provide expertise to the Committee on traffic planning matters;
Attends meetings with local Councillors, community members, the general public, outside agencies and other external and internal stakeholders as required to represent the City’s traffic planning interests, respond to questions and provide expertise;
Leads workshops with inter/intra-departmental colleagues to develop solutions to new problems or conflicts related to the creation of new municipal roadways through the land development process; and,
Manages the review of very large and/or complex development applications.
Monitoring and Reporting:
Provides expertise and support related to road corridor and access management that include the authoring of corporate reports to the Leadership Team and Committees of Council;
Ensures coordinated and consistent reporting of issues and communications at all levels; and,
Oversees the procurement and management of professional consulting services led by the team for the completion of traffic/transportation related studies.
Skills and Qualifications
Education and Experience:
Post-secondary graduate from a recognized institution with a degree in Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering or a related engineering or applied science program, or an equivalent combination of post-secondary education, qualifications and experience relevant to the role;
Professional engineering certification (P.Eng. or applicable Limited Engineering Licence) in good standing with Professional Engineers Ontario is preferred;
Minimum 8 years related experience with at least 3 years in a leadership role;
Demonstrated project management experience; and,
Municipal experience is considered to be an asset.
Knowledge and Expertise:
In-depth knowledge of traffic planning and traffic engineering principles, practices, guidelines and regulations;
Broad knowledge of the municipal land development process, including the Planning Act, the City's Official Plan, and the nuances of the various types of development applications; and
Understanding of key principles traffic modelling, traffic safety, traffic control, roadway corridor management, active transportation, transportation demand management, roadway geometric design, capital planning, and other related disciplines.
Competencies and Skills:
Demonstrated leadership skills and ability to provide guidance and direction to staff while motivating and fostering a strong team;
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the demonstrated ability to deliver presentations to technical and non-technical audiences;
Strong interpersonal, negotiation and collaboration skills, with a demonstrated ability to develop and foster effective working relationships;
Demonstrated tact and diplomacy when dealing with the public and elected officials;
Effective decision making and problem solving skills with the ability to determine an effective course of action that drives progression;
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing tasks;
Demonstrated competency in leadership, accountability, customer service, continuous improvement and City's core values - trust, quality and excellence; and,
Ability to provide self-transportation options to meetings and project sites within Mississauga and Peel.

•    Perform regular peak hour studies and observations;

•    Previous co-op experience related to “Transportation Engineering Technology” would be an asset;

title: Municipal by-Law Enforcement Officer
description:
Req ID: 28634
Vacancy Type: Combination
Contract Duration: Various

Job Summary
Responsible for enforcement of City by-laws by interpreting the by-laws and communicating these to the general public.
Duties and Responsibilities
The Specialized Housing Enforcement (SHE) Unit administers and enforces a range of municipal by-laws, licensing requirements, and regulatory standards governing City-regulated housing accommodations. The team conducts inspections, investigations, public education, and enforcement activities related to apartment buildings, short-term rentals, additional residential units, lodging houses, and other regulated housing uses to ensure compliance and support safe housing conditions for residents. Bylaws enforced include, but are not limited to the Rental Apartment Buildings By-law, the Property Standards By-law, and the Short-Term Rental Accommodation Licensing By-law.
To be considered, candidates must meet and maintain the following requirements:
Interpret and apply municipal by-laws, legislation, policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.
Investigate complaints, collect evidence, and perform follow-up inspections and investigations to achieve and maintain compliance.
Conduct inspections and investigations to determine compliance and identify contraventions.
Resolve compliance issues through education, voluntary compliance, and enforcement. Where necessary, take legal action in order to bring violators into conformity/compliance, providing professional testimony and evidence for court and tribunal hearings
Prepare and maintain accurate inspection records, correspondence, reports, notices, orders, and prosecution briefs.
Initiate legal proceedings where necessary and present evidence before courts and tribunals.
Participate in joint enforcement operations with police and other enforcement agencies.
Provide information and education to residents, businesses, City staff, elected officials, and industry stakeholders.
Review by-laws, operational policies and procedures, and recommend amendments, changes, etc.
Adhere to a strict code of confidentiality, incidental to all investigations.
SHE is one of 3 by-law enforcement Units, the others being Property Standards, Investigations, and Enforcement (PSIE), and By-law, Compliance, and Enforcement (BCE), who deal primarily with private property investigations and licensing/nuisance bylaws, respectively.
Perform other duties as assigned.
NOTE
: This position will require the successful candidates to work various shifts, which include days, evenings, overnight, weekends and statutory holidays and, at times, will require overtime. This position may involve operating a City fleet vehicle and wearing of a City-issued uniform. A Vulnerable Sector Check (Level 3) will be required of all successful candidates, at their own expense, to verify the absence of a criminal record for which a pardon has not been granted. There may be a written test conducted as part of the interview process. Successful candidates for this Municipal By-law Enforcement Officer (MBEO) competition may be considered for other MBEO positions, including PSIE and BCE, based on operational needs.
Skills and Qualifications
Municipal Law Enforcement Officer certification (may be obtained upon hiring)
Certification from the Ontario Association of Property Standards Officers (preferred; may be obtained upon hiring)
Graduate of a recognized community college in discipline of law enforcement, security administration, criminal justice studies or a by-law related course/major.
3-5 years working experience in related disciplines
Excellent communication, interpersonal and conflict-resolution skills
Strong organization and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Experience with Microsoft Office programs and appropriate City software.
Site visits where there is considerable debris to manoeuvre around. May require some lifting of objects. Detailed visual inspections.
Ability to work primarily in the field operating a vehicle to conduct inspections and general patrols, along with general office duty
Must hold a valid Driver's Licence

TRANSIT ENFORCEMENT OFFICER
or

Operating in control room; entering/maintaining/collecting information, conducting radio checks frequently

Flexible to work a variety of shifts  up to 12 hours including days, afternoons, evenings and weekends, holidays, and may involve working alone

•    Review, reorganize, and maintain files and folders; identify outdated, duplicate, or misplaced content; and recommend practical improvements to document management.
•    Embed and organize Power BI reports and dashboards in SharePoint so operational and performance information is easy to find and use.

•    Support reports, dashboards, standard operating procedures, work instructions, templates, and other process documentation.

•    Perform other related duties in support of the Facilities Maintenance team as assigned.

title: Supervisor, Forestry Maintenance & Operations
description:
Req ID: 28549
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/12/2026
Job Summary
Are you passionate about trees and leadership in a forward-thinking non-unionized workplace with an amazing team culture that puts our people and their safety first and is committed to quality work? Are you someone who challenges the status quo, gets things done, sees the big picture, and inspires others?
As one of our Supervisors, Forestry Maintenance & Operations, you will lead an award-winning team of arborists and forestry technicians that deliver tree care services safely and efficiently on streets, parks, and natural areas across one of Canada’s largest cities. From managing in-house crews to contractors, and from proactive maintenance to emergency storm response, this is far from your traditional municipal operations role. You will lead by example and bring an execution-focused and delivery-driven mindset to achieving operational excellence in ensuring public safety and a healthy and resilient urban forest. You will report to the Manager, Forestry Maintenance & Operations and work alongside another Supervisor and three Forestry Coordinators that help facilitate day-to-day operations with our contractors and in-house crews.
Your pay will negotiated based on your experience, abilities, and qualifications, and your benefits and perks will include access to a defined benefit pension plan (OMERS), competitive paid vacation, and a comprehensive employer-paid benefits plan that includes extended health, dental and life insurance, and access to a 24/7 Employee and Family Assistance Program. You will join our on-call supervisor rotation and provide overtime support during extreme weather and storms. All emergency and overtime hours are fully compensated.
Duties and Responsibilities
Supervise the planning and delivery of arboricultural and boulevard vegetation management services within an assigned area in a safe, efficient, and effective manner.
Supervise the planning, coordination, scheduling and supervision of contractors, personnel, equipment, supplies, materials within an assigned area to ensure the most efficient and effective use of in-house and contracted resources.
Sets operational priorities and objectives within an assigned area, including milestones, timelines, and performance measures.
Supervise the planning, development, tendering, and administration of contracts within an assigned area.
Supervise emergency response and preparedness for extreme weather events and critical incidents impacting forestry assets in an assigned area. Acting as Incident Commander and leading incident response teams.
Supervise, motivate, mentor, and train assigned staff, including recruitment and hiring, scheduling, assigning, and reviewing of work. Authorizes and coordinates standby, overtime, and leave requests.
Determines staff training and development needs, monitors and evaluate staff performance, providing coaching, performance management, and taking disciplinary action when necessary.
Provides input and administers the annual operating and capital budget for an assigned area, and ensures that the expenditures are controlled and maintained within approved budget.
Develops and implements operational plans, policies, procedures, service standards, service level agreements.
Evaluates operational effectiveness and efficiency, monitors performance, and fosters a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Ensures the timely delivery of quality customer service and resolutions to service requests, complaints, and inquiries from the public, elected officials, or other City staff.
Develops, prepares, and submits correspondence, reports, briefing notes, memoranda, and presentations for leadership and Council.
Cultivates effective working relationships with internal and external partners, including members of Council and their staff, other departments, divisions, and sections, and members of the public.
Represents the Division at public meetings, committees of Council, inter-divisional, and inter-departmental meetings.
Leads, participates and/or contributes to working groups, committees, task forces, and project teams.
Develops and fosters a strong culture of health and safety and ensures compliance with all applicable health and safety legislation and policies (i.e. Occupational Health and Safety Act).
Ensures quality of work and services meets legislated, corporate, departmental, divisional, and section standards.
Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary degree or diploma, or an approved equivalent, in urban forestry, arboriculture, ecology, environmental science, or related discipline.
Must be a Certified Arborist with the International Society of Arboriculture (ISA) and possess the Tree Risk Assessment Qualification.
ISA Certified Urban Forest Professional or ISA Board Certified Master Arborist considered an asset.
Must have a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in urban forestry.
Must have extensive knowledge of urban forestry and arboriculture principles and practices.
Extensive experience with tree maintenance operations and/or boulevard vegetation management in streets, parks, and City property by in-house staff and contractors.
Demonstrated experience overseeing projects, crews and/or contractors (this might include developing procurement documents, budget control, meeting deadlines and deliverables, quality control, working with/on project teams and working groups, and/or planning and coordinating complex arboricultural operations and tasks).
Demonstrated interpersonal and leadership skills to provide direction to staff and/or contractors.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to interact with residents, stakeholders and elected officials effectively;
Sound knowledge of applicable legislation, regulations, policies, and standards (i.e. Occupational Health and Safety Act, Municipal Act).
Must be able to work flexible hours including evenings and weekends and participate in the Forestry On Call program.
Must hold a valid Ontario Class G Driver’s License or higher with an acceptable driving record.
Must be willing to obtain and provide a current driver's abstract at your own expense.
Must be able to work in all weather conditions, on uneven terrain, and perform heavy lifting.

title: Deputy City Solicitor, Planning, Development & Real Estate Law
description:
Req ID: 28657
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/12/2026
Job Summary
Reporting to the Director, Legal Services and serving as a member of the Legal Services Management Team, the Deputy City Solicitor provides leadership to the Real Estate, Planning & Development Law Section and oversees the delivery of legal services in support of the City's growth, development and strategic priorities.
This position combines people leadership, legal expertise and strategic business leadership. The successful candidate will lead a team of lawyers, law clerks and legal assistants, fostering a collaborative, respectful and high-performing culture while ensuring the delivery of timely, practical and risk-informed legal advice. The Deputy City Solicitor is a trusted advisor who builds strong relationships across the corporation, provides strategic counsel to senior leaders and Council, and supports the ongoing development of a modern, client-focused legal practice. The role requires strong judgment, political acuity, exceptional interpersonal skills and a demonstrated commitment to mentoring and developing people.
Duties and Responsibilities
Leadership and People Management
Lead, mentor and support a team of lawyers, law clerks and legal assistants, creating an inclusive, respectful and high-performing work environment.
Foster employee engagement, accountability, collaboration and professional growth through coaching, mentoring and open communication.
Promote employee well-being and a positive, respectful and high-performing workplace culture that reflects the City's values and strategic priorities.
Manage workload distribution and resources to ensure effective service delivery while supporting employee development and success.
Strategic and Operational Leadership
Participate as a member of the Legal Services Management Team and contribute to the strategic direction, business planning and operational leadership of the division.
Support modernization initiatives, process improvements and the adoption of technologies that enhance legal service delivery.
Monitor service levels, operational priorities and emerging risks to ensure responsive and effective client service.
Contribute to budget planning and the oversight of external legal service expenditures.
Support divisional and corporate initiatives requiring legal leadership and strategic advice.
Legal Services and Client Advisory
Maintain a portfolio of complex legal matters while providing strategic oversight of significant planning, development, real estate and Ontario Land Tribunal matters.
Provide strategic legal advice and representation on planning, development, real estate and growth-related matters, including major development applications, development agreements, land transactions and Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings.
Advise senior leadership, Council and City staff on matters involving legal, operational, financial and reputational risk.
Retain and direct external counsel where appropriate.
Prepare reports and opinions for Council and Committees and attend meetings as required.
Represent the City in negotiations, mediations, hearings and other proceedings as required.
Relationship Building and Collaboration
Build and maintain strong working relationships with City departments, senior leadership, Council, external partners and industry stakeholders.
Represent Legal Services on corporate initiatives, working groups and strategic projects.
Communicate complex legal issues to diverse audiences in a clear, practical and accessible manner.
Skills and Qualifications
LL.B. or J.D. and membership in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario.
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible legal experience, including significant experience in planning, development and real estate law within a municipal or public sector environment.
Demonstrated experience leading, developing and managing professional teams in a complex, client-service-driven organization.
Proven ability to build and sustain a positive, inclusive and high-performing team culture through effective leadership, coaching and mentoring.
Exceptional interpersonal, communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility and influence with staff, senior leaders, elected officials, clients and external stakeholders.
Strong political acuity, organizational awareness and judgment in managing sensitive, complex and high-profile matters.
Strategic and solutions-oriented mindset, with the ability to balance legal risk, operational realities, business objectives and client service expectations.
Thorough knowledge of municipal planning, development and real estate law, including development approvals, development agreements, land transactions and growth-related matters affecting Ontario municipalities.
Demonstrated experience negotiating, drafting and advising on complex planning, development and real estate agreements.
Significant experience providing strategic legal advice on major development applications, planning matters and growth-related initiatives.
Experience appearing before administrative tribunals, including the Ontario Land Tribunal, and directing complex litigation and external counsel.

title: Technologist, Building Services
description:
Req ID: 28656
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/22/2026
Job Summary
This role reviews applications for building permits to confirm all building applications accepted and issued comply with the Ontario Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, “applicable law” and are processed in accordance with the standards and requirements established in the Building By-law.  Accurately assess each proposal to determine applicable fees and charges and determine appropriate construction values.
Duties and Responsibilities
Review & Assessment
•    Review and assess building permit application submissions in accordance with the Ontario Building Code Act, Building By-law , as well as other applicable law, department policies and procedures.
•    Review building permit applications to determine necessary approvals in accordance with applicable legislation and ensure compliance has been achieved prior to permit issuance.
•    Review and assess requests for conditional permits to determine eligibility and provide recommendations for management approval
•    Process building permit applications, including the review of documents, drawings and specifications for limited scope building permit applications to ensure compliance with the Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, Building By-law, municipal by-laws and other applicable legislation as part of our express review services. Liaise with inspections staff to resolve design and construction issues and provide permit status
•    Coordinates and monitors approval process for projects subject to site plan approval and other applicable planning approvals.
•    Monitor application timelines to ensure compliance with prescribed timelines in the Ontario Building Code Act and take corrective action as necessary
Interpretation
•    Accurately interpret and apply the Ontario Building Code Act, Ontario Building Code, Building by-law and other applicable legislation.
•    Interpret the Building Code Act, Building By-law and other applicable legislation as defined, to determine applicable fees and charges
•    Performs research for and prepares technical reports as required or requested
•    Accurately provide professional advice on building permit applications and associated processes
Data Entry & Record Keeping
•    Compile and maintain accurate records and associated documentation in accordance with established internal controls, protocols and legislation.
•    The accurate documentation is required in order to mitigate financial, reputation risks, and legal challenges.
•    Daily use of MAX, SharePoint, SAP and ePlans.
Customer Service
•    Act as the principal point of contact throughout the building permit approval process for the public, applicants, City staff and external agencies.
•    Provide guidance and direction to applicants and internal stakeholders regarding building permit applications and associated approvals. Assists applicants in the coordination and expedition of building permit applications to ensure overall customer satisfaction.
•    Assists applicants in the facilitation of building permit issuance in compliance with prescribed timelines
•    Proactively build and maintain relationships with clients, able to provide clear, timely and transparent communication of information to facilitate timely building application approvals.
Meetings
•    Attend meetings to discuss and provide advice regarding building permissions, approvals applicable legislation and associated processes. Conduct preliminary meetings and consultations advising applicants of the required approvals, documents, specifications and drawings required to facilitate building permit issuance and provide direction as to the necessary procedures and protocols.
Skills and Qualifications
•    Undergraduate Degree or Community College Diploma in one or more of the following areas: Architecture, Engineering or related discipline
•    Registered Building Official with the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MMAH)
•    Qualification in the following categories as defined under  Part 3, Division C of the Ontario Building Code from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MMAH) in the following categories: House, Small Buildings, General Legal Process, HVAC-House, Plumbing-House.  Qualification in additional categories would be considered an asset.
•    Eligibility for and willingness to obtain and maintain the Certified Building Code Official (CBCO) designation from the Ontario Building Officials Association (OBOA)
•    Thorough knowledge of the Building Code Act and Ontario Building Code
•    Working knowledge of Construction Regulations and Occupational Health and Safety Act
•    Working knowledge of the following principles and standards: building design and construction principles; building construction methods, building industry issues, trends and best practices.
•    Minimum of five years of related work experience reviewing and interpreting architectural drawings and policy documents or equivalent combination of education and experience
•    Knowledge of building and development application processes and associated legislation is highly preferred
•    Proficient in reading and interpreting drawings, specifications and other technical documents
•    Excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal skills to effectively deal with the general public, consultants, developers, staff and others stakeholders within the building approvals process.
•    The ability to effectively communicate technical information to a non-technical audience is required
•    Well-developed analytical, research, organizational, negotiation and problem solving skills
•    Strong computer literacy is required with experience using MS Office and Adobe Acrobat; experience with Mississauga Approvals Express (MAX), EDMS, SharePoint, electronic plans submission (ePlans) or other permitting software is considered a strong asset
•    Must be flexible in adapting to rapidly changing workloads and work environments

title: Asset Management Specialist - Enforcement
description:
Req ID: 28636
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 2
Closing Date: 10/28/2026
Job Summary
The Asset Management Specialist leads the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the Enforcement Division’s asset management program, supporting a diverse portfolio of vehicles, technology, communications equipment, uniforms and specialized operational assets across eight regulatory and enforcement service areas.
The role provides strategic and operational leadership through the development of asset strategies, lifecycle and investment plans, governance frameworks, performance measures and business processes that support operational readiness, sustainability, accountability and effective resource allocation. Working collaboratively across corporate and operational teams, the Specialist provides subject matter expertise, oversees asset management systems and data, and leads initiatives that optimize asset performance and support front-line service delivery.
Duties and Responsibilities
Lead the Division’s asset management program, including the development and implementation of strategies, policies, governance frameworks, standards, controls and performance measures.
Establish and maintain consistent processes governing asset planning, acquisition, deployment, utilization, maintenance, replacement, transfer and disposal to support effective life cycle management and accountability.
Develop lifecycle plans, replacement forecasts, multi-year asset plans, budget forecasts, business cases and funding recommendations to support long-term investment and resource allocation decisions.
Assess asset condition, utilization, criticality, risk, and lifecycle requirements to identify investment priorities, optimization opportunities, funding gaps and future asset needs.
Lead procurement planning and acquisition strategies, including requirements development, specification preparation, evaluations, contract administration, vendor management and warranty oversight.
Implement and oversee asset management systems, inventories and registries to ensure accurate asset data, effective tracking, lifecycle accountability and audit readiness.
Evaluate and optimize asset management technologies and related business processes to enhance asset visibility, system effectiveness and operational efficiency.
Develop dashboards, performance measures and management reports and analyze financial, utilization, inventory and lifecycle data to identify trends, risks and opportunities for optimization and continuous improvement.
Conduct audits, reconciliations, risk assessments and benchmarking activities to strengthen governance, optimize asset performance and support informed decision-making.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations regarding asset investment, governance, procurement, lifecycle planning, operational risk and resource allocation.
Lead stakeholder engagement, consultation and requirements gathering with Fleet Services, Finance, Procurement, IT, Materiel Management and operational partners to support coordinated asset planning and stewardship.
Lead cross-functional initiatives and represent the Division on corporate committees, working groups and enterprise projects to advance asset management objectives and operational effectiveness.
Coordinate operational asset stewardship activities, including vehicles, inventories, assignments, transfers, recoveries, replenishment and compliance monitoring.
Ensure governance, funding, procurement, training, tracking and life cycle controls are established to support the successful introduction of new programs, services, technologies and operational assets.
Performing other duties, responsibilities and special projects as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Business Administration, Public Administration, Asset Management, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Operations Management, Information Technology, or related discipline.
Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in asset management, program development, inventory management governance, fleet coordination, logistics, operational resource management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing asset management policies, governance frameworks, lifecycle strategies, internal controls, performance measures and continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated experience providing governance, planning or analytical support for a large, high-value and operationally diverse asset portfolio.
Experience conducting strategic planning, risk analysis, lifecycle forecasting, state-of-good repair reviews, inventory management, asset optimization, budget development and business case preparation.
Demonstrated ability to assess financial exposure, operational consequences and organizational risk and translate complex findings into practical strategies, controls and recommendations.
Experience administering or providing functional oversight of corporate or enterprise assets, inventory, fleet or technology-management systems, such as SAP, fleet management information systems, IT asset-tracking tools or equivalent platforms.
Demonstrated knowledge of data governance, asset registries, audit controls, performance measurement, management reporting and asset lifecycle data.
Strong research, policy development, analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to interpret corporate policies, operational requirements, technical information and industry best practices and develop appropriate divisional standards, procedures and processes.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint, with the ability to analyze complex data, develop dashboards, prepare professional reports, presentations and business cases.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information and present recommendations to management and stakeholders.
Strong interpersonal, consultation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes and establish effective working relationships across multiple business areas.
Demonstrated project management and change management skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives involving competing priorities, multiple stakeholders and complex operational requirements.
Ability to exercise independent judgement, manage sensitive information and work with minimal supervision in a complex, high-accountability environment.
Knowledge of municipal procurement, inventory management, fleet operations, and asset optimization and management best practices is considered an asset.
Knowledge of LEAN principles and continuous improvement methodologies is considered an asset.
Certification in Asset Management, Supply Chain Management, Project Management or a related discipline is considered an asset.
Valid Ontario Class G Driver’s Licence.

description:
Req ID: 28471
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 3
Closing Date: 10/16/2026
Job Summary
MiWay is seeking experienced and motivated leaders to supervise the day-to-day maintenance of transit buses and non revenue fleet vehicles.
Reporting to the Assistant Manager, Transit Maintenance, the Supervisor is responsible for leading skilled trades staff in a unionized, safety critical environment to ensure vehicles are safe, compliant, and ready for service. This position plays a key role in supporting daily service delivery, fleet availability, and MiWay’s commitment to safety, reliability, and customer service.
Guided by a forward thinking strategic plan, MiWay’s vision is to be a transit system that makes Mississauga proud by providing a safe, reliable, and efficient transit system built on strong traditions of safety, service, and courtesy.
Why Work for MiWay
Full time, permanent employment
Competitive salary
Annual performance and economic adjustment reviews
Career advancement opportunities
Four (4) weeks of paid vacation
Comprehensive benefits package
OMERS pension plan
Overtime premiums
Skilled trades premiums - $1.75/hour
Afternoon shift premiums - $2.00/hour
Overnight shift premiums - $2.75/hour
And more.
Note
: This position requires a valid 310T Truck and Coach certificate and flexibility to work different hours, shifts, and days off to be considered.
Duties and Responsibilities
Under the direction of the Assistant Manager, Transit Maintenance, the successful candidate will:
Supervise the day to day activities of Transit Maintenance staff to ensure the safe, efficient, and timely inspection, repair, cleaning, and servicing of transit buses and non revenue fleet vehicles.
Assign work, allocate personnel and equipment, and adjust priorities to support daily fleet availability and service requirements.
Schedule maintenance activities and prepare work orders using a computerized maintenance management system.
Ensure all maintenance work complies with Ministry of Transportation legislation, applicable safety regulations, manufacturer specifications, and MiWay policies and procedures.
Provide front line leadership by setting clear performance expectations, monitoring work quality, and supporting staff through coaching and feedback.
Manage staffing requirements, attendance, overtime, and shift coverage in accordance with operational needs and collective agreements.
Work collaboratively with management, Human Resources, and union representatives to address employee relations matters and support effective labour relations.
Respond to service impacting failures, road calls, incidents, and urgent maintenance issues as required.
Ensure staff are properly instructed in safe work practices, approved methods, procedures, and performance standards.
Support the onboarding, orientation, and ongoing development of MiWay  Maintenance staff.
Support and, when required, supervise the operation of bus wash area, fueling stations, and bus cleaning activities.
Monitor and manage records including absences, overtime, incident reports, and operational data.
Assist with identifying warranty issues, tagging defective components, and ensuring warranty claims and supplier commitments are upheld.
Ensure tools, parts, materials, and cores are properly handled, stored, returned, or disposed of in accordance with procedures.
Conduct technical investigations, inspections, and procedural or quality audits as required.
Promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace that is free from harassment and discrimination.
Support MiWay’s commitments under the Ontario Human Rights Code (OHRC), the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, and related corporate policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Skills and Qualifications
Minimum grade 12 - Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD) or verified equivalent, is considered an asset.
Valid 310T - Truck and Coach Technician Certificate of Qualification, issued by Skilled Trades Ontario and maintained in good standing.
A minimum of five (5) years of experience as a Journeyperson following attainment of trade certification, with exposure to the full range of transit bus maintenance activities or an equivalent combination of education / certifications and experience.
Three (3) years of progressive experience demonstrating leadership responsibility, including supervision or acting supervisory duties is preferred.
A valid 310S Automotive Service Technician Certificate of Qualification, issued by Skilled Trades Ontario, is considered an asset.
Valid Ontario Class G Driver’s Licence with an acceptable driving abstract; a Class C licence with Z endorsement is preferred.
Ability to work various shifts including days, afternoons, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays.
Strong working knowledge of heavy vehicle maintenance, diagnostics, and manufacturer specifications.
Knowledge of shop management practices, preventative maintenance programs, and applicable OHSA, MTO, MOL, and MOE legislative requirements.
Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and support employees in a unionized environment, with a focus on safety, collaboration, consistency, and respectful workplace practices.
Strong interpersonal, organizational, and written and verbal communication skills.
Experience or exposure to battery electric buses or alternative propulsion technologies is considered an asset.

description:

Job Summary
The City of Mississauga is seeking an experienced Application Developer to support the modernization of the Property Tax Management system. The successful candidate will design, build, test, deploy, and support cloud-native web applications that replace legacy Oracle Forms and reports. We are looking for a pragmatic application developer who can translate complex taxation workflows, legacy PL/SQL logic, forms, and reports into maintainable digital products. The candidate should be comfortable working across frontends, backend, data, integration, security, and DevOps. You collaborate effectively with business analysts, architects, database specialists, security teams, infrastructure teams, vendors, and municipal partners, and you can balance modernization goals with business continuity and data integrity.
The role operates in a hybrid work environment, with office presence required at Mississauga City Hall, 300 City Centre Drive, Mississauga.
Duties and Responsibilities
The Successful Candidate will:
Develop accessible, responsive web interfaces using TypeScript and a modern frontend framework such as React or Angular.
Develop and maintain Java services, APIs, business rules, integrations, and batch-processing components supporting property-tax workflows.
Build reusable front-end components and RESTful APIs that follow API-first, modular and testable design principles.
Develop containerized services on Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate, using Amazon S3 and DynamoDB for state management and asynchronous job processing
Design and implement RESTful APIs and reusable services that integrate frontend applications, workflow orchestration, databases, reporting components, and external systems.
Implement asynchronous and scheduled processing for reports, calculations, file generation, data transformation, and other long-running jobs.
Build batch, scheduled-report and event-driven workflows using AWS Step Functions and container-based job processing.
Create and maintain automated unit, integration, API, end-to-end, regression, performance, and security tests.
Participate in the progressive migration of forms and reports while supporting coexistence between the modern AWS platform and the legacy environment.
Apply role-based access control using Azure AD federation, AWS Cognito, JWT claims, and application-level authorization.
Contribute to DevOps CI/CD pipelines, including static application security testing (SAST), code coverage, and pull-request review workflows.
Protect data and secrets through TLS, encryption at rest, least-privilege IAM roles, AWS KMS, and AWS Secrets Manager.
Investigate and resolve application defects, failed workflows, performance issues, integration errors, and production incidents.
Produce technical designs, interface specifications, data mappings, runbooks, deployment instructions, test evidence, and support documentation.
Estimate development effort, identify delivery risks, and contribute to sprint planning, backlog refinement, release planning, and technical governance.
Follow the City’s SDLC and AI-SDLC standards: author specifications and steering files, review all AI-generated output, and stay accountable for submitted code.
Provide operational support, knowledge transfer, and continuous enhancement for TXM applications and services.
Skills and Qualifications
Post-secondary degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
Minimum 3-5 years of experience developing enterprise applications.
Experience developing applications using Java and object-oriented programming principles.
Experience with modern JavaScript/TypeScript development frameworks such as React, Angular, or Vue.
Experience developing and integrating RESTful APIs and web services.
Experience with AWS services like ECS Fargate, S3, Aurora DB, ALB, Cloudfront etc.
Experience with relational databases and SQL preferably Postgre SQL.
Experience with cloud-based application development (AWS preferred).
Experience with source control, automated testing, and CI/CD practices.
Knowledge of application security principles and secure coding practices.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.

Job Summary
As the City of Mississauga intensifies, planning for, delivering parkland, and protecting City parkland assets becomes increasingly challenging and essential as we strive to create healthy complete communities.
The Parks Assets, Urban Design team consists of both planners and landscape architects who work together to plan parks, expand the City's parkland and greenlands, protect park assets; and comment on development applications, and City parkland matters.
Under the direction of the Lead Parkland Planner, the successful applicant will be responsible for representing the departmental interests on development applications and realty matters which include license/easement agreements, parkland acquisition, as well as parkland planning studies and other technical studies. This position will require the ability to resolve issues within a fast paced environment, manage several projects at one time, have a full breadth of knowledge of the planning process, comment on legal agreements, and have excellent public communication skills.

Reporting to the Manager of Urban Design, the successful candidate will:
Prepare, review and manage comments on all types of Development Applications, Environmental Assessments, Realty Requests and associated Agreements related to Parkland and Greenlands, including Parkland Cash-in-lieu determinations on behalf of Parks Assets, Urban Design
Coordination, review, and preparation of comments related to license and easement agreements, land acquisition and surplus declarations that impact City owned parkland and greenland
Liaises and meets with public agencies and departments, professionals, consultants, elected officials, staff, residents and special interest groups as required with respect to the projects and the future development of parks and recreational facilities
Attend and lead public meetings for presentation as well as provides professional advice and input to the public, Council and other professionals
Research and prepare reports to Committees and Council
Attend and provide evidence at Ontario Land Tribunal hearings
Performs other related duties as assigned

Graduate from a recognized university in Planning or related discipline with a minimum of 5 years of experience in development planning
Demonstrated knowledge and experience of municipal land development processes including subdivision, rezoning and site plan applications as well as servicing and development agreements
Ability to liaise with elected officials, other City Departments, federal & provincial authorities, conservation & regional authorities, and other outside agencies as required
Demonstrated project management and time management skills
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Demonstrated ability to provide detailed analysis of development applications and to negotiate and advocate for Parks Assets, Urban Design interests
Ability to work well in a team environment and independently
Knowledge of related computer applications required including Microsoft Suite software and ePlans
Eligibility for membership in the Ontario Professional Planners Institute and Canadian Institute of Planners is required

Job Summary
As a DevOps Specialist, you will work with technical teams across the organization to implement DevOps strategies and automate applications and infrastructure across on-premise and cloud environments. You will be responsible for understanding requirements and designing, documenting, supporting and delivering secure, scalable and reliable solutions within a defined framework.
The successful candidate will collaborate with software development teams, project managers and infrastructure architects to design, build, deploy, operate and monitor enterprise applications and services. Responsibilities include implementing Infrastructure as Code (IaC), cloud automation, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring solutions and operational best practices.
This role requires hands-on experience with AWS services including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM and networking services, as well as Windows and Linux administration. Experience with Azure DevOps, scripting, AI-assisted tools and automation is also desirable. Occasional work outside regular business hours is a requirement of the position. The role follows a hybrid work model, requiring employees to be onsite in the office 3 days per week and allowing remote work for the remaining days. Specific in-office days may be set by the team or department to support collaboration and business needs.
Duties and Responsibilities
Design, implement and support DevOps practices, cloud infrastructure, automation solutions and CI/CD pipelines.
Develop and maintain Infrastructure as Code and configuration management solutions using Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible or similar tools.
Configure, manage and troubleshoot AWS services including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC and Elastic Load Balancing.
Develop and support containerized applications using Docker and Amazon ECS, and administer Windows and Linux environments across cloud and on-premise infrastructure.
Develop automation and integrations using PowerShell, Python, YAML, REST APIs and related technologies.
Implement monitoring, alerting, logging and performance optimization solutions for applications and infrastructure.
Investigate and resolve application, infrastructure, networking, security and deployment issues.
Collaborate with development, infrastructure, security and business teams to deliver production-ready solutions that comply with City standards and industry best practices.
Develop and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, operational procedures and recovery plans.
Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI-assisted DevOps tools and Microsoft Power Platform, to improve operational efficiency and service delivery.
Provide technical guidance, training and knowledge transfer to staff and project teams.
Participate in after-hours support, maintenance activities and emergency response as required.

Post-secondary degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline, or possess an equivalent combination of education, certifications and experience
3+ years of experience as a DevOps Engineer, DevOps Specialist, Cloud Engineer or in a similar role.
Strong understanding of Agile methodologies, DevOps principles, source control and CI/CD practices.
Experience designing and implementing CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Jenkins or similar platforms.
Strong experience configuring and supporting AWS environments, including ECS, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Route 53, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC and load balancing services.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code and configuration management tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, Ansible, Chef or Puppet.
Experience with Docker, Amazon ECS and containerized application delivery.
Strong scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python and YAML.
Related IT certifications are an asset. AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Solutions Architect or equivalent is preferred.
Advanced hands-on experience with Windows and Linux administration, monitoring, logging and troubleshooting.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, collaboration and documentation skills, with the ability to work independently or within cross-functional teams.
Experience with Microsoft Azure or other cloud platforms would be considered an asset.
Experience evaluating and implementing AI-assisted tools for software development, infrastructure operations and DevOps workflows would be considered an asset.
Experience with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps and Power Automate, would be considered an asset.
May require light lifting of supplies or materials and prolonged use of computer keyboards and screens in a primarily office-based environment.

Control and obey all regulations, policies and procedures to ensure pedestrians are safely assisted at designated school crossings.

Document and communicate all incidents and/or unsafe conditions to management, school officials and/or Peel Regional Police.

Must have the ability to remain alert and perform responsibilities quickly and safely.
Must have excellent customer service skills and the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with management, pedestrians, residents, school officials and police.

Must be able to extend an arm out parallel to shoulder holding a “STOP” sign (weight of approximately 1 pound) for up to one minute frequently.
Must be able to effectively hear and see oncoming traffic at a safe distance (approximately 300 feet).
Previous experience dealing with the public and/or children is an asset.
Training on the Highway Traffic Act and Health and Safety Act as it relates to the job and City policies and procedures is provided to all School Crossing Guards by the City.

AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY:
Reporting directly to the Treasurer, this role provides strategic direction and expert advice to the Finance Division on financial planning, budget review, and ensuring fiscal efficiency. The role involves preparing detailed assessments, aligning departmental proposals with the City’s Strategic Plan, and ensuring financial and legislative compliance. This position also plays a critical role in City-wide strategic planning, fostering a collaborative environment that values trust, diversity, and inclusivity.
Stakeholder Relationships
Collaborate with stakeholders to identify improvement areas, facilitate solutions, and promote a culture of fiscal responsibility and innovation. •    Build effective working relationships at all levels, particularly with senior leaders in client departments across the City, ensuring the highest possible level of client satisfaction and being established as a trusted advisor. •    Build and foster strong working relationships and collaborative arrangements with internal and external customers, stakeholders, business and community leaders, sponsors, public and the media.
Operation Strategy
Lead initiatives that enhance operational excellence, setting goals and implementing policies to support Council priorities. •    Identify and manage complex, interdependent projects, ensuring alignment with relevant strategic goals. •    Provide the Treasurer with recommendations on managing critical issues and risks. •    Ensure a high standard of financial planning, budget, management reporting, and analytical support is delivered consistently to their department portfolio. •    Establish clear goals and create policies that support the Council’s priorities and the City’s strategic vision. •    Regularly review and report on the status of strategic initiatives to ensure continuous alignment with strategic goals.
Financial Analysis & Strategic Planning
Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Advise on financial impacts of budget proposals and submit recommendations to the leadership team and Council. •    Participate in strategic planning at both the sectional level as well as the provision of expertise to the broader City-wide strategy. •    Prepare detailed financial reports that include analysis, projections, and recommendations. •    Assist with the annual budget planning process, ensuring it meets the City’s financial requirements and strategic objectives.
Policy & Legislative Support
Interpret legislation, monitor trends, and use research and data analytics to inform policy and strategy decisions. •    Maintain knowledge of all laws, regulatory, judicial mandates, ordinances, legislative various acts, codes and by-laws set out by Federal, Provincial or Municipal levels of government. •    Continuously update policies and procedures to reflect legislative changes and best practices.
Financial Modelling & Advice
Develop financial models and provide insights to support decision-making, collective bargaining, and resource management. •    Offer guidance to finance staff across City departments. •    Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Provide expert advice on the financial implications of various budget proposals to the leadership team and Council.
Communication and Reporting
Prepare and present complex financial reports and recommendations, keeping leadership informed of key activities and initiatives. •    Develop comprehensive financial reports that accurately reflect the City’s financial status and projections. •    Regularly update the leadership team on key financial activities and initiatives. •    Maintain a high level of transparency in all financial communications to build trust and credibility.
SELECTION CRITERIA:
Education:
Post-secondary degree in Economics, Business, Public Administration or other relevant discipline. •    CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) or CFA or MBA is preferred.
Experience:
Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in finance or public administration, preferably within a municipal or similarly complex organization, with significant responsibility for strategic and financial analysis, multi-year operating and capital budgets, funding strategies, and business case development. •    Proven experience advising senior leadership, leading and facilitating complex cross-departmental initiatives, and applying legislative and policy analysis to support financial, strategic, and organizational decision-making.
Other Skills and Assets:
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving abilities, with proficiency in Microsoft tools. •    Ability to handle sensitive situations with discretion and maintain strong internal and external relationships. •    Strong knowledge of financial planning, budget management, and capital funding analysis. •    Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing and presenting complex financial reports and recommendations. •    Expert knowledge of Municipal, Regional, Provincial and Federal Governments, applicable Legislations and awareness of current social, economic and political priorities •    Ability to prioritize highly complex tasks with critical deadlines •    Experience developing policies and procedures and ensuring compliance

This position is responsible for providing operational support to the Disability Management Team with a focus on the coordination of WSIB claims from creation to closure as well as administratively supporting the management of STD and LTD claims. The incumbent will facilitate and process documentation and transactions related to WSIB and disability claims management and help with educating our managers and employees with the workers compensation and disability claims processes.
OPERATIONS SUPPORT
Support HR stakeholders in managing WSIB claims management.
Maintain records of all WSIB claim files from creation to closure.
Review WSIB cost statement to ensure appropriate costs are levied at the City.
Coordinate RTW/Medical Accommodations meetings with all employees who require an accommodation for medical reasons or are returning from an extended medical absence for occupational or non-occupational illnesses.

Participate in problem solving, including addressing and resolving complaints with pay and entitlement.
Assist with the maintenance of case files.

Arranging for assessments to take place including FAE’s (functional abilities evaluation) and IME’s (Independent Medical Examination), etc.
Ensure the safeguarding of all confidential files.
CUSTOMER SERVICE
Respond and handle service related enquiries within the established service standard timelines.
Providing advice and guidance, including policy procedure, and collective agreement interpretation on disability management, return to work and medical accommodation.
CORPORATE CONTRIBUTION
Conduct research and analysis using various resources to gain insight of current program/project, processes and practices to assist team in ways to improve service solutions and support operational needs.
Researching and coordinating training sessions on abilities management, return to work and medical accommodation.
COMMUNICATION AND REPORTING
Monitoring WSIB, STD and LTD claims by maintaining communication with the employee and their leader.
Collecting data, analyzing and generating reports and program statistics while ensuring data quality.
Assist with the development of templates, forms, letters, etc.
Prepares communications (letters, etc.) to supervisors, employees and insurance providers regarding claims management.
Working collaboratively with the various unions, while addressing complex cases with the WSIB, HR, OD and the LTD providers.
TEAMWORK AND COOPERATION
Assist in special projects as required.
Work within diverse groups to support operational goals and objectives.
Demonstrate corporate values at all times.
Participate as a member of cross-functional team.
Provide support/backup as necessary to team members.

Education:
Post-secondary degree in Human Resources, Occupational Health, Kinesiology, Nursing, Social Work or other related academic program
Experience:

Working knowledge of policies, legislation and principles pertaining to disability management and accommodation, such as the Workplace Safety & Insurance Act, Ontario Human Rights and Accessibility legislation, and other relevant legislation.
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written and presentation skills.
Attention to detail, excellent organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proven ability to manage time in a deadline-oriented environment.
Working knowledge of policies, legislation and principles pertaining to disability management and accommodation, such as the Workplace Safety & Insurance Act, Ontario Human Rights and Accessibility legislation, and other relevant legislation.
Customer service skills, including exercising tact, diplomacy and sensitivity when dealing with employees in a multi-union and non-unionized environment and staff at all levels, as well as external stakeholders.
Ability to work as both a team player and independently, with minimal supervision.
Demonstrate a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through continuous development, modeling inclusive behaviors, and proactively managing bias.
Problem solving and critical thinking skills.
Proficient in the use of spreadsheets, databases and word processing.
Excellent data analysis ability and familiarity with computerized absence tracking and reporting methods.
A high level of computer proficiency, especially with collection of information, data, and reporting.
Developed computer skills in Microsoft Office, SharePoint, PeopleSoft, Parklane or other claims/attendance management systems.
NIDMAR Certified Return to Work Coordinator Certification (CRTWC) or Certified Disability Management Professional (CDMP) is an asset.

My Community. My Lifestyle. My Career.
Firefighter Opportunity
Are you interested in helping to build a safe community? If so, City of Brampton Fire and Emergency Services may be the right place for you....
Bring your talents and step into a firefighter career where serving our diverse community and the opportunities to make a difference are endless. Our Brampton Fire and Emergency Services team are driven by exceptional service delivery. As a member of our team, you will feel the pride of values-driven achievements and will experience life-long supportive relationships. Be a part of a fast-paced and rewarding environment where you can contribute to building a safe community, improving Emergency Response, Public Safety and Public Education for the citizens of Brampton.
In this highly visible role, you will:
Serve as a highly valued and respected member of the community;
Feel the excitement that comes with serving the community. Every shift has a different challenge or situation requiring a diverse set of skills;
Respond to all emergencies when called upon;
Combating fires;
Performing rescue operations and providing medical assistance in an emergency environment;
Handle routine maintenance of firefighting equipment/ department property;
Public fire safety education and inspect properties and equipment for fire hazards;
Handle state of the art apparatus and modern equipment;
Have the ability to help your community and network as an ambassador at charity and community events;
Participate in continuous learning to advance your knowledge and skills;
Be part of a culture that values the personal and professional growth and development; and
Perform other similar and related duties as assigned.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Ontario Secondary School Diploma or academic equivalent.
Minimum of 18 years of age or older
Legally entitled to work in Canada.
National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1001 Firefighter I & II and NFPA 1072 (NFPA 472) Hazardous Materials Awareness/Operations certifications or equivalent as recognized by the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) (must have proof of Pro Board or IFSAC).
Possess a valid and current Standard First Aid and CPR "C" certification
Possess a valid and unrestricted Ontario Class “D” driver’s license with a “Z” endorsement or equivalent (deemed equivalent by Ontario Ministry of Transportation) and a driving record that is acceptable to the City of Brampton.
Provide a satisfactory Police Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening
Completion of the Ontario Fire Administration Candidate Testing Program Stage 2
OR
Completion of the York University Firefighter Fitness Testing
NFPA 1006 Certified in Surface Water Rescue – Level II (2013 Standard) or Operations Level (2021 Standard)
OR
Completion of OFAI Swim Test (as verified by possession of a current and valid certificate)
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across a variety of situations and audiences.
Ability to work rotating 24-hour shifts, including nights, weekends, statutory holidays, and other scheduled shift assignments.
Demonstrated ability to swim proficiently and successfully complete the required swim assessment.
Candidates must meet the vision requirements established by NFPA 1582
Demonstrated ability to safely perform the intense and sustained physical activities associated with firefighting, including working in physically demanding and stressful environments.
The ability to attain certifications within 18 months from the date a conditional offer of employment
BENEFICIAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:
College diploma or university degree from a recognized and accredited post-secondary institution.
Commitment to volunteerism humanitarian, or community service.
Act with integrity, exercise sound judgment, solve complex problems, support continuous improvement, and consistently provide professional and respectful service to the community.
Accepts direction, work effectively within a team environment, establishes and maintains a positive professional relationships, and demonstrate compassion, respect, and empathy toward others.
Maintains confidence, professionalism, and composure when responding to stressful, challenging, or traumatic situations.
Demonstrate effective strategies for managing occupational stress, maintaining personal well-being, and supporting a healthy work-life balance.
Demonstrate resilience, tenacity, and perseverance when faced with difficult or changing circumstances, while maintaining a positive and solution-focused approach.
Previous experience working in customer service, public service, or other roles involving regular interaction with members of the public.
Trade apprenticeship or a minimum of one year of experience in a skilled trade recognized in Ontario.
Minimum of one year of previous experience as a volunteer, part-time, or full-time firefighter.
Minimum of one year of previous experience in an emergency services environment other than fire suppression.
Minimum of one year of experience operating large or heavy vehicles and/or heavy machinery.
Minimum of one year of experience as an elevator technician, fire alarm technician, fire and life safety technician, member of the military, or member of the Canadian Coast Guard.
National Lifeguard Certification: Possession of a current National Lifeguard (NL) certification.
Occupational Health and Safety: Completion of occupational health and safety training or certification, such as Joint Health and Safety Committee (JHSC) Part 1 and Part 2 certification.
Possession of a current Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) certification.
Previous experience, training, and/or (Operations or Technician) certification in technical rescue disciplines, including water, ice, trench, rope, or confined space rescue, consistent with the competencies identified in NFPA 1006.
Previous experience in hazardous materials removal, environmental remediation, or private-sector disaster management, including chemical spills, environmental clean-up, mould, asbestos, biohazard, or contamination remediation.
Demonstrated ability to work with diverse communities (race, culture, ability, mental health, sexual orientation, faith, gender identity and all diverse identities)
Multilingual skills preferred

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
:
Reporting to the Manager, Internal Audit, (or to the Director, Internal Audit on solo projects) this position plans, performs internal audit assurance and advisory engagements of moderate complexity for the City of Brampton in accordance with the Internal Audit Charter and recognized Internal Audit Professional Practices and codes of professional conduct. This includes initiating, leading and conducting, risk based audits, operational effectiveness reviews, audits of compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, by-laws, City policies and procedures and working with management to develop effective and efficient risk mitigation strategies. Ability to work independently and objectively when conducting audit engagements of moderate complexity, preparing audit reports and evaluating management action plans. Supports the Director in planning, coordinating and management of audit resources, including third party consultants. Participating in the development of the audit function’s strategic plan and multi-year and annual internal audit work plan.  The role is an ambassador for risk management and continuous improvement of the control environment, and brings innovative ideas and methods to increase awareness and buy-in from management.
Conducts operational audits in accordance with professional audit standards in the role of lead auditor, team member or working independently on some projects, with responsibility to supervise more junior project staff
Performs assigned projects of moderate complexity (or work with a Manager, Internal Audit on complex audit engagements) and deal with high dollar values and confidential and sensitive information affecting the City operations, assets and resources
Develops a solid understanding of the audit entity or subject matter by conducting background research accomplished through use of the internet, discussion with the auditee, site visits, the review of relevant documents such as multi-year business plans, consultant reports, statues, regulations or standards, committee and council minutes, previous year’s audited financial statements and management letters, contact with other professional and municipal organizations
Develops (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the project plan including determining audit objectives, scope and methodology; assessing risk and internal controls; establishing budget and reporting timelines
Prepares (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the audit program and /or evidence collection plan which includes defining of audit criteria by performing extensive research of sources such as recognized bodies of experts, applicable laws, regulations and other authorities, other bodies or jurisdictions delivering similar programs and services, internal policies and procedures and applicable criteria successfully applied in other audits or reviews done internally and externally; developing audit procedures and tests; and determining what evidence is needed, how the evidence can be collected, will be analyzed, interpreted
Complete assigned audit procedures (interviews, analysis, examination of documentation, site visits, and other testing) in accordance with the project plan and adapts /expands audit procedures, as necessary, based on issues identified as the audit progresses
Conducts thorough assessment and analysis and obtains sufficient and appropriate evidence
Identifies significant audit issues and improvement opportunities, quantifying cost savings / revenue opportunities, and illustrating non-financial impacts
Develops practical and meaningful audit recommendations that will help improve City services or operations
Prepares and / or reviews audit working papers (audit project files) that contains evidence supporting the findings, conclusions, and recommendations and ensures that they adhere to professional auditing standards and Internal Audit’s office guidelines and audit manuals.
Evaluate audit results and prepares a written summary of major audit issues (audit observations, conclusions, and recommendations) independently or in consultation with the Manager, Internal Audit or the Director of Internal Audit
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in all aspects of work (audit planning, fieldwork, audit finding evaluation, and reporting)
Prepares draft audit reports or parts thereof, for review by the senior management of Internal Audit prior to submission to auditee, Audit Committee and /or other standing committees
Makes presentations to auditee personnel to communicate audit recommendations, as required.
Evaluates action plans in response to recommendations
Keeps Director/Manager, Internal Audit informed of audit progress, any emerging issues and /or significant areas, and recommends appropriate action and /strategies to meet planned project objectives and audit reporting deadlines
Attends Audit Committee meetings and makes presentations on audit project(s) as required
Performs special audits and investigations including fraud reviews and forensic audits, as required
Maintains good auditee relationships and acts at all times in a professional manner
Liaises with and keeps current of the operations of assigned departments with particular reference to audit concerns and issues
Contribute to effective teamwork and communication, high standards of work quality and organizational performance and continuous learning
Participates in development and implementation of Internal Audit’s corporate initiatives, including coordinating training, IT system applications, continuous process improvement projects etc)
Contributes to the Internal Audit’s strategic planning process, such as the City-wide risk assessment, and annual and long-term work plan
SELECTION CRITERIA
Education:
University Degree, with a professional Accounting Designation (such as CPA, CA; CPA, CGA; or CPA, CMA); or designation as an auditing professional (CIA, CGAP, CRMA, CISA).
An equivalent combination of education, skills and considerable experience in the field of performance auditing, operational and control auditing, and other audit projects will be considered.
Fraud certifications Audit certifications (such as CFE) are an asset.
Experience:
A minimum of 5 years of practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money/performance audits, operational/control audits, and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals. Public sector internal audit experience is desirable.
Comprehensive in-depth knowledge of all aspects of audit principles, practices, techniques and standards (including the IIA Standards and the Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards.)
Other Skills and Assets:
Sound organizational, interpersonal, oral and written communications skills.
Sound project management, analytical, excellent initiative, and problem solving skills.
Ability to deal courteously and effectively with all levels of staff, management and members of council, and build consensus.
Ability to work independently and with minimum supervision.
Ability to work in a multi-disciplinary setting and team environment.
Computer proficiency in MS Office Suite and audit applications such as TeamMate or Pentana.
Experience with data analytics applications (such as ACL, TeamMate Analytics) and performing data analytics as part of audits or other special projects which assist in the collection and analysis of electronic data would be asset.
Experience with Pentana, TeamMate or other audit software is strongly preferred.
Mandatory Requirements:
University Degree in relevant fields (business, accounting, management), coupled with an accounting designation (CPA, CA or CPA, CMA or CPA, CGA); or and auditing designation such as CIA, CISA.
A minimum of 5 or more years practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money (performance) audits, operational/control audits,  and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals.
