POSITION DUTIES:
Reporting to the Director, Cultural Services, this position provides senior-level strategic and operational leadership to advance the City of Brampton’s readiness for the future transfer of the Peel Art Gallery, Museum and Archives (PAMA), effective January 1, 2028, through the design and integration of a new Museums & Collections line of business.
The role operates within a multi-party governance structure where the PAMA Transition Board provides strategic direction and oversight, the Region of Peel maintains operational responsibility during the transition period, and external advisors (including KPMG) support operating model development.
Within this context, the position is accountable for leading the City’s internal planning, integration, and operational readiness work, translating Transition Board direction and consulting outputs into City-ready service models, implementation plans, and decision frameworks. The role ensures that the City is prepared to assume operations with a cohesive, financially sustainable, and operationally viable Museums & Collections service
Museums & Collections Strategy and Service Model Development
Lead the development of an integrated Museums & Collections service framework, including mandate, scope, and service delivery model
Define how PAMA, gallery and exhibition functions, heritage sites (including Bovaird House and Alderlea), and programming operate as a coordinated municipal service
Establish clear roles, relationships, and workflows between collections stewardship, curatorial practice, exhibitions, and public programming
Align the Museums & Collections service with existing Cultural Services lines of business while defining a distinct and sustainable service identity
Ensure alignment between external operating model work (including KPMG) and the City’s broader Cultural Services framework
Identify service delivery options, including governance considerations, programming approaches, and partnership opportunities
Develop long-term vision and positioning for municipal museum and gallery services in Brampton
Prepare briefing materials, business cases, and strategic recommendations for senior leadership and Council
Align work with broader corporate initiatives and transition-related studies
PAMA Transition Planning and Readiness
Lead Cultural Services’ role in transition planning to support the future transfer of PAMA
Translate Transition Board direction into actionable City requirements, including service delivery expectations and operational implications
Develop and maintain a City-focused transition roadmap, including key milestones leading to January 1, 2028
Identify and document readiness requirements, dependencies, and constraints across systems, staffing, and operations
Establish and monitor readiness frameworks and validation criteria to ensure preparedness for transfer
Identify, assess, and escalate risks to the City’s future assumption of operations, including financial, operational, and reputational risks
Coordinate cross-functional planning across Finance, HR, Legal, IT, Planning, Communications, and Facilities
Support development of implementation plans, timelines, and resource requirements
Provide ongoing updates, analysis, and advisory support to senior leadership
Bovaird House Collections and Strategic Positioning
Lead a comprehensive review of collections, assets, and current operations at Historic Bovaird House
Develop and oversee implementation of a collections management and rationalization strategy, including retention, deaccessioning, and transfer
Establish or refine collections management standards, documentation practices, and risk mitigation protocols
Develop recommendations for the future role, function, and positioning of Bovaird House within the Museums & Collections portfolio
Align site operations and programming with the future integrated service model
Oversee development of an interim programming and operating approach during the transition period
Ensure collections and curatorial decisions support long-term exhibition, programming, and public engagement outcomes.
Operational Planning and Financial Modelling
Translate operating model concepts (including external consulting work) into practical, implementable City operating plans
Develop costed operating models, including staffing requirements, budget forecasts, and infrastructure needs
Define future-state workflows, procedures, and service delivery standards across all sites and functions
Establish alignment between collections management, curatorial development, exhibitions, and programming delivery
Identify resource requirements, gaps, and financial pressures, and propose mitigation strategies
Support development of multi-year implementation and operational plans leading to the transfer date
Ensure alignment between strategic direction and operational feasibility
Inform long-term financial sustainability planning for the Museums & Collections service
Stakeholder Coordination and Strategic Advisory
Provide senior-level strategic advice to the Director, Cultural Services and Community Services Management Team
Support coordination between City staff, the PAMA Transition Board, and external consultants
Liaise with internal departments, including Finance, Budget Office, Legal, HR, Planning (Heritage), Communications, IT, and Facilities
Ensure the City’s interests and requirements are clearly represented in transition planning processes
Engage with heritage stakeholders, community organizations, and cultural sector partners
Prepare reports, briefings, and presentations for internal and external audiences, including Council
Identify and communicate risks, issues, and mitigation strategies
Build relationships and influence across divisions to advance complex, cross-functional work
SELECTION CRITERIA
Education:
Post-secondary degree in Museum Studies, Cultural Heritage Management, Arts Administration, Public Administration, or a related field.
Experience:
Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in museum operations, cultural planning, or heritage management
Experience in service model development, organizational planning, or transformation initiatives
Experience supporting large-scale organizational transition, service integration, or implementation initiatives
Experience contributing to operating model development, budgeting, or financial analysis in a public or institutional context
Experience working within a municipal or public-sector environment preferred
Demonstrated experience with collections management and curatorial practices
Experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder environments
Special Requirements:
Strong knowledge of museum standards, collections management, and curatorial practices
Strategic thinking and ability to translate high-level direction and operating model concepts into practical, implementable service and financial plans
Strong project leadership and coordination skills
Ability to provide strategic advice within complex governance structures, including boards and senior leadership environments
Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and evolving environments
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
Strong written and verbal communication skills for executive audiences
Ability to build relationships and influence without direct authority

POSITION DUTIES:
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Revenue, responsible for the management and direction of all collection activities for defaulted Provincial Offence Act (POA) fines, non-parking Administrative Monetary Penalty (AMPS), tax accounts in arrears, and miscellaneous receivables owed to the City.  In addition, this position is responsible for all administrative aspects of the Tax Collection, POA, and General Receivables sections. This individual provides leadership, strategic direction, and overall staff development within the Corporate Collections area.  The individual will be required to either personally represent the Corporation or co-ordinate representation in dealings with external agencies, various clients, legal proceedings and appeal hearings.  Provides direction, guidance and skills development to non-union and union staff.
Manage all operational and administrative aspects of the tax arrears, defaulted POA fines, Non-parking AMPS and general accounts receivable billing and collection processes including supervision, hiring, guidance and direction of staff; •    Review and initiate staff development activities; •    Monitor/ coach area supervisory staff to ensure that proper priorities and service levels are established and maintained; •    Recommend, plan, develop and implement new or innovative procedures to improve efficiency and the overall success of collection activities; •    Recommend and implement changes to Corporate Policies and Standard Operating Procedures as required; •    Provide leadership to ensure high productivity to realize corporate priorities; •    Manage debt collection activities undertaken by both internal staff and on behalf of the City by external service providers, such as collection agencies and bailiffs; •    Ensure accuracy of commissions paid to external collectors; •    Ensure that all collection activities are compliant with applicable legislation, Municipal Act,  City policies and By-laws, and Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of the Attorney General for POA fine activities; •    Manage the Tax Sale process in strict compliance with the requirements of the Municipal Act, Ontario Regulations, and court precedent; •    Represent the Department/City in meetings with internal and external customers, suppliers, tribunals, legal proceedings, professional associations, and municipal and provincial governments; •    Responsible for the accuracy and balance of the Accounts Receivable system ; •    Ensure a proper system of internal controls are in place for entries to TXM 2000 tax system, CAMS, the Integrated Court Offences Network (ICON), the Accounts Receivable system and related General Ledger entries; •    Review and authorize cheque requisitions and reconciliations for the distribution of the POA fines collected on behalf of other municipalities and government agencies; •    Responsible for the approval and posting to the general ledger of journal entries for POA revenue and general accounts receivable. •    Review doubtful accounts and make annual financial provision for doubtful allowance in the general ledger. •    Responsible for identification of uncollectable accounts (POA, property tax and general accounts receivable) and preparation of Council reports for write-off of accounts. •    Prepare reports as required for Council information and approval •    Prepare and monitor the annual budget for all accounts under Corporate Collections responsibility. •    Prepare related schedules of annual Financial Information Return (FIR) as needed; •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with  effective collection processes; •    Responsible for managing the procurement process (Request for Proposal, Request for Quote) and administer contracts with external vendors related to the operation of the Collections unit. •    Collaborates with systems administrators and vendors in preparation of business requirements, testing and deployments of any new software for the Collections unit. •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with effective collection methods; •    Provide assistance/backup to Supervisor of Tax Collection and Collections Group Leader as required; •    Ensure that records retention is in compliance with legislative and by-law requirements.

Area of Responsiblities:
Reporting to the Manager, Enterprise Corporate Systems, this position will participate in a major City-wide project to implement an application that will deliver automation and transform business processes and practices in the area of WFM Workforce Management solutions supporting Employee Time Capture, Absence Management (Time and Attendance) and Workforce Scheduling. This position is responsible for assessing, researching, analysing and documenting business and systems requirements while working with both internal, external and City-wide department resources. In addition, the incumbent will be heavily involved in the design of business processes, testing, training and the preparation of operational documentation.
This role partners with HR, Finance and Operating Departments in supporting, troubleshooting, coordinating, implementing and recommending solutions that meet client needs. This role can be involved in the RFP process as well as development of business requirements to ensure that projects align with strategies.
Once this application is live and in production, this position will be responsible for the support and on-going maintenance of the application as well as recommend solutions to leverage the functional capabilities to meet future business needs. This position will also offer guidance, support, advice, and direction to various City departments in post-implementation operations of this system and related integrations/interfaces to enhance the use of these systems, thus leveraging functionality to gain efficiencies in business processes and/or greater insight into information. This position provides excellent customer service while protecting the integrity of the data, automating business processes, participating in major system implementations, upgrades, troubleshooting incidents and maintaining optimal configuration.
Business Analysis
- Liaise with clients to gather business requirements, to conduct current and future process mapping to determine the fit/gap in the planning and development of new system functionality and/or related business processes. Consult with Stakeholders and evaluate business needs to develop understanding of true requirements and translate into functional specifications while working with technical teams, to recommend solutions. Interpret Union collective agreements and collaborate when necessary to understand the rules, knowing how they intersect with business processes, system functionality and related system configuration. Present, explain, and validate analysis with client to ensure proposed solution meets their business needs. Lead the implementation of necessary business and systems changes. Serve as a functional source of expertise in supporting the maintenance and/or development of process improvements and changes. Perform benchmarking to help determine the future/strategic direction of the systems.
System Technical Analysis
- Responsible for defining interface parameters between systems, identifying system data dependencies, and approving all technical specifications and changes. Responsible for the daily operation and troubleshooting of user problems.  Lead and contribute to project teams to assist in the research, selection, evaluation and implementation of new software applications and services.
Confidentiality
- Access to system wide confidential data for analysis and operations. Participate in development and implementation of confidential initiatives.
Testing and Quality Assurance
-
Prepare, review and collaborate on development of test strategy, test plans and test metrics. Create user stories, use cases and subsequently create and execute detailed test scripts including documenting of defects, defect reporting and collaborative issues resolution. Prepare testing time and effort estimates and schedule testing activities with various resources. Report on testing status and progress against project plans. Manage the design, specification and execution of tests, including ensuring that test design accounts for risk and selecting the appropriate test types. Review and improve on test cases developed by other testers. Interacts with developers, project team resources and vendors during issue resolution and re-testing. Utilize appropriate tools for test scripting, test execution, defect reporting and overall status reporting.
System Lead and Trainer
- Act as Project Lead or Project Support for different initiatives. Act as the System Lead in developing and providing direction to a team of employees in the maintenance, implementation or upgrades of all systems with a view of other areas impacting or being impacted by change. Ensure that application standards are followed, and that development, set-up/configuration, testing and data validation are completed successfully and on time. Develop and maintain training materials and conduct user training sessions to support system business demands including both functional, system and related business processes and procedures.
Project
Lead and Support
– Support Team Lead and the Project Manager in
d
eveloping and maintaining applicable project documentation that clearly defines what processes, functionality, timelines and results will be expected for each new functionality implementation or upgrade of the systems. Develop project plans and lead assigned operational projects.
Data Integrity and Report Development
- Develop and maintain data integrity standards using system audits and business process reviews.  Audit and review the system framework that supports business processes.  Prepare functional specifications in creating new reports and system enhancements. Capture, interpret and develop a detailed understanding of data reporting requirements to create and test standard and ad hoc queries and mass data extracts for data requests for often time sensitive and confidential data requests.
Compliance
- Maintain system documentation as it pertains to configuration, issue resolution, test plans, project decisions, standard operating procedures, data standards, processes, training and support.
Security
– Ensure security requests are actioned and analysed to ensure compliance with security strategy, related policies and audit assessments to safeguard the system and confidential business data. Evaluate all requested changes to ensure segregation of duties in business processes are not compromised. Includes processing daily access requests, regular system audits and escalations.
System Support
– Develop / configure / set-up / maintain functional application configuration and rules to ensure required functionality and reporting capability meets the needs of the Corporation and end users. Troubleshoot User and system issues, perform root cause analysis and document resolutions. Provide guidance, clarification and resolution to system issues.
System Administration
- Develop, maintain and audit system defined standards and processes. This includes ensuring batch job processing schedules, interfaces and integrations are processed in a timely manner to support time sensitive business processes. This also includes the setup and maintenance of system-wide installation, configuration settings, controls and security/privacy design. Ensure application data integrity, system access and data distribution managed appropriately. Investigate, analyze, design, test and recommend optimal system enhancements.

Education:
Degree/diploma in Business, Computers Science, Human Resource Management or equivalent
Experience
:
3 to 5 years experience in implementing and/or maintaining and supporting an enterprise scale WFM (including Time and Attendance / Time, Absence Management, Scheduling) and integrations with other internal and external applications such as Payroll, employee data whare houses, etc.
Minimum 3 to 5 years experience in translating enterprise business requirements into WFM (HR/Time and Attendance/Scheduling/Absence Management) application functionality, business processes and policy impacts
Strong knowledge of Human Resources, Payroll, Information Technology policies and practices with an ability to assess the impacts of policies and practices on related technologies supporting business processes
Other Skills and Assets:
Knowledge of Duty Rostering, Scheduling and Time Attendance Practices and Processes.
Strong project planning and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects that include cross-functional teams in different business units

Experience in testing / quality assurance processes, test cycles, defect management, testing tools and test automation is an asset
Experience with Oracle-PeopleSoft Enterprise HRMS / HCM and/or Payroll, WorkforceSoftware (cloud solution) would be an asset

Experience in business process mapping and redesign, relational database concepts, SQL query tools, data integrations, dashboarding tools and project management techniques
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including the ability to deliver effective training and translate functional requirements for technical people and technical details to functional people, i.e. within own team, HR, Payroll, Functional Departments, Vendors and other Technical Teams

Job Summary
Reporting to the Manager of Water & Wastewater Planning, the Project Manager is responsible for leading Region-wide water and wastewater infrastructure servicing studies and long-term growth-related capital implementation plans. Key undertakings include the completion of Water and Wastewater Servicing Studies, feasibility studies, system capacity assessments, growth monitoring related to system capacity, development reviews, development charges background technical studies, and infrastructure staging plans which are integral to the Region's Development Charge Bylaw and Allocation Programs.

Act as Project Manager for infrastructure Servicing Studies that will determine the preferred infrastructure through applying an engineering and environmentally responsible perspective as it relates to the environment, including but not limited to natural, socio-economic and cultural/archaeological environments.

Acting as a trusted advisor and primary HR contact, the position partners with leaders and employees to deliver guidance and solutions on a wide range of HR matters, including talent acquisition, employee relations, attendance and disability management, job evaluation, performance management, training and development, organizational effectiveness, health and safety, and legislative compliance. HR Business Partnering and Advisory Services
Serve as the primary Human Resources contact for assigned client groups, providing timely, practical, and solution oriented advice on a broad range of human resources matters;
Build strong working relationships with managers and employees to support operational objectives, workforce needs, and employee engagement initiatives;

title: Senior Building Inspector
location: Garden St. Branch Office, Whitby, ON
description:
Our team is highly skilled, passionate about our community, and we care. Let’s grow together.
Who We Are
In Whitby, we are dedicated to our work, our community, and each other. We work hard, we have fun, and we celebrate our successes.
The Town of Whitby is a community in transformation that is located in the heart of Durham Region in the eastern Greater Toronto Area. Whitby is the second-largest municipality in the region and one of the fastest-growing communities in Canada. Located on Lake Ontario and only an hour east of Toronto, the population of Whitby is expected to grow from 140,000 to more than 200,000 by 2031. Whitby’s Official Plan has been updated to establish new directions for Whitby’s planned growth and development; the protection of our natural and built environments; urban design intensification; sustainability; community improvement; and, new employment within this time frame.
The Town of Whitby combines a small town atmosphere with the sophistication and amenities of a larger urban centre.
Whitby boasts two beautiful heritage downtowns, one of the finest recreational harbours with an award-winning marina, year round sports and recreation activities, parks, trails, and a robust arts and culture scene, all of which are part of the extraordinary amenities that Whitby residents enjoy every day.
Whitby has an exciting and aspiring future, with a community that is welcoming, growing and transforming. On our team, you can expect to make a difference through your work and have a direct impact on shaping our growing community. Creating an inclusive environment where employees experience job satisfaction and have rewarding careers is important to us. We live our values and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, respect and engagement where people enjoy coming to work.
The Town of Whitby is a hybrid organization. This means staff are empowered to do their best work from various locations, as appropriate for the position.
We want to be the preferred employer for the most talented people who care about the Town of Whitby, and are excited and proud to serve our vibrant community.
Let’s grow together.
What You Will Get To Do
The successful candidate will have a positive impact on our corporate culture by demonstrating the Town’s CARE core values (Collaborative, Accountable, Respectful, Engaged) through daily interactions with individuals at all levels of the organization, external contacts and elected officials.
By effectively building positive rapport and relationships both internally and externally, the successful candidate will help us achieve our mission that together we deliver services that make a difference in our community.
Reporting to, and under the direction of, the Supervisor of Building Inspections, the Senior Building Inspector is responsible for performing legislated building inspections required by the Ontario Building Code while ensuring compliance with all applicable Laws, Town By-laws and the Ontario Building Code. Primary duties include, but are not limited to:
conducting inspections for Part 9 and/or Part 3 buildings as well as general inspections (footing, back fill, framing, insulation, and final);
coordinating approvals from other departments and outside agencies;
investigating unsafe conditions related to, but not limited to fire, explosions wind and/or vehicular damage;
issuing compliance orders under the Building Act Code;
reviewing drawings with site supervisor;
consulting with external clients such as engineers and architects to resolve on-site issues;
reviewing test and site reports;
preparing and maintaining accurate files and records of inspections;
assist clients with inquiries concerning the Ontario Building Code;
assessing building code complaints to ensure compliance; and;
other duties as may be assigned.
Who You Are
Our Building Services team is looking for an enthusiastic, solutions-oriented team player, with strong work ethic.  You are self-motivated, self-starting and utilize a proactive approach to work, while modelling positive and professional behaviour. You value partnerships. Your excellent communication and interpersonal skills coupled with your experience enables you to skillfully build, establish and maintain positive working relationships. You demonstrate tact, diplomacy and sound discretion when working with a broad range of partners.
You bring to the team your strong reasoning, analytical, numerical, research and presentation skills.  You solve problems by identifying, gathering and processing relevant information.  Using your knowledge and experience in the field allows you to navigate through difficult interpersonal situations in a positive manner.  You demonstrate adeptness in conflict resolution and approach situations with the goal to improve communication, diffuse tension, resolve problems and build effective working relationships with all stakeholders.
What You Bring To Our Team
As the successful applicant, you must possess:
a post-secondary diploma or degree in Architecture, Architectural/Engineering Technology or a related discipline;
familiar with Part 3, 4, 9, 10 and 11 and Alternative Solutions of the Ontario Building Code
a minimum of three (3) years directly related experience;
qualification(s) as per the Ontario Building Code in the categories of:
General/Legal processes
House
Small Buildings
Large Buildings
Building Services
Building Structural
Complex Building
Plumbing (House)
HVAC (House)
Working at Heights certification;
basic level proficiency in MS Office (Word, Outlook, Excel) and AMANDA and
Successful candidates are required to hold and maintain a valid Province of Ontario Class "G" Driver's Licence and qualify for the Town’s Safe Driver Program criteria. This position drives a fleet vehicle.
What We Offer You
Benefits and retirement plan offered in accordance to Corporate programs and/or the applicable Collective Agreement.
A hybrid work environment and flexible work arrangements where employees are empowered to do their best work in the way that works for them. This is designated as a Mobile Hybrid role. Mobile Hybrid recognizes that approximately 50% of job functions associated with the role are done from a Town vehicle. Some work not completed from a Town vehicle can be done remotely. Further details on these programs will be discussed through the selection process.
Salary Range/Hourly rate:
$42.66 - $53.38
Hybrid information:
Mobile Hybrid
Hours:
Current shift schedule: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m., 35 hours per week.  Hours of work may be subject to change, shifts may be scheduled between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday.

October 20, 2026

description:

Permanent
Department:
Salary:
$99,994.00 - $124,994.00
Close Date
(closes at 12:00 am on date noted below):
November 2, 2026
Hours per Week:
35
Openings:
1
Position Summary
About Milton
Join one of Ontario’s fastest-growing and most dynamic municipalities. The Town of Milton is proud to deliver high-quality, sustainable municipal services that support a vibrant, inclusive, and forward-looking community where residents thrive, businesses succeed, and nature is respected and protected.
Our vision is to foster a safe, diverse, and welcoming environment—one that honours its natural landscapes and rich heritage, supports thriving and inclusive neighbourhoods, nurtures a strong and balanced economy, and offers exceptional opportunities to live, learn, work, and play.
About InvestMilton
InvestMilton is the Town dedicated economic development division and Milton’s economic engine — leading businesses and investors to real opportunities on the ground. The team is focused on supporting business growth, investment attraction, innovation, economic research, and strategic partnerships that advance Milton's economic prosperity.
What We Offer?
This position is eligible for the following:
•Annual Salary Range: $99,994 - $124,994
•Benefits: Regular full-time employees receive a comprehensive benefit package, with all premiums paid by the Town, an Employee Assistance Program, top-up maternity/parental leave benefits and life insurance.
•Eligibility to participate in the OMERS pension plan
•Paid time off, including vacation, incidental and volunteer days
•Employee perks/discounts: Discount on Active Living Pass and Perkopolis
•Flexible work arrangements, including hybrid work options and participation in the Town’s compressed work-week program (for eligible positions)
•For further details of what we offer, please visit Why Milton
Position Summary
Reporting to the Manager, Economic Development, this position provides strategic insight and guidance, subject matter expertise, and project management support to advance key economic development priorities. Responsibilities include the development and enhancement of core economic development functions, including: sector strategies, market and data intelligence/ analysis, marketing/brand development, and strategic partnership activities that support investment attraction, business retention and expansion, and Milton's long-term economic growth and competitiveness.
This position specifically serves as the division's lead for:
1. Business growth, business retention and expansion (BR&E), and innovation ecosystem development;
2. Market intelligence, economic analysis, and competitiveness research; and
3. Economic development marketing, digital engagement, and growth of the InvestMilton brand.
Major Job Responsibilities
Business Growth, Retention, Expansion & Innovation
Leads implementation of investment attraction, retention and expansion initiatives, innovation ecosystem programming and entrepreneurial support in alignment with Milton’s Economic Strategic Plan
Creates and implements effective innovation programming and entrepreneurial initiatives, including pursuing business and development leads and opportunities with owners, executives, developers and site selectors to promote Milton
Acts as the primary point of contact for businesses, investors, developers, entrepreneurs, and site selectors.
Develops, reviews and leads business retention initiatives and maintains strong relationships with local business leaders
Provides direction and advice to investors, developers, contractors and businesses navigating planning and building processes, and resolves issues through cross-departmental collaboration, as required
Leads business development, retention activities, inquiries, active files, and reports on outcomes and metrics
Builds and fosters relationships with the innovation ecosystem, consultants, government representatives, institutions and other community organizations / local bodies to drive Economic Development goals
Actively problem-solves with Town staff, Halton Region and other external agencies providing assistance and referrals that resolve issues for existing businesses
Develops and implements sector-related programs and initiatives to attract and grow businesses
Fosters relationships, consults and drives partner activities with Halton Region Small Business Centre and Innovation Factory, as well as other community organizations on matters pertaining to business support, investment attractions, local innovation programming, co-marketing campaigns, research and community data projects, and other various economic development activities/events
Contributes data to customer relations management database (Executive Pulse) including contact information for leads, prospects, brokers and other representatives of properties and site selection inquiries for economic development projects and activities
Leads meetings, event coordination and represents the Town at industry events, conferences, investment and trade initiatives, as required
Collaborates with the departmental and corporate internal staff to support inquiries and special projects
Market Intelligence, Competitiveness & Economic Analysis
Leads implementation of market intelligence plan and data strategy for division in alignment with Milton’s Economic Strategic Plan
Develops economic reporting dashboard leveraging PowerBI and other similar digital tools to support Milton Economic Development Advisory Board Updates, Council and internal memos, reports, presentations and events
Works with EDO’s to conduct ongoing research, analysis and monitoring of key data to support reporting across various channels and on InvestMilton’s Digital Data Hub
Develops robust investment pipeline tracking/reporting for inquiries, active files, leads, opportunities and outcomes
Identifies, monitors, and analyzes investment and business leasing, and sales activities, as well as data within the community available digital tools – Costar, MGIS, etc.
Undertakes trends analysis and visual storytelling using economic, community, demographic and development data to support key initiatives that enhance Milton’s value propositions and competitiveness
Establishes, cultivates and maintains strategic relationships essential to intelligence gathering, local market intel and ongoing analysis
Monitors key economic indicators, including non-residential data, real estate and market trends.
Prepares reports and updates using internal growth forecasts, investment pipeline activity, sector dynamics and market trends for Manager and leadership teams
Analyzes and monitors performance metrics, tracks results to achieve objectives -making adjustments throughout the year as needed
Prepares Council reports, presentations and briefing materials for the Chief Administration Office, Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives, and Manager, Economic Development
Economic Development Action Plan & InvestMilton Digital Marketing Assets
Implements annual Digital Asset & Marketing Strategy for InvestMilton, as division’s subject matter expert – working with division EDOs and Corporate Communications team
Develops and contributes content, property information, key data and business stories for InvestMilton digital channels with help from departmental staff
Develops key narratives as subject matter expert for marketing and promotional materials that drive investment opportunities and support the knowledge-based economy
Manages all website content with help from EDO’s, including property listings, community statistics/data, business support resources and digital mapping tools with help of departmental staff
Leads the development and implementation of annual Economic Development Action Plan and facilitates activities, initiatives, events and partnerships required to forward the goals of Milton’s Economic Strategy
Monitors and analyzes performance metrics to assess progress against the Economic Strategy and Action Plans, identifies opportunities for improvement, and adjusts activities as needed to achieve objectives
Project manages creation of the Economic Development Annual Report and supports development of other key marketing and digital promotional materials that advance divisional strategic objectives
Corporate, Strategic & Financial Support
Tracks and forecasts non-residential development in collaboration with Planning department to aid in determining the anticipated non-residential impacts for corporate budget and annual reporting
Represents Economic Development at quarterly variance meetings, as back-up for Manager, if required
Education & Experience
Minimum Qualifications
Degree in Urban/Economic Geography, Business, Marketing, Public Administration, Economics, Environmental Studies or Planning
7 years of experience in Economic Development or related field
Post-secondary training in Digital Marketing or Digital Data Tools and Analysis used in Economic Development considered an asset

Job Summary
The Health & Safety Coordinator is responsible for supporting the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the City’s occupational health and safety programs and systems.
This role provides support to ensure compliance with applicable health and safety legislation, while advancing a proactive safety culture focused on prevention, risk reduction, and employee well‑being.
Working in a complex, multi‑site, project‑driven, and unionized environment, the Coordinator partners with the People Services team, City leaders, Employees, multiple Joint Health & Safety Committees, contractors, and external stakeholders to drive effective safety practices, manage workplace incidents and claims, and deliver impactful training and programs across the organization.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Health & Safety Compliance
Support the development, implementation, review, and continuous improvement of the City’s health and safety programs, policies, procedures, standards, and safe work practices.
Contribute to the evolution of the City’s health and safety management system and overall safety strategy.
Ensure organizational compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA), Workplace Safety and Insurance Act (WSIA), and related legislation.
Coordinate and support health and safety programs, including workplace inspections, hazard assessments, contractor safety, confined space entry, workplace violence prevention, and first aid compliance.
Conduct compliance audits and gap assessments to ensure adherence to OHSA, applicable regulations, standards, and corporate requirements.
Monitor legislative changes, emerging trends, and best practices, recommending program enhancements to maintain compliance and support continuous improvement.
Risk Management & Incident Prevention (Operational)
Conduct workplace inspections, audits, hazard assessments, and job hazard analyses across municipal facilities, operational worksites, and active project/construction sites.
Lead or support incident, injury, and near‑miss investigations, including root‑cause analysis and corrective action implementation.
Where needed, support leadership to verify contractor compliance with municipal safety expectations, project‑specific requirements, and regulatory obligations
Coordinate occupational hygiene and exposure monitoring initiatives (noise, chemical, biological, ergonomic, indoor air quality).
Support emergency preparedness planning, drills, and response activities.
Provide advice to leaders, project managers, and employees on hazard identification, risk mitigation, and safe work procedures.
Training, Education & Culture
Identify legislated training requirements and support organization‑wide compliance with mandatory training programs.
Develop, coordinate, and deliver health and safety training programs, including orientations, project‑site safety briefings, and instructor‑led sessions.
Promote a culture of safety through engagement, communication, and awareness initiatives.
Support continuous improvement of learning systems and training compliance tracking.
Committees & Stakeholder Collaboration
Provide leadership and coordination support to multiple Joint Health & Safety Committees (JHSCs), including inspections, meetings, and follow‑up actions.
Act as a technical resource to JHSCs and departmental leaders regarding legislative requirements and health and safety best practices.
Support departmental leaders in meeting their due diligence and health and safety responsibilities.
Build effective relationships with employees, unions, supervisors, contractors, and external partners.
Wellness & Organizational Support
Support programs related to psychological health and safety, workplace violence and harassment prevention, and employee wellness.
Reporting & Analytics
Maintain safety data, documentation, and records required to demonstrate legislative compliance and due diligence.
Track and report on leading and lagging health and safety performance indicators.
Monitor compliance trends and prepare recommendations to improve organizational performance.
Prepare reports, dashboards, and analysis to support decision‑making and continuous improvement.
WSIB & Disability Management
Support the People Services team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse to coordinate WSIB claims management, including reporting, documentation, and case management.
Support the People Services team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse to facilitate return‑to‑work and modified‑duty planning in collaboration with key stakeholders.
Analyze and report back findings to the People Services Team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse the WSIB trends and performance metrics to identify opportunities for prevention and improvement.

Health and Safety diploma or equivalent
Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in occupational health and safety.
Experience in a municipal sector, construction, or unionized broader public‑sector environment is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience in:
Leading inspections, audits, and investigations
Supporting or advising multi‑site Joint Health & Safety Committees
Developing and delivering health and safety training programs
WSIB claims management and return‑to‑work coordination
Supporting safety on construction or capital project sites
Strong experience applying Ontario health and safety legislation in a complex environment.
Strong working knowledge of:
OHSA and applicable regulations
WSIA and return‑to‑work practices
Workplace violence and harassment legislation
Human Rights Code and duty to accommodate
Ability to translate legislation into practical, operational solutions.
Strong communication, facilitation, and relationship‑building skills.
Proven ability to influence and support leaders and employees in a unionized setting.
Strong analytical and problem‑solving capabilities.

Standard / Intermediate First Aid and CPR Level C.

Working in an Incident Command System, the Firefighter’s role is to protect life and property through firefighting, emergency medical and other types of emergency incidents, often performed under conditions requiring strenuous physical and mental exertion. Firefighters are also expected to provide excellent customer service as well as being leaders in public fire safety education. Firefighters are active participants in ongoing training in all phases of emergency response, including suppression, inspection, emergency operations, rescue, and providing medical assistance.
Key Responsibilities
Respond to fires, rescue, and medical emergencies in a safe and efficient manner.
Perform firefighting, hazardous materials response, and technical rescue operations.
Collaborate effectively with your crew and other first responder agencies while upholding the highest standards of professionalism.
Complete reports, record keeping and administrative duties.
Participate and support fire prevention and public education activities.
Participate and complete all training as assigned.
Clean, inspect and maintain equipment and apparatus conducting full maintenance and safety checks.
Ensure facilities, equipment, and grounds are clean and orderly.
Perform other similar and related duties as assigned.

Legally entitled to work in Canada.
Grade 12 level education or equivalent (e.g. General Education Diploma).
NFPA 1001 Fire Fighter I and II certified from an accredited program from a recognized institution, accredited by the International Fire Service Accreditation Congress (IFSAC) or Pro Board.
Possess valid Ontario Fire Administration Inc. (OFAI) Candidate Testing Service Stages 2, 3 (FPAT only) and swim test certificates.
Valid Ontario driver's license with a good driving record (no more than six (6) demerits).
Valid Class “D” license with a “Z” air brake endorsement by hire date.
Emergency Medical Responder (EMR) Certificate.
Medical clearance by a physician.
Clear Vulnerable Sector Security Check.

.

title: Project Manager, Information Technology (Temp up to 24 months)
description:
We’re looking for a Project Manager, Information Technology (Temporary up to 24 months) to join Clarington’s Finance and Technology Department!
Why Clarington?
Clarington is a community full of possibilities.
As one of the fastest-growing municipalities in Durham Region, Clarington is home to over 107,000 residents across four urban centres and 14 hamlets. With our population expected to double by 2051, Clarington offers a perfect blend of urban living and small-town charm. We’re known for our thriving energy and agricultural sectors, vibrant historic downtowns, and exceptional quality of life.
Our team thrives in a collaborative environment that promotes work-life balance and meaningful community impact. We value accountability, integrity, and respect, and we are deeply committed to fostering equity, inclusion, and diversity in the workplace. Together, we’re building a stronger Clarington — for today and for future generations.
The future is bright – and working with the Municipality of Clarington means you can help shape it. How will you make your mark?
About the Role
Vacancy Statement:
Unless specifically stated, all job postings at the Municipality of Clarington are to fill existing vacancies within our organization.
Work Model:
Hybrid
Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, with a dotted-line relationship to the Supervisor, Business Development and the Deputy CAO/Treasurer, this position is responsible for supporting the project lifecycle for Clarington’s implementation of a new Microsoft Dynamics 365 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution, replacing the Municipality’s legacy finance and operations systems.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the full project lifecycle for Clarington’s implementation of Microsoft Dynamics 365, from charter and business case through design, build, go-live and post-implementation review.
Develop, participate and assist in procurement (NRFP/RFP or Cooperative Agreement, evaluation, assist with negotiations, contract logistics) in partnership with Municipality’s procurement team while following Clarington’s by-laws.
Serve as a point of accountability for scope, schedule, tracking and reporting on project budget, risk and quality, including budget submissions and financial reporting for each phase of the program.
Coordinate cross-functional teams spanning Finance, IT, Human Resources/Payroll, Procurement, operating departments, the implementation partner and vendor resources; chair steering and working groups; prepare Council and executive updates.
Oversee technical readiness (environment provisioning, integrations and interfaces, data migration and cleansing from legacy systems, cybersecurity, cut-over, testing, and contingency planning).
Manage functional workstreams across general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, budgeting, procurement, project and grant accounting, asset management and financial reporting, including business process re-engineering and the secondment of subject matter experts.
Ensure knowledge transfer to internal staff, producing robust documentation, SOPs and training that strengthen Clarington’s long-term ERP capabilities.
Embed continuous improvement, capturing lessons learned and identifying future enhancements (e.g., human resources and payroll, asset management, analytics).
Champion data-security and privacy by ensuring all project artefacts remain within Clarington-controlled systems.
Drive parallel finance modernization workstreams such as chart of accounts redesign, retirement of manual and spreadsheet-based processes, integration with the Dynamics 365 CRM platform, and reporting and business intelligence.
Coordinate technology dependencies pertinent to the ERP migration, including licensing, environments, server, storage and cloud services, working with Infrastructure & Security and Client & Application Services teams to minimize downtime.
Contribute to PMO best practices, creating templates, dashboards, and knowledge-transfer sessions that strengthen Clarington’s project-delivery maturity long term.
Advise departmental leaders on scoping, budgeting, and prioritizing future technology initiatives that align with the municipality’s IT Strategy (Strengthen, Innovate, Transform).
Develop change-management and training plans, ensuring end-users adopt new tools and workflows effectively across Finance & Technology and all operating departments.
Provide executive-level reporting, distilling complex schedules, risks, and financials into clear updates for Council, senior leadership, and internal stakeholders.
What you bring
University degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting, Project Management or related discipline.
Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification is required.
Minimum 3 years’ progressive IT project-management experience delivering complex, multi-stakeholder technology projects.
Proven success leading large-scale RFPs and contract negotiations in a municipal or broader public-sector setting.
Hands-on experience delivering ERP or enterprise financial system implementations, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 (Finance & Operations or Business Central).
Demonstrated ability to monitor project budgets and to work with leaders, executives and/or stakeholders.
ITIL, Agile/Scrum or Prosci Change Management certifications is an asset.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications, or experience with ERP implementation methodologies such as Microsoft Success by Design, is an asset.
Expert grasp of project-management methodologies (Agile & Waterfall) and tools (MS Project, Teams, Azure DevOps).
Understanding of public sector procurement legislation, public-sector governance, and municipal financial processes and reporting standards (PSAB).
Excellent communication, written and verbal, facilitation and vendor-management skills.
Advanced analytical, risk-management and report-writing abilities.
Must be legally able to work in Canada and able to obtain/maintain a satisfactory Criminal Reference Check.
What we offer
Salary: Grade 7 ($104,564 to $127,099) of the 2026 Non-Affiliated Salary Administration Program.
The Municipality of Clarington offers flexible work arrangements for eligible roles, where employees are empowered to do their best work in the way that works for them. This position is eligible for a flexible work arrangement option. Further details on this program will be discussed through the selection process.

title: Tree Planting Project Technician - Contract
description:
Reporting to the Manager, Environment and Climate, the Tree Planting Project Technician will support tree planting projects on Town-owned land, including along road rights-of-way and in parks. The Tree Planting Project Technician will bring their technical tree and environmental knowledge to identify and map potential tree planting locations, support tree planting contract management, conduct tree inventory data collection, and manage/analyze related spatial data.
The Technician will also play a key role in engaging with the public, businesses, and community groups to collaborate on tree planting initiatives, increase awareness of the benefits of trees, and share information on how the community can plant, care for, and protect trees. As needed, the Technician will support other environmental projects to help advance the Town’s vision as a nature-rich community and support implementation of the Town’s Strategic Plan. This role will spend about half the time working on-site and engaging with the community and partners, and the other half will be office.
Accountabilities
:
Comply with corporate and departmental policies and procedures.
Ensure a high degree of service for both internal and external customers in accordance with Town standards.
Identify and map potential tree planting locations on Town-owned land, primarily along road rights-of-way and in parks.
Complete site assessments of potential planting locations including assessing soil type, collecting soil samples, and checking for above- and below-ground conflicts, such as utilities.
Recommend suitable tree species based on site conditions.
Consult with other staff/departments as appropriate to confirm suitability of planting locations.
Engage regularly with residents, businesses and community groups/organizations to identify potential planting sites, share information about the benefits of trees, communicate upcoming tree planting & management activities, and promote best practices for tree planting and care.
Assist with planting contractor management, such as providing planting location instruction, follow-up inspections, and on- or off-site support as needed.
Collect inventory data for trees, other green infrastructure assets, and invasive species, as assigned, using a tablet and hand-held GPS receiver.
Manage spatial data and ensure data quality through data review and following up on deficiencies.
Support community groups leading naturalization plantings on Town land and maintain regular communication with the group lead.
Assess naturalization planting locations for required site prep and coordinate associated activities.
Support (on site) during naturalization planting activities/events, as needed.
Assist with the development of the Town’s Green Infrastructure Asset Management Plan as needed, such as support with asset inventories, mapping, data analysis, etc.
Assist with other environmental stewardship projects as needed, such as invasive species management projects, Privately Owned Tree Management Strategy actions, developing communication content, conducting research, supporting grant applications, biodiversity projects, etc.
Support environmental community outreach and engagement programs, as needed.
Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
Qualifications:
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Forestry, Urban Forestry, Arboriculture, Natural Resource Management, Forest Conservation, or a related discipline, or the equivalent in combined education and experience
ISA certified arborist is considered an asset
Minimum of 1 year’s work experience in urban forestry, forestry, arboriculture or a directly related field.
Excellent tree identification skills, knowledge of native tree species and common tree pests and diseases and understanding of tree biology.
Applied knowledge of tree planting and care best practices.
Knowledge and understanding of invasive species, soils, and ecology in Ontario.
Strong research and analytical skills.
Excellent organizational, project management, time management and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently, multi-task and prioritize work to meet project deadlines.
Working knowledge of computer software and techniques applicable to the areas of inventory databases, such as Access or ArcGIS to create and maintain an inventory database.
Experience working with the public or community groups through collaborative projects and/or engagement and outreach.
Proficient in the use of MS Office (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook).
Class G Driver license in good standing and reliable vehicle to use occasionally on corporate business.
Compensation:
The compensation rate for this temporary contract position is $32.27 - $38.41 (35 hours per week). Duration of Contract is approximately twelve (12) months, with the possibility to extend.
Location:
This position allows a blend of working onsite and remotely based on the needs of the business, in accordance with the Town’s Work from Home Policy, and as subject to change. This position will also require some flexibility in the incumbent’s availability and work schedule.
Application:

posting 202660
on your cover letter.

Reporting to the Town Solicitor, as a member of the in-house Legal Department, the Assistant Town Solicitor serves to safeguard and advance the public interest of the municipal corporation by providing legal services and advice to staff and Council, including representing the Town in litigation and hearings, providing oral and written legal opinions, drafting and reviewing legal documents, including agreements and by-laws, preparing and reviewing reports, and attending Council meetings.

description:

Job Responsibilities:
Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor, this position is being offered as a full-time permanent staff compliment to the Transit Department (Maintenance Division). Duties will include but not be restricted to:
Lays out, builds, tests, troubleshoots, repairs and modifies developmental and production electronic components, parts, equipment, and systems, such as Smartbus technologies, destination signs, communication equipment, fare collection equipment and other Transit related equipment and systems.
Ability to develop, maintain and operate test equipment by applying principles and theories of electronics and electrical circuitry.
Discusses layout and assembly of procedures and problems with manufactures and ability to draw sketches to clarify design details and functional criteria of electronic units.
Assembles experimental circuitry (breadboard) or complete prototype model according to engineering instructions, technical manuals, and knowledge of electronic systems and components.
Recommends changes in circuitry or installation specifications to simplify assembly and maintenance.
Sets up standard test apparatus or devises test equipment and circuitry to conduct functional, operational, environmental, and life tests to evaluate performance and reliability of prototype or production model.
Analyses and interprets test data.
Adjusts, calibrates, aligns, and modifies circuitry and components and records effects on unit performance.
Writes technical reports and develops charts, graphs, and schematics to describe and illustrate system's operating characteristics, malfunctions, deviations from design specifications, and functional limitations for consideration by engineers in broader determinations affecting system design and laboratory procedures.
May instruct and provide guidance to other technical personnel.
Diagnose electrical problems and simulate conditions.
Repair test equipment as required.
Search for substitute parts for out-of-stock or out-of-production replacement parts, and check the specifications of substitute parts.
Input and retrieve vehicle repair information from the Fleet Maintenance System.
Complete other routine forms, records or reports, including minor written reports on work inspected.
Performs other similar and related duties to this position, as assigned.
Qualifications:
Grade 12 education or equivalent secondary education as established by the Ontario Ministry of Education.
Successful completion of Community College courses in electronics or equivalent.
3 years of related experience in the electronics field.
Ability to work with circuit board components.
Demonstrated ability to read and understand schematic diagrams.
Able to work shifts and variable hours.
Able to handle physical demands of the job.
Able to work outside and in all weather conditions.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with an emphasis on customer service.
Strong time management and organizational skills.
Able to work independently and as part of a team in a fast paced environment.
Able to wear required personal protective equipment and use appropriate safety equipment to complete job tasks in a safe manner.
Must be resourceful and have initiative to work with little supervision.
Must hold (or have the ability to obtain as a condition of employment) and provide a copy of a valid and unrestricted Ontario Driver’s License Class C with a Z air brake endorsement with a driving record that demonstrates responsible and safe driving behaviour.
Note:
Applicants with 6 or more points are ineligible for consideration.
The successful applicant, who is a new hire, will be required to provide the Corporation with a current drivers abstract (no older than 30 days) prior to assuming the position.

Make a Difference in Your Community – Join Our Team!
Are you looking for a job that keeps you active, helps you learn new skills, and lets you give back to your community? We’re hiring Facility Maintenance Attendants to help keep our community centres and ice rinks clean, safe, and welcoming for everyone.
As a Facility Maintenance Attendant, you’ll be a vital part of the team that keeps everything running smoothly — from setting up events to maintaining the ice and outdoor spaces.
Why Work with Us?
Flexible hours that fit around school, family, or other commitments
Supportive, community-focused team that values your contributions
Play a key role in supporting local programs and events — help ensure facilities are clean, safe, and ready for activities like skating, sports leagues, and public gatherings

Meet new people and make a real impact in your neighborhood

Event & Activity Support
Set up and take down tables, chairs, and equipment for sports, meetings, and special events
Ensure all areas are clean, organized, and ready for the next scheduled activity

Cleaning and sanitizing restrooms, changerooms, hallways, and activity areas
Restocking essential supplies such as soap, paper towels, and toilet paper
Regularly removing garbage and recycling to maintain a tidy environment
Maintaining outdoor areas through sweeping, litter pickup, and snow removal as needed

Customer Service
Respond to customer inquiries and concerns, including providing directions and information about the facility
Address service requests from staff and customers in a timely and helpful manner
Greet and interact with customers in a friendly, respectful, and approachable manner
Maintain a calm and courteous attitude, even in busy or challenging situations
Ice Rink Support
Assist with cleaning and maintaining a smooth, safe ice surface
Set up nets, temporary boards, and other rink equipment as needed
Help keep rink areas clean, organized, and safe for all users
Health & Safety
Proactively identify and report health and safety issues
Ensure safety procedures and protocols are followed
Communicate delays or complications clearly and promptly
Assist in emergencies (e.g. power outages)

No previous experience required — we provide full training
A positive attitude and a willingness to learn new skills
Reliable, organized, and able to work independently or as part of a team
Comfortable working in active and occasionally cold environments (like ice rinks)
Physically able to lift/move equipment and stay on your feet during shifts

title: Manager, Human Resources
description:
Full-Time Employment Opportunity
Manager, Human Resources
Salary Range: $115,356-$134,950

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer, as a member of the senior management team, this position is
responsible for overseeing all Human Resources functions within the organization. The Human Resources
Manager provides leadership and subject matter expertise to management and staff in a variety of areas such
as employee and labour relations, policy & collective agreement interpretation, coaching, organizational design,
staffing, investigations, attendance management, and training and development. The HR Manager also has
functional oversight of the following corporate HR programs: health, safety and wellness; disability management
and attendance support; recruitment and onboarding; employee engagement; and performance management.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

A. Staffing:
• Corporate recruitment processes including staffing needs analysis, attraction methods (job postings,
advertising, etc.), screening, interviewing, selection, pre-employment assessments, and preparing offers
of employment. Coordinate with external staffing agencies, as required.
• Provide coaching and support to hiring managers through staffing, recruitment and on-boarding
processes.
• Work collaboratively at department and divisional levels to help design new structures and jobs to meet
the ongoing operational needs, including development of organizational charts and job descriptions.
• Oversight of succession plan for the Township.
• Provide expertise and guidance to managers and staff on disability and other accommodation requests.

B. Compensation and Benefits:
• Lead job evaluation processes, including maintaining current job descriptions and job evaluation records.
• Lead attendance support programs including managing short term disability and long-term disability
claims, return to work plans, accommodation and modification.
• Negotiate salaries based on the current salary grids.
• In coordination with the Finance Department, administer pay practices as per the collective agreement.
• Answer basic benefit inquiries from staff and management regarding entitlements.
• Answer questions on sick leave administration.

C. Organizational Development:
• Conduct needs analysis for departments and prescribe training and development.
• Recommend external training programs, trainers and/or methods to respond to department training
needs.
• Coordinate and lead instruction on various topics including but not limited to: leadership development,
change management, Personality Dimensions, team development, crisis intervention, and dealing with
difficult people.
• Oversee performance management and employee development programs.
• Provide project management for organization-wide-people initiatives.
• Chair the Engagement and Wellness staff committee; organize and facilitate events and team
engagement activities.

D. Employee Relations:
• Conduct investigations, advise on policy violations, and make recommendations for corrective actions.
• Assist managers to implement performance improvement plans.
• Provide advice on disciplinary matters such as past practices, the appropriate level and type of
discipline, and whether or not to discipline.
• Develop comprehensive reports and present the findings and conclusions to senior management,
Council, and the employee(s) involved.
• Conduct terminations as needed.

E. Labour Relations:
• Lead negotiations for the Township on collective agreement contracts, grievances, hearings,
memorandums of understanding, etc.
• Liaise with the various provincial ministries, boards, external lawyers, consultants, insurance brokers &
carriers, and other municipalities as needed.
• Provide advice and guidance on matters pertaining to collective agreement administration.
• Advise management staff of Memorandum of Settlements and how they affect their department.
• Provide advice on legislation-related issues such as the Employment Standards Act, Labour Relations
Act, Human Rights Code, etc.
• Attend grievance meetings, mediation and arbitration hearings.
• Implement grievance or arbitration settlements.
• Ensure the grievance process is conducted in accordance with the relevant collective agreement,
legislation, and arbitral jurisprudence.

F. Policies and Procedures:
• Identify and develop HR policies and procedures for the Township.
• Examine past/current practices to ensure consistency within department/Township, and identify issues
that may lead to policy development, training, etc.
• Review and recommend changes to current HR policies.

G. Leadership
• This position oversees the HR Advisor role and provides guidance and support, coaching and counseling;
feedback and performance appraisal.
• Sets goals for the department in collaboration with the HR Advisor and evaluates progress.
• Ensure quality service is delivered to all staff.

H. Additional Responsibilities:
• Oversee the Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, Accessibility staff committee
• Responsible for oversight of Health and Safety for the Township; accountable for policies regarding the
safety and security of employees and facilities and ensuring that employees work safely and in
compliance with the relevant statutes, regulations, and safe work procedures and directives as established
by the Township.
• Undertake special projects and perform other related duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:
• Bachelor’s Degree in Labour Relations and/or Human Resources or Bachelor’s Degree and post-graduate
Diploma in Labour Relations and/or Human Resources.
• A minimum of five (5) years’ experience in a HR management role in a unionized setting.
• Labour relations and collective bargaining experience in a municipal or public sector environment.
• Demonstrated experience in benefits, staffing, compensation, and first line collective agreement
administration.
• Thorough knowledge of employment legislation; collective agreements; Occupational Health and Safey
Act; Ontario Human Rights Code; Township Policy Manual; and HR policies and procedures.
• Certified Human Resources Leader (CHRL) designation is an asset.
• Adult Educators Certificate is an asset.
• Valid Class “G” Ontario Driver’s License, with regular access to a vehicle for corporate matters.

COMPETENCIES REQUIRED:
• Extensive mediation and negotiation skills.
• Demonstrated problem-solving and conflict/dispute resolution skills.

innovative solutions.

Service at our Core Do the right thing Connect with Compassion Reflect and Grow
The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. With over 5,000 officers and approximately 2,500 civilian employees, we are dedicated to delivering best-in-class police services, in partnership with our communities, by being where the public needs the Service the most, by embracing partnerships to create safe communities, and by focusing on the needs of the City.
The Opportunity:
Are you passionate about Human Resources, do you have strong organizational and customer service skills combined with the ability to work under multiple timelines? If this sounds like you, we have an excellent opportunity as an Employee Services Representative.
What can I expect to do in this role?
In this role, you will provide first point of contact support to Uniform and Civilian members of the Service for inquiries within the scope of payroll, benefits and human resources through written and verbal communication channels. The Employee Services Representative ensures that all members of the Toronto Police Service and external contacts receive Human Resource support, while prioritizing issue resolution via investigation, problem solving and collective agreement alignment to ensure a positive member experience.

Updates and maintains call tracking logs as indicated by Unit specific procedures.
Performs administrative office duties:
Opens and sorts mail, files and purges records, creates, copies and distributes documents, scans paper files and documents.
Schedules and coordinates activities, events, correspondence, meetings as required to support Employee Service Centre service levels.
Generates and/or distributes routine correspondence to clients and customers.
Performs all other duties, functions and assignments inherent to the position.

Post-secondary education (degree, diploma or certificate) in Payroll, Benefits or Human Resources

Analysis and problem-solving skills.

The Toronto Police Service is looking for a candidate that shares our core values:
Service at our Core Do the right thing Connect with Compassion Reflect and Grow
The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. With over 5,000 officers and approximately 2,500 civilian employees, we are dedicated to delivering best-in-class police services, in partnership with our communities, by being where the public needs the Service the most, by embracing partnerships to create safe communities, and by focusing on the needs of the City.
We are hiring Special Constables:
The Toronto Police Service is now accepting applications for anticipated 2027 Special Constable hiring requirements. We are seeking dedicated, community-focused individuals who are committed to promoting safety, professionalism, and public trust across the City of Toronto.
About the Role:
Special Constables play an essential role in supporting public safety and enhancing community well-being. This position requires strong communication skills, sound judgement, and the ability to remain calm, effective, and respectful in fast-paced and dynamic environments.
What We re Looking For
We invite applicants who demonstrate:
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
The ability to multi-task and remain composed under pressure
Professionalism, maturity, and integrity in all interactions
Strong decision-making skills and sound judgement
A commitment to fairness, respect, and community service
Motivation, reliability, and the ability to work independently
Why Join Us?
This is an excellent opportunity to build a meaningful career in law enforcement while contributing to the safety and well-being of Toronto s diverse communities. As a Special Constable, you will gain valuable experience, training, and development within one of Canada s largest and most respected police services.
What can I expect to do in this role?
As a Special Constable, you may be required to rotate in any of the following positions throughout your career:
Assigned to Court Services
, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Maintaining security and control of persons in custody who must attend court
Transporting prisoners to and from detention centres, immigration facilities, medical facilities, hospitals, police divisions, court houses, arrest locations or other detention locations
Controlling, monitoring and escorting persons lodged in holding cells and escorting them to court
Maintaining security and order in courtrooms
Monitoring courthouse entrances via electronic screening
Executing arrests when required
Obtaining DNA samples from persons in and out of custody, as ordered by the court
Attending court and testifying as required
Assigned to the booking area
of a division, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Booking of prisoners, including searching, fingerprinting and photographing persons in custody
Maintain the security and wellbeing of prisoners in custody
Liaise and communicate with various stakeholders throughout the division and the Service regarding prisoner status and management
Manage persons in emotional crisis and physical distress, using available resources such as MCIT, Emergency Medical Services or arranging transport to a hospital, as appropriate
Attending court and testifying as required
Assigned to a division
, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Report writing, evidence collecting, canvassing and assisting in search of missing persons.
Enforcement of some City of Toronto parking by-laws
Attending and assisting in protecting secured crime scenes under on-scene police constables or supervisors
Maintaining a notebook containing an accurate and thorough account of up-to-date- activities
Prisoner transportation, prisoner security and prisoner management
Attending court and testifying as required
How do I qualify?
Minimum Requirements:
Successful completion of Grade 12 (OSSD or equivalent)
Have a minimum of one year of related experience (i.e. working with the general public or working in a customer service environment)
Must be Canadian Citizen or Permanent Resident
License and Certification Requirements:
Possess valid "G" driver's license (upon submission of application) with no more than six demerit points, permitting you to drive an automobile in Ontario with full driving privileges
Current certification in Intermediate First Aid (formerly known as Standard First Aid) from an accredited agency by the time an offer of employment is given.
Possess a valid O.A.C.P. (Ontario Association of Chiefs of Police Certificate) certificate.
Have a minimum of 20/40 (uncorrected) vision, with normal colour acuity.
Successfully pass the hearing and vision standards as outlined by the O.A.C.P.
Successfully complete the PREP (Shuttle Run: Stage 6 & Pursuit Restraint Circuit within 3 minutes)
For further information on obtaining an OACP Certificate of Results and/or testing, visit:
https://oacpcertificate.ca
Please Note: If selected to move forward, applicants will be invited to attend the PREP test at the Toronto Police College.
Skills/Competencies:
Ability to deal effectively with persons in crisis and to work in a stressful environment that requires problem solving, judgement, conflict resolution, communication, teamwork and co-operation
Possess strong interpersonal and communication skills in order to deal with members of the Service, persons in custody and the public in a professional and tactful manner
Motivated self-starter, able to work with minimal supervision
Must be able to endure prolonged physical activity associated to rigorous defensive tactics training, on a daily basis
Conditions of Employment:
Must successfully pass the required Toronto Police Service driving test to operate a police vehicle (TPS Blue Card)
Deemed medically fit for the position through a medical assessment
Meet all requirements to attain the status of a Special Constable as outlined by the Ministry
Successfully complete the Special Constable Training Program that consists of:
15 week training program at TPC (70 Birmingham Street)
Monday to Friday 7am - 3pm (may also include evenings and weekends)

6 months
