title: Communications Operator
description:
Posting Title: Communication Operator
Job ID #: 8029
Status: Regular Full-Time
Salary: $83,538 - $109,755
Shift: This position is assigned to a platoon-based rotational schedule. All employees are required to work a regular rotation of days, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays.
Location: Communications Services
Vacancies: Several
Job Code: C71CMZ Class 7 (40 hours)
Our Mindset ~ Our Connections ~ Our Impact ~ Our Development
Service at our Core ~ Do the right thing ~ Connect with Compassion ~ Reflect and Grow
The Opportunity:
Can you stay calm when others can t?
In moments of crisis, the voice of 911 becomes a lifeline to community members experiencing their worst day. Are you able to think clearly, listen actively, and make rapid, sound life and death decisions under pressure?
Do you listen to understand?
Can you pick up on what s said and what s not? Do you have the ability to hear urgency, fear, or confusion and respond with clarity and compassion?
Are you passionate about serving the city of Toronto and all its communities?
Are you a master of multitasking?
Can you juggle multiple calls, systems, and priorities without missing a beat? Do you thrive in fast paced environments? Are you seeking challenge and meaning in your career? Are you able to manage multiple on-going tasks and changing priorities?
Is your communication clear and confident?
Whether it s a panicked caller or a police officer in the field, can you deliver information calmly, accurately, and respectfully?
Do you have the resilience to handle tough situations?
Emergencies are unpredictable. Can you manage stress, maintain emotional control, and bounce back after difficult calls? Do you understand the importance of a health work-life balance and have mechanisms in place to cope with difficult situations?
Are you tech-savvy and detail-oriented?
Can you operate complex communication systems and databases while staying focused on accuracy and procedure?
Can you think critically under pressure?
Emergencies are dynamic.
Situations change in a moment as do the requirements of our communications operators.
Are you flexible and adaptable? Are you able to think critically through situations? Can you analyze situations and apply relevant policies and procedures?
Do you thrive in a team environment?
Can you coordinate with police, fire, ambulance, and other agencies to ensure the right help gets to the right place fast?
If You Answered Yes ...
You might be exactly who we re looking for.
The Toronto Police Service is seeking
exceptional individuals
to become
Communications Operators
the calm in the chaos, the voice of reason, and the first point of contact in emergencies.
What can I expect in this role?
In this role, you will be responsible for receiving, monitoring and assessing incoming emergency calls, and taking or expediting the required action in accordance with Service procedures.
This is a dynamic work environment. As a Communications Operator, you will:
Answer 911 calls from citizens in life-threatening and emergency situations.
Answer telephone calls on the non-emergency, dedicated and internal police lines and take the appropriate action.
Provide instructions and support to callers in distress, building rapport and valuing lived experiences.
Dispatch police officers and support units to emergency situations; coordinating with partner agencies such as Ambulance and Fire as required.
Monitor events and adjust priorities in real time based on updates and new information.
Monitor police pursuits and gather information to assist the supervisor and the police officer(s) involved. Liaise with other divisions or other police services to provide an appropriate response
Operate various computerized communications consoles and associated equipment to receive, assess and relay information to police officers in the field. Report major or unusual occurrences to supervisor
Operate Services databases (including C.P.I.C.) to check for and relay requested information to field personnel
Perform typical duties inherent to the position such as conducting follow-up calls to citizens, other police units or related agencies as required.
How do I qualify?
Mandatory:
Must have successful completion of grade 12 or an approved equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Official
transcripts and diplomas will be required.
Note:
If you received your high school and/or college education in a province other than Ontario, or;
If you received your high school, college and/or university education in a country other than Canada, you
MUST
obtain official proof of equivalency from an accredited agency, such as the International Credential Assessment Services of Canada (ICAS) or World Education Services - Canada (WES Canada).
Educational equivalency documentation MUST be presented upon request.
Must have a minimum of two years of previous customer service experience in a fast paced and multi-tasking environment.
Must be available to work on-going, regular, rotating shifts, including days, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays as scheduled.
Ability to hear and readily relay information accurately with high attention to detail, while operating various methods of communication equipment (Computer Aided Dispatch, TTY, portable radios, telephones) despite constant interruptions and distractions.
Must successfully complete the medical approval process, including vision and hearing tests.
In addition, the Toronto Police Service values the following qualifications:
Completion of a recognized Public Safety Communication Course is an asset.
Experience in emergency response, and/or high-stress call centre environments is preferred.
Key Competencies:
Resilience:
High level of emotional stability and resilience under high-pressure situations, maintaining composure and sound judgment during times of high stress and high emotions over long term exposure.
Ability to navigate through dynamic situations involving a high level of stress and maintaining composure. Keep calm, collective and make quick life changing decisions.
Solid understanding of a healthy work life balance and reliable, healthy coping strategies to manage stress over the long term.
Multi-tasking in a fast-paced environment:
Strong multitasking skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and deal with critical and time sensitive calls for service.
Ability to confidently make emergency decisions and act on these decisions under strict and definitive policies and procedures.
Customer Service:
Strong customer service skills with experience to influence and de-escalate others emotions to provide service during emergency situations.
Ability to de-escalate conflict in a professional and tactful manner over the phone.
Problem Solving:
Ability to deal effectively with persons in crisis and work in a stressful environment which requires problem solving, judgement, conflict resolution, de-escalation, communication, teamwork and co-operation.
Testing Process:
Applicants must successfully pass a multi-level CritiCall testing process.
Phase 1 (CritiCall)
Candidates will be tested on CritiCall software which tests short term memory, keyboarding (typing speed), spelling, clarity and reading comprehension.
Call taking skills, such as computer-related multi-taking abilities, data entry skills, memory retention, prioritization, map reading, call summarization and performance under stress.
If selected, you will receive an email from TEST GENIUS where you will be provided with instructions. Please monitor both your inbox and junk/spam for this email.
Note:
Candidates will only be allowed one (1) attempt for CritiCall Testing per job posting. Duplicate applications will not be considered and will result in your removal from the job call process.
Only applicants who are successful in the Criti
C
all testing (Phase 1) will proceed to Phase 2 of testing.
Phase 2 (Perfex):
A telecommunications simulator test, measuring motor skills, eye-hand co-ordination, multi-tasking, memory retention and performance under stress. This test includes a hand-written component.
Candidates successful at Phase 2 testing will proceed to the following recruitment stages:
Interview
Background Checks (inclusive of a psychological assessment)
Job Shadow
Conditions of Employment:
Must pass medical assessment.
Must successfully pass the intensive training program:
Communications Operators must successfully complete a lengthy, intensive (paid) training program - comprised of 7 weeks of in-class call-taker training, followed by live environment coaching for 240 hours, and 5 weeks of in-class dispatch training, followed by live environment coaching for 240 hours. Training will include days, afternoons, midnights and weekends. You will be reporting to various locations during your training program, which will be provided to you on the first day of class. A minimum standard of 75% is required on tests and practical examinations to remain in the training program.
Communication Operators are assigned to a platoon and are required to regularly work weekends as part of their rotational schedule. All Communications Operators are also required to work statutory holidays as the rotational platoon schedule. Communication Services is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days year.
Communication Operators will handle emergency 9-1-1 and non-emergency calls.
The most serious emergencies include difficult and stressful situations such as violent crimes in progress, suicidal callers, fatalities, and traumatic events.
These calls are expected and regular daily occurrences.
Communication Operators are expected to be calm and make decisions methodically based on their critical thinking skills, TPS protocol and training.
Communication Operators will be exposed to difficult situations and require intense concentration for extended periods of time.
Due to the nature of the work, Communication Operators are restricted to their workstation, breaks and lunches are pre-scheduled and dependent upon workload.
Must be able to commit to the Communication Operators work schedule
.
Must be able and willing to commute to work location for the job. NO REMOTE WORK.
Must be able to understand the serious and stressful nature of the calls I may be required to handle.
Must be able to make sound and rapid decisions in a highly fast-paced and stressful environment
.
Probationary Period:
18 Months
As a condition of employment, you will need to successfully meet the minimum standards within the 18-month probation period.

The Toronto Police Service is looking for exceptional
Experienced Police Constables
who want to serve the city of Toronto and protect the community.
Modernizing the Toronto Police Service will be achieved by transforming how we relate to the public, how we deliver our service, how people access our services, ensuring the affordability and sustainability of our operations, and creating a culture of excellence. The Human Resources modernization plan will support our efforts by hiring members to support community-centric policing, diversity and inclusion. These are important principles because the ability of the Toronto Police Service to keep Toronto the best and safest place to be has always depended on the trust and support of the people we serve.
As an experienced officer joining the Toronto Police Service, your focus will be to protect members of the public, to prevent and investigate crimes and to assist victims. In joining us, you will work in partnership with communities and service delivery agencies to address crime, disorder, and community safety issues with an understanding of, and a sensitivity toward, the complex needs specific to each neighbourhood.
To learn more about the benefits of working for the Toronto Police Service, we invite you to watch the following video clips featuring members who joined as experienced officers (links will open in a new window):
Adrianne's Story

The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. Our well-earned reputation as a world leader in policing is a reflection of our commitment to excellence, innovation, quality leadership, and ongoing professional
development.
A career in policing is primarily about working with people to ensure public safety through crime prevention and law enforcement. Police work requires the building of relationships in the community, and sensitivity towards the needs of people from all races, cultures, and backgrounds.
The Toronto Police Service is currently hiring. We are looking for exceptional people who want to serve the city of Toronto and protect the community as a cadet in-training to become a Police Constable.
Modernizing the Toronto Police Service will be achieved by transforming how we relate to the public, how we deliver our service, how people access our services, ensuring the affordability and sustainability of our operations, and creating a culture of excellence. The Human Resources modernization plan will support our efforts by hiring recruits to support community-centric policing, diversity and inclusion. These are important principles because the ability of the Toronto Police Service to keep Toronto the best and safest place to be has always depended on the trust and support of the people we serve.
The fundamental role of a police officer is about commitment to public service. As a new constable or an experienced officer joining the Toronto Police Service, your focus will be to protect members of the public, to prevent and investigate crimes and to assist victims.
